title: Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation of AISI 316L Stainless Steel Parts Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite (
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF.
                  </jats:p>

title: Semi-automated histomorphometric quantification of acetabular labral surface roughness
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Histopathologic surface changes, including fibrillation, fraying, undulation, and disruption, are important indicators of tissue wear and acetabular labral degeneration. Surface assessment, however, commonly relies on descriptive or semiquantitative grading and may be partly observer-dependent when applied to naturally curved fibrocartilaginous surfaces. This study developed and evaluated a semi-automated histomorphometric workflow for quantifying acetabular labral articular surface roughness using histologic images. Sixteen human hemipelves from nine embalmed cadavers were divided into eight anatomical segments and grouped into superior, anterior, inferior, and posterior quadrants. Sections were stained with haematoxylin and eosin and Safranin O/Fast Green, scanned at high resolution, and analysed using Fiji/ImageJ and Python. The labral articular surface was isolated, skeletonised into a one-pixel-wide line, and exported as coordinates. A specimen-specific LOWESS-smoothed reference contour was generated, and roughness percentage was calculated from the mean absolute pointwise deviation between the original and smoothed profiles. Roughness percentage did not differ significantly across anatomical quadrants. In contrast, it differed significantly across histopathologic surface severity levels, with severely degenerated surfaces showing higher values than normal, mild, and moderate surfaces. Intra- and inter-observer reliability was excellent, with intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.994 and 0.962, respectively. This workflow provides a reproducible quantitative extension to conventional histopathologic grading with potential future application to other curved, load-bearing fibrocartilaginous tissues.</jats:p>

title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.
                  </jats:p>

The Effect of Instructional Videos On Students’ Learning Outcomes In Cell Biology In Grade XI at SMA Negeri 6 Pematangsiantar
journal: International Journal of Science, Technology & Management
abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to determine the effect of instructional videos on students’ learning outcomes in cell biology, particularly animal and plant cells, among Grade XI students at SMA Negeri 6 Pematangsiantar. The study employed a quantitative experimental approach using a pre-test and post-test control-group design. The sample consisted of 71 students: 35 students in class XI M3 as the experimental group, which learned with instructional videos, and 36 students in class XI M4 as the control group, which learned without instructional videos. Data were collected through learning-outcome tests and analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U test because the normality results indicated that the data were not normally distributed. The thesis reports that the experimental group’s mean score increased from 26.57% on the pre-test to 79.00% on the post-test. The control group increased from 25.42% to 49.47% in the results section. The Mann–Whitney test produced U = 118.500, Z = −6.017, and an asymptotic two-tailed significance value reported as 0.000 (p < 0.001). These findings indicate a statistically significant difference in learning outcomes between the two groups and support the use of instructional videos in teaching cell biology. The control-group post-test percentage requires confirmation because the thesis conclusion gives a different figure (48.47%).</jats:p>

title: Pulmonary Ionocytes Regulate CFTR-Mediated Chloride Transport in Human iPSC-Derived Epithelium
journal: American Journal of Respiratory Cell and Molecular Biology
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Rationale</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pulmonary ionocytes, representing approximately 1% of airway epithelial cells, exhibit high CFTR expression and unique transcriptional markers, including FOXI1, ASCL3, and V-ATPase. Their exact role in human airway physiology is incompletely understood.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study employs induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived airway epithelial models (iPSC-airways) to elucidate the role of FOXI1 in pulmonary ionocyte differentiation and function.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CRISPR-Cas9 was used to generate FOXI1-knockout iPSCs, into which a doxycycline-inducible FOXI1-overexpression cassette was introduced. Edited and control lines were differentiated into airway epithelia to evaluate ionocyte formation, epithelial composition, and ion transport. Rescue studies assessed the effects of FOXI1 re-expression in a FOXI1-KO background, and the addition of inducible WT-CFTR ionocytes to F508del/F508del cystic fibrosis (CF) cultures on restoring chloride transport.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Measurements and Main Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>FOXI1 deletion abolishes ionocyte formation and alters airway epithelial composition, with increased mucus-secreting goblet cells and decreased ciliated cells. Functional assays confirmed ionocytes as key regulators of chloride homeostasis, with FOXI1-deficient airways displaying diminished ion transport. Induction of FOXI1-overexpression restored CFTR-mediated chloride transport. Introduction of WT ionocytes into CF airway models rescued chloride transport deficits, with no rescue observed in vehicle-treated controls lacking ionocyte induction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings highlight FOXI1’s essential role in pulmonary ionocyte development, airway cell composition, and airway chloride transport. We present a fully manipulable, gene-edited iPSC-derived system that enables investigation of ionocyte biology and function within a human airway context, highlighting them as promising therapeutic targets for respiratory disorders.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: We mapped positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) research in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy and described clinical applications by malignancy. Methods: We combined bibliometrics, publication-level clinical annotation, and narrative comparison of selected original reports from the Web of Science Core Collection (2013–2026; 30 September 2026 snapshot). Results: Of 358 assessed records, 114 were included for bibliometrics (51 journals; 1913 citations) and 113 for clinical annotation: 87 B-cell lymphoma or non-Hodgkin lymphoma reports, 12 multiple myeloma, eight acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), and six other or nonspecific reports. Sixty reports described PET/CT before and after infusion, 33 before only, and 20 after only. Specific products or constructs were identified in 74 reports (65.5%) and not identified in 39 (34.5%). In selected lymphoma cohorts, higher baseline metabolic tumor volume and higher one-month Deauville scores were each associated with shorter progression-free survival. In separate myeloma cohorts, true extramedullary disease was associated with shorter survival, while early PET/CT negativity was not significantly associated with progression-free survival. In ALL, serial PET/CT illustrated extramedullary response in a small case series. Conclusions: Findings should be interpreted by malignancy and scan timing. The evidence does not establish a universal schedule, threshold, or benefit from imaging-guided management.</jats:p>

title: Correction: RanBP2 promotes ferroptosis resistance and compromises therapeutic response by stabilizing SLC7A11 through LRSAM1 SUMOylation and ubiquitination in lung adenocarcinoma
A Novel B-Cell-Targeted Adjuvant APRIL Improves the Breadth and Persistence of Anti-SARS-CoV-2 Immunity
abstract: <jats:p>Background: A broad, robust, and long-lasting antibody response is essential for effective anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunity and the prevention of breakthrough infections. As a key member of the tumor necrosis factor superfamily, a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) participates in multiple B cell fate processes, including B cell survival, class-switch recombination, and plasma cell (PC) differentiation, but its potential utility as a SARS-CoV-2 vaccine adjuvant remains largely unexplored. Methods: Balb/c mice were immunized with recombinant XBB.1.5 S protein formulated with alum, with or without the addition of APRIL. Serum, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), and fecal samples were collected for measuring antigen-specific IgG/IgA titers and antibody avidity by ELISA. Neutralization against Delta, BA.2.12.1, BF.7, XBB.1.5, and JN.1 was determined in HEK293-ACE2 cells, while cellular responses were assessed by flow cytometry and Enzyme-Linked Immunospot (ELISPOT). Gene expressions were quantified by RT-PCR. Results: APRIL augmented the immunogenicity of XBB.1.5 S in a dose-dependent manner. It promoted the generation of both systemic and mucosal antibodies, broadened the binding breadth and avidity, and conferred superior neutralizing activity against multiple variants. During a 20-week post-immunization monitoring period, mice maintained effective antibody titers and retained the capacity to neutralize diverse variants. Mechanistically, APRIL was associated with upregulated AICDA and UNG mRNA expressions, accompanied by expansion of the B cell repertoire, differentiation into PCs and antigen-specific memory B cells, and maintenance of high-avidity long-lived PCs. Conclusions: APRIL acts as an effective adjuvant that elicits broad-spectrum, long-lasting immunity against SARS-CoV-2 variants. It represents a promising immunostimulatory component for optimizing the performance of recombinant spike protein vaccines.</jats:p>

title: Transformasi Akuntansi Manajemen pada Era Artificial Intelligence: Tinjauan Literatur Terstruktur tentang Efisiensi, Pengendalian Biaya, dan Pengambilan Keputusan Management Accounting Transformation in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Structured Literature Review on Efficiency, Cost Control, and Decision-Making
journal: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies
abstract: <jats:p>Aim: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in four core management accounting functions: cost analysis, budgeting, management control, and decision-making. Method: A structured literature review synthesizes findings from systematic reviews, case studies, experiments, a dissertation, and professional reports to distinguish demonstrated predictive benefits from broader claims about organizational performance. The review is limited by the absence of a complete database export and a study-specific PRISMA flow; it should therefore be read as a structured synthesis of accessible literature rather than a fully reproducible systematic review. Results: Machine-learning models can match or exceed human estimates in selected cost-estimation tasks when adequate historical data are available. In budgeting, machine learning can improve prediction accuracy, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish causal effects or guarantee appropriate resource allocation. In management control, digital tools support more timely and anticipatory monitoring, although the available evidence does not always isolate the effect of AI itself. For decision-making, the usefulness of AI depends on data quality, model explainability, user trust, professional competence, and the preservation of human accountability. Novelty/Implications: The novelty lies in organizing the evidence by management accounting function and strength of evidence, separating technical outcomes (prediction accuracy) from organizational outcomes. AI is best positioned as support for professional judgment rather than a replacement for management accountants. Organizations need data governance, model evaluation, and training to ensure responsible adoption, and the article proposes an empirical research agenda, particularly in Indonesian organizations, on AI use, efficiency, cost control, and decision quality.</jats:p>

title: Transformasi Wakaf Produktif sebagai Instrumen Pemberdayaan dan Kesejahteraan: Analisis Efektivitas Pengelolaan Wakaf pada BPW Ar Risalah Kota Padang The Transformation of Productive Waqf as an Instrument of Empowerment and Welfare: An Analysis of Waqf Management Effectiveness at BPW Ar Risalah, Padang City
journal: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies
abstract: <jats:p>Aim: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of productive waqf management in improving the welfare of beneficiaries at the Waqf Management Board (BPW) Ar Risalah, Padang City. Method: The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with field research. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with four beneficiaries and institutional documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing based on five effectiveness indicators: program understanding, target accuracy, timeliness, goal achievement, and monitoring. Results: BPW Ar Risalah is effective as a benefit distributor (distributive effectiveness): targeting is perceived as accurate, distribution is generally on time with one compensated delay, and monitoring is conducted periodically according to the type of beneficiary. Social assistance of IDR 500,000 per month, scholarships of IDR 1,500,000 per semester, and income of IDR 1,500,000 per month contribute to meeting living needs, education, and income stability, with job creation as the most transformative benefit. However, transformative effectiveness cannot yet be fully concluded: beneficiaries' understanding of the concept and mechanism of productive waqf remains limited, the benefit amounts are supplementary, and monitoring does not yet measure impact. Novelty: This study assesses the effectiveness of productive waqf directly from the beneficiaries' perspective using five indicators within a single analytical framework, and distinguishes distributive from transformative effectiveness. Productive waqf has the potential to become an empowerment instrument, provided that beneficiary literacy, follow-up empowerment pathways, impact evaluation, and asset performance transparency are strengthened.</jats:p>

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: <jats:p>Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.</jats:p>

title: Game-based learning bilang estratehiyang pedagohikal sa pagtuturo ng Filipino sa elementarya: Karanasan at hamon sa mga guro
journal: International Journal of Research Studies in Education
abstract: <jats:p>Tinalakay sa pag-aaral na ito ang paggamit ng game-based learning bilang estratehiya sa pagtuturo ng Filipino sa elementarya. Binigyang-pansin dito ang mga larong ginagamit ng mga guro, ang kanilang mga karanasan sa paggamit nito, ang mga benepisyong naidudulot sa pagkatuto ng mga mag-aaral, at ang mga hamong kinakaharap sa pagpapatupad nito. Gumamit ang pag-aaral ng kwalitatibong disenyo sa pamamagitan ng penomenolohikal na pamamaraan. Sampung (10) guro mula sa Guruyan Elementary School na may aktuwal na karanasan sa pagbuo at paggamit ng game-based learning ang pinili sa pamamagitan ng purposive sampling. Isinagawa ang pangangalap ng datos gamit ang semi-structured interview na nakabatay sa mga gabay na tanong upang higit na maunawaan ang kanilang mga karanasan at pananaw. Sinuri ang mga nakalap na datos sa pamamagitan ng tematikong pagsusuri upang matukoy ang magkakatulad na ideya at mabuo ang mga pangunahing tema. Batay sa mga natuklasan, tatlong digital na plataporma ang ginagamit ng mga guro sa pagtuturo ng Filipino: Wordwall, Quizlet, at Quizizz. Nakatutulong ang mga ito upang gawing mas kawili-wili ang mga aralin, mapataas ang interes at pakikilahok ng mga mag-aaral, mahikayat ang pagtutulungan, at mapadali ang pagtataya sa kanilang pagkatuto. Gayunpaman, nakararanas ang mga guro ng ilang hamon, kabilang ang kakulangan sa mga kagamitang teknolohikal at maayos na koneksyon sa internet, pamamahala ng oras at kaayusan ng klase, at limitadong pagsasanay sa wastong paggamit ng mga larong pampagkatuto. Ipinakikita ng pag-aaral na maaaring maging makabuluhang estratehiya ang game-based learning sa pagtuturo ng Filipino sapagkat ginagawa nitong mas masigla, kawili-wili, at interaktibo ang proseso ng pagkatuto. Gayunman, mahalagang maiangkop ang mga larong ginagamit sa mga layunin ng aralin at pangangailangan ng mga mag-aaral upang higit na maging mabisa ang pagtuturo at pagkatuto.</jats:p>

Reliability-Aware Adaptive Split Federated Learning with Uncertainty-Guided Personalization for Non-IID ECG Classification in IoMT Networks
abstract: <jats:p>The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) enables distributed electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring, but statistical and resource heterogeneity complicates collaborative learning. This study proposes Reliability-Aware Adaptive Split Federated Learning (RA-ASFL) for non-independent and non-identically distributed (non-IID) ECG classification. The framework integrates three mechanisms: adaptive split selection based on resource constraints, privacy exposure risk, predictive uncertainty, and split-conditioned reliability; reliability-aware aggregation using client-level learning quality and stability to determine separate contribution weights; and uncertainty-guided global–local personalization. These mechanisms distinguish computation placement, client reliability estimation, and aggregation influence. Experiments used five-class MIT-BIH heartbeat classification and five-superclass multilabel PTB-XL classification under simulated heterogeneous IoMT conditions. On MIT-BIH, RA-ASFL achieved 98.03% accuracy, 97.93% F1-score, and 99.43% ROC-AUC, exceeding resource-only AdaptSFL by 0.55 and 0.58 percentage points in accuracy and F1-score, respectively. On PTB-XL, macro AUROC reached 94.3% and macro F1-score reached 74.6%, compared with 92.8% and 72.3% for AdaptSFL. Ablation results identified reliability-aware aggregation and personalization as the principal contributors to predictive performance, while adaptive splitting provided additional benefits. These findings support coordinated reliability-aware learning for ECG classification under simulated heterogeneous IoMT conditions.</jats:p>

title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of
                      <jats:italic>Rhus chinensis</jats:italic>
                      in complex mountainous field conditions.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1% increase in mAP and approximately a 5.6 times improvement in FPS compared to the original YOLOv5s.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight model and acceleration strategies effectively balance high accuracy with high-throughput onboard image processing. The developed UAV-edge computing system provides a promising prototype for future efficient nectar flowering status monitoring, with potential applications in smart apiculture.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Screening and Evaluation of Computationally Predicted JAK1-Binding Candidates from Multi-Source Chemical Space Using Deep Learning and Generative Models
abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) is a key mediator in inflammatory and autoimmune signaling pathways and represents a validated therapeutic target. Despite the availability of several JAK inhibitors, challenges in safety and efficacy persist, necessitating further computational prioritization of candidate molecules. Methods: We developed an integrated virtual screening workflow combining ensemble deep learning scoring (KPGT, KarmaDock, DrugCLIP), ADMET-AI filtering, and AutoDock Vina (v1.2.3) docking. The workflow was applied to the NPBS Atlas natural-product database and to molecules generated by 3DSMILES-GPT. Selected candidates were further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations, DFT calculations, and synthetic accessibility assessment, with Filgotinib used as a reference compound. Results: Three natural-product-derived and three AI-generated molecules were prioritized. Among them, the MM-PBSA-estimated binding free energies were −26.251 kcal/mol for NPBS_111591, −19.858 kcal/mol for 3DSMILES_17365, and −19.593 kcal/mol for 3DSMILES_38767, compared with −29.253 kcal/mol for the reference compound Filgotinib. These MM-PBSA values were obtained under the same computational protocol and can provide relative computational comparisons, but pharmacological potency still requires validation by IC50 or biochemical binding assays. Conclusions: The study prioritizes computationally predicted JAK1-binding candidates and provides a multi-stage in silico workflow for further experimental evaluation.</jats:p>

title: A Frequency‐Decomposed Residual Learning Framework for Volume Data Neural Representation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Implicit neural representations (INRs) have been widely adopted for volume data modeling in scientific visualization due to their continuous representation capability and flexibility. However, existing INR‐based methods still struggle to accurately capture high‐frequency details due to spectral bias, which can degrade reconstruction quality and affect downstream analysis. To address this issue, we propose a frequency‐decomposed residual learning framework for neural volume representation. Specifically, we decompose the volume data into low‐frequency components and high‐frequency residuals, and jointly model them with a shared INR by reformulating volume representation as a multi‐task learning (MTL) problem. To alleviate potential learning conflicts between different frequency branches while preserving model compactness, we introduce a lightweight feature gating mechanism on top of the shared backbone to adaptively reweight shared features for the two branches, enabling more effective modeling of low‐ and high‐frequency information. Experimental results on multiple scientific datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches in reconstruction, super‐resolution, and compression tasks, while maintaining comparable model size and computational efficiency. Further ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed frequency‐decomposition and feature gating mechanism. Source code is publicly available at
                    <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="https://github.com/LiuLan2001/FDNR">https://github.com/LiuLan2001/FDNR</jats:ext-link>
                    .
                  </jats:p>

title: Estimation of Rice Leaf Area Index Coupling Feature Selection from Multi-Temporal UAV Imagery with Machine Learning
abstract: <jats:p>Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a key biophysical parameter characterizing crop canopy structure and growth status. Large-scale, dynamic, and high-precision estimation of LAI using remote sensing is critical for crop growth assessment and yield forecasting. This study investigates rice LAI estimation across multiple growth stages by integrating optimally selected features from multi-temporal unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery into modeling algorithms. Based on controlled experiments with varying nitrogen fertilizer gradients, rice field LAI data were synchronously collected alongside high-resolution red–green–blue (RGB) and multispectral UAV images. Vegetation spectral indices were then extracted, and principal component analysis (PCA) was performed on these indices to obtain the first principal component (PC1). Subsequently, gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) calculations were conducted on the PC1 image to extract texture features. Feature selection was performed separately using recursive feature elimination (RFE) guided by Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) for random forest (RF), variable importance in projection (VIP) for partial least squares regression (PLSR), and backward elimination for stepwise regression (SR). Each model was developed using its corresponding selected predictors for individual growth stages and the combined dataset. The results demonstrated that the RF model for the entire growth cycle performed the best, with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9197, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.4309, and a relative root mean square error (rRMSE) of 16.85%. The estimated LAI maps clearly revealed the spatial distribution patterns and gradient variations in LAI under different growth stages and nitrogen treatments. Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that integrating multi-source, multi-temporal UAV remote sensing features with modeling algorithms enables the high-precision retrieval of rice LAI, effectively capturing within-field growth heterogeneity. This study provides reliable technical insights for dynamic crop monitoring, variable-rate fertilization decision-making, and smart agricultural management.</jats:p>

title: Lifecycle Narrative: Reconstructing the Development Process of a Machine Learning Model
abstract: <jats:p>Machine learning models are increasingly proposed for high-risk domains, such as healthcare and public policymaking. However, their growing complexity creates significant obstacles to transparency. This complexity arises from various factors; in this work, we focus on making the organizational development process of a model transparent. A model is often developed over many years and involves multiple version updates, carried out by different individuals, and based on varying subsets of data. To address these issues, we propose a new model reporting framework called a lifecycle narrative, characterized by three dimensions: first, how the purpose of the model has incrementally evolved over time; second, how the data used in the model and the model itself have been developed; and third, what inferences can be made with the model and what the consequences of its use are. We demonstrate these three dimensions using a case study of a high-risk application in healthcare. Our framework complements existing model reporting tools, such as model cards and datasheets, by reconstructing the full lifecycle of the model—a documentation requirement of the EU AI Act. Ultimately, the lifecycle narrative empowers external stakeholders, such as regulators, researchers, citizens, and national competent authorities, to holistically understand a model’s development process.</jats:p>

title: Assessing Machine Learning Model Stability and the Value of Hyperparameter Transfer: Effects of Sample Size and Dataset Heterogeneity
abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This study investigates two critical factors affecting the performance of traditional machine learning (ML) models: training dataset size and the impact of integrating external, potentially noisy data (dataset heterogeneity). Additionally, we evaluate the effectiveness of hyperparameter transfer. Experiments utilized three distinct COVID-19 blood test datasets: the Wuhan dataset (356 cases), used as the source for hyperparameter extraction; the San Raffaele Hospital (OSR) dataset (1,624 cases), serving as the primary target for training, testing, and creating balanced subsets of varying sizes; and the Istituto Ortopedico Galeazzi (IOG) dataset (58 cases), which was integrated to simulate heterogeneity due to its collection via different devices and clinical settings. The discussion extends to a simple TL approach in which optimal hyperparameters were transferred from the Wuhan source to OSR target models. Both Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) and Generalized Linear Model (GLM) algorithms were tested in traditional and TL settings. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity. Results show that data quantity and quality substantially influence model performance, with saturation typically observed around 450–500 observations. The addition of external, noisy data (IOG) significantly impacted specificity, particularly in GBM models trained on smaller OSR samples. Specifically, the GBM-based hyperparameter transfer learning (HTL) model demonstrated a “crossover” effect; while it initially lagged behind traditional ML in accuracy at low data volumes (0.74 vs. 0.78 at n = 50), it surpassed ML in larger datasets, reaching a peak accuracy of 0.87 (vs. 0.84 for ML) at n = 1,100. However, due to heterogeneity, this approach also exhibited sensitivity fluctuations in high-data regimes. GLM models demonstrated greater robustness with consistent accuracy levels (~0.84) and minimal variance, possibly due to their simpler structure and better alignment with underlying data characteristics. This study highlights the importance of considering both training data volume and integrity in ML and TL applications. While increasing the quantity of data can enhance performance, the unfiltered inclusion of noisy external data may degrade it. Hyperparameter transfer is a promising strategy for maintaining model reliability across varying data conditions.</jats:p>

title: An Integrated Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Cell-to-Pack Imbalance Prediction in Electric Vehicle Battery Systems
journal: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
abstract: <jats:p>This study presents a machine learning framework for predicting cell-to-pack imbalance in electric vehicle batteries. A set of battery attributes that affect battery performance, including State of Charge (SOC), State of Health (SOH), temperature (including ambient temperature and humidity), and cabin temperature, were used to make this prediction. The collected battery data were pre-processed to improve prediction performance. Three preprocessing methods were used: (i) Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD); (ii) deep denoising autoencoders, and (iii) feature selection using minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) mutual information. This preprocessing step removes noise from the dataset and identifies useful information for prediction. Cell-to-pack imbalance prediction was performed using three interpretable machine learning models: (i) an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM); (ii) fuzzy regression; and (iii) RuleFit. These models provide transparent predictions and help in understanding the factors responsible for battery imbalance. Models were evaluated on an independent 20-sample test set held out from the 100-record dataset. Among the three interpretable models, Fuzzy Regression achieved the strongest predictive performance (R² = 0.998), followed by RuleFit (R² = 0.976), while EBM achieved a lower R² of 0.201 on this independent test set despite providing detailed feature-level explanations. These results indicate that combining signal preprocessing, feature selection, and interpretable regression can provide useful and explainable information for cell-to-pack imbalance prediction, while also showing that performance can vary substantially between interpretable models on a small, two-pack dataset; validation on larger and more varied battery datasets is needed to confirm generalizability.</jats:p>

title: EXTREPSO: An Energy Estimator Based on Machine Learning with PSO Optimization for UASNs
abstract: <jats:p>Underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) are severely affected by propagation delay, limited bandwidth, and constrained node energy. This work presents EXTREPSO, a machine learning framework that combines an Extra Trees Regressor with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for offline hyperparameter tuning of a hop-level energy-efficiency predictor. The target is derived from Aqua-Sim NG trace fields using the payload size, the simulator Tx_power field, and observed hop delay. Aqua-Sim NG defines PT as transmitted signal power in watts, so the target has dimensional units of bit/J; however, because the observed hop delay includes propagation and protocol-related waiting, it is treated as an operational trace-derived metric rather than a state-resolved modem-energy measurement. In the original 80:20 benchmark, Extra Trees was the strongest baseline among seven classical ML and three DL models. A leakage-resistant sender-grouped outer five-fold evaluation with inner grouped validation was subsequently used to compare baseline Extra Trees, PSO-tuned Extra Trees, and an interpretable inverse-power baseline on untouched test folds. PSO tuning produced a modest average improvement over baseline Extra Trees (mean RMSE 2107.31 versus 2230.58), but the improvement was not consistent across folds; the inverse-power baseline achieved the lowest mean RMSE (1765.88). A separate five-run equal-budget PSO/GWO sensitivity check also found no meaningful superiority of PSO over GWO. These results support the trace-driven prediction and hyperparameter-tuning workflow while limiting claims of universal optimizer benefit or direct network-energy improvement.</jats:p>

title: A pilot classroom intervention using project-based learning for steel framing design in a civil engineering course
abstract: <jats:p>Project-based learning in Civil Engineering can connect structural modelling, standards application, and technical communication through an authentic design task. This descriptive educational case study documents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a semester-long steel-framing redesign project. It examines what its collective output reveals about the traceability of calculations and collective assessment. Twenty-five seventh-semester students worked in five groups for approximately 16 weeks and consolidated their contributions into a single redesign project. The activity combined interpreting reference documents, structural configuration, modelling in SAP2000, verification against regulations, preparing drawings, receiving tutor feedback, and preparing the calculation report. The lecturer assessed the integrated project using a weighted rubric comprising eight criteria. The project achieved a total score of 85 per cent, with 100 per cent for structural configuration, application of standards, and presentation, but 60 per cent for the calculation report. The technical results characterised the collective output and, together with the rubric, enabled a distinction between the project's computational execution and the traceability of the documented calculations. The case study identifies calculation traceability and the limitations of collective assessment as teaching issues. For future implementations, it is proposed to introduce staged calculation logs and direct assessment of individual reasoning.</jats:p>

title: Development and external validation of an interpretable machine learning model for identifying prevalent metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in patients with early-onset type 2 diabetes
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with early-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus (EOT2D) are at high risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet interpretable tools for estimating prevalent MASLD in this population are lacking. We developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model using routinely available clinical variables to prompt consideration of liver ultrasonography at the index visit.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We included 1,322 outpatients and inpatients with EOT2D (907 [68.6%] with prevalent MASLD), divided 7:3 into training (n = 925) and internal test (n = 397) sets. After multiple imputation by chained equations (m = 5), 68 candidate variables underwent least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, Boruta selection, and collinearity screening (variance inflation factor &lt; 5). Eight machine learning models were tuned by 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was selected on the basis of internal discrimination and calibration, interpreted with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and externally validated in 515 patients (68.0% with MASLD) from four affiliated community hospitals in the same region.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twelve variables were retained. The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model matched the leading algorithms in discrimination and maintained stable calibration. It achieved an AUROC of 0.773 (95% CI 0.721–0.824; AUPRC 0.864) in the internal test set and 0.753 (95% CI 0.708–0.797; AUPRC 0.852) in the external cohort, with calibration slopes of 1.03 and 0.93 and Brier scores of 0.169 and 0.180. SHAP identified total protein, globulin, albumin, and indirect bilirubin as the leading contributors. Complete-case analysis (AUROC 0.751), five random splits (0.764 ± 0.023), and nested cross-validation (0.755) were consistent with the main analysis. A free web calculator provides individualised probabilities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An XGBoost model based on 12 routinely available variables estimated prevalent MASLD in EOT2D with moderate discrimination and good calibration. External validation was institutional, geographic, and temporal but confined to one region. The model is intended to prompt consideration of liver ultrasonography during routine diabetes care and to complement ultrasound and clinical judgment. Prospective implementation studies are required before clinical adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Enhanced FusionNet: a deep learning structure for multimodal input-based emotion-aware deepfake speech identification
abstract: <jats:p>Voice-based deepfakes pose a significant security concern for voice-based systems and require effective methods for distinguishing genuine and synthetic speech. This study presents Enhanced FusionNet, an emotion-aware deep learning framework for deepfake speech detection that combines Log-Mel-based acoustic representations with MultiScaleCNN, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Multi-Head Cross-Attention, Residual Feature Fusion, and Adaptive Gated Fusion. An emotion representation is learned separately from the RAVDESS dataset using a speaker-independent emotion encoder and subsequently transferred to the FoR-based deepfake detection framework. On the independent FoR hold-out test set, Enhanced FusionNet achieved 98.67% accuracy, 98.18% precision, 99.17% recall, 98.67% F1-score, and 99.88% ROC-AUC. Five-fold cross-validation produced a mean accuracy of 99.08 ± 0.35% and ROC-AUC of 99.94 ± 0.05%. The model further achieved 99.40% sensitivity, 98.75% specificity, and 0.91% EER in the out-of-fold evaluation. Component-level ablation analysis demonstrated the varying contributions of the major architectural components, while a controlled FoR-only versus FoR + Emotion experiment showed that the transferred emotion representation provided complementary information but did not improve overall detection performance under the evaluated protocol. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of Enhanced FusionNet under the evaluated benchmark conditions, while also highlighting the need for external cross-dataset and unseen-generation evaluation. Future work will focus on multilingual and cross-domain evaluation, contemporary anti-spoofing baselines, unseen synthesis methods, and computationally efficient variants for real-time deployment.</jats:p>

title: English translation enhancement technology supported by deep learning and knowledge graphs
From Evaluation to Legacy: Reflecting on Over a Decade of Citizen Science Learning and Impact
abstract: <jats:p>How do you robustly evaluate a citizen science project, capturing long-term value, such as participant agency and community ownership, which frequently emerge only after formal funding ends, without excessively burdening participants? The Inclusive Citizen Science group draws on nearly two decades of practice across diverse initiatives, tracing the evolution of our approaches to evaluation and legacy planning, to offer effective strategies. It is valuable to integrate a monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) framework and legacy planning from a project’s inception to strengthen both project outcomes and ways of working. Developing a theory of change (ToC) helps align activities with goals. Obtaining and using feedback from participants and researchers to improve a project during its lifetime is as valuable as summative evaluation. Adopting pragmatic mixed methods helps capture diverse outcomes. Implementing “soft endings” maintains trust and prevents extractive relationships. We provide recommendations that prioritise learning and inclusivity to ensure citizen science delivers lasting socio-ecological impact.</jats:p>

NEUROCIÊNCIAS NA EDUCAÇÃO: CONTRIBUIÇÕES DA NEUROPLASTICIDADE PARA O PROCESSO DE ENSINO E APRENDIZAGEM EDUCATIONAL NEUROSCIENCE: CONTRIBUTIONS OF NEUROPLASTICITY TO THE TEACHING AND LEARNING PROCESS NEUROCIENCIAS EN LA EDUCACIÓN: CONTRIBUCIONES DE LA NEUROPLASTICIDAD AL PROCESO DE ENSEÑANZA Y APRENDIZAJE
abstract: <jats:p>Nas últimas décadas, as neurociências têm avançado significadamente em relação ao funcionamento do cérebro humano e nos processos de aprendizagem. O desenvolvimento de técnicas e pesquisas permitiu identificar mecanismos cerebrais envolvidos na aquisição do conhecimento, na memória, na atenção, na linguagem e nas funções executivas, fornecendo importantes contribuições para o campo educacional. Nesse contexto, a aproximação entre Neurociência e Educação tem sido de suma relevância para o desenvolvimento da Neuroeducação, cujo objetivo é compreender como o conhecimento científico sobre o cérebro pode subsidiar práticas pedagógicas mais eficazes.A neuroplasticidade refere-se à capacidade do cérebro de criar, fortalecer, reorganizar ou eliminar conexões sinápticas em resposta aos estímulos provenientes do ambiente que a criança está inserida. Cada que nova aprendizagem venha provocar alterações tornando o cérebro um órgão dinâmico e permanentemente adaptável. Portanto, os avanços científicos, observa-se que muitos conceitos da Neurociência ainda são interpretados de forma errada no ambiente educacional. As funções cerebrais ou a existência de estilos fixos de aprendizagem não encontram respaldo científico, mas continuam influenciando práticas pedagógicas. Dessa forma, torna-se indispensável aproximar educadores das evidências produzidas pelas pesquisas neurocientíficas, promovendo uma formação continuada baseada em conhecimento científico.</jats:p>

title: A Lightweight Hybrid Representation Learning Framework for Colorectal Lesion Classification in Colonoscopy Images
abstract: <jats:p>Accurate colorectal lesion classification is important for computer-aided colonoscopy, yet many existing approaches require computationally intensive architectures. This study proposed and experimentally evaluated LHRF, which integrates BoVW encoding, SAE compression, TE-based metric refinement, optional HC augmentation, and FC-ResNet classification. Two configurations were investigated: LHRF-Core (BoVW → SAE → TE → FC-ResNet) and LHRF-HC, which additionally incorporates clustering-derived features. The experiments included three study-specific binary classification tasks constructed from CVC-ClinicDB, CVC-ColonDB, and a merged Kvasir/Kvasir-SEG collection. The CVC tasks used study-assigned sequence-level pathology categories, with sequence-grouped evaluation for CVC-ClinicDB and source-grouped evaluation for CVC-ColonDB. LHRF-HC achieved the highest accuracy on CVC-ClinicDB (96.24%, AUC 0.9741, MCC 0.9248), whereas LHRF-Core achieved the best results on CVC-ColonDB (95.88%, AUC 0.9698, MCC 0.9176) and Kvasir/Kvasir-SEG (98.74%, AUC 0.9908, MCC 0.9746). Five-fold cross-validation on CVC-ClinicDB yielded an accuracy of 97.43 ± 1.29%. Under matched experimental protocols, LHRF achieved higher classification accuracy than the evaluated lightweight baselines while requiring approximately 0.45–0.51 million trainable parameters. Measured post-decoding CPU throughput ranged from 351.67 to 2353.97 FPS, excluding image decoding and disk input/output. HC improved accuracy on CVC-ClinicDB but slightly reduced it on the other datasets, indicating a dataset-dependent contribution. The study also specified a gradient-based keypoint-attribution procedure, although its empirical faithfulness and clinical interpretability require further evaluation. Overall, the experimental findings highlight the potential of compact hybrid representation learning for colorectal lesion classification. Further evaluation using independently verified pathology annotations, patient-independent partitions, source-matched datasets, and external clinical collections would strengthen the assessment of robustness and clinical generalizability.</jats:p>

title: The DIRIS model for extending reflective learning through knowledge sharing in digital ecosystems
abstract: <jats:p>This study proposes the Design–Implement–Reflect–Improve–Share (DIRIS) framework and provides an initial empirical examination of its central reflective-sharing mechanism. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 350 in-service secondary school teachers in Vietnam using purposive sampling methods. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring reflective learning, knowledge sharing, and self-reported teacher professional development and analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The findings revealed positive associations between reflective learning and knowledge sharing and between knowledge sharing and perceived professional development. The direct association between reflective learning and professional development was not statistically significant, whereas the indirect association through knowledge sharing was significant. Although the measurement model showed a close fit, some limitations in construct validity were identified. These findings provide initial empirical support for the proposed reflective-sharing mechanism but do not establish causal mediation or validate the complete five-phase DIRIS framework. This study contributes an integrative conceptual framework and highlights the need for longitudinal research and further validation of the measurement.</jats:p>

title: Enhancing the robustness of brain-inspired perception decision machine for fake speech detection
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The rapid development of speech synthesis, voice conversion, and large-scale generative models has made fake speech more natural and difficult to detect. Existing detectors can respond differently to the same sample, yet fixed fusion does not use the state of each detector to decide how much that detector should contribute.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Building on the brain-inspired perception-decision framework of Feng et al., we propose the Dynamic Routing Perception-Decision Machine (DR-PDM). The method retains detector embeddings, class probabilities, one-class Softmax scores, and evidential uncertainty as detector-state information, and uses these states to generate sample-dependent fusion weights. For internally evaluated systems, operating thresholds are selected by a reproducible discrete equal-error-rate rule on development scores and frozen before evaluation. WaveFake uses its own nonoverlapping training, development, and evaluation splits: all four experts and the Router/fusion backend are trained on WaveFake training data, and no ASVspoof-trained expert weights are used. It is therefore a within-dataset experiment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>At the applied thresholds, DR-PDM obtains precision/missing-rate pairs of 99.995%/2.085%, 99.815%/0.930%, and 100.000%/0.007% on ASVspoof2019 LA, ASVspoof2021 LA, and WaveFake, respectively. The zero-false-positive WaveFake result has a two-sided 95% exact precision interval of 99.986% –100.000%. A serial FP32 benchmark of the complete 1.292-billion-parameter system on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 measures 102.919 ms mean forward-pass latency for a 4.0375-s input, or 4.260 times the average single-expert latency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The evidence supports detector-state routing under the evaluated protocols, but does not establish overall error reduction, cross-dataset WaveFake transfer, or low-cost deployment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Thickness sensing and anomaly detection for shotcrete support in roadways based on machine learning
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Aiming at the problem that the shotcrete thickness detection in roadway engineering relies on discrete manual spot checks and it is difficult to identify continuous low-thickness regions, this paper constructs the full-field thickness perception and anomaly detection method (FTP-AD). Taking the two-phase light detection and ranging point clouds before and after shotcreting as input, this method establishes the surface correspondence through global registration and region of interest local registration, and uses floor correction and principal normal translation preservation to reduce the offset of registration to the change of shotcrete thickness. Subsequently, while retaining the candidate points at high-curvature boundaries, sparse outliers are eliminated, a finite-length normal cylindrical neighborhood is used to estimate the local thickness, and the thickness field is formed through median smoothing, then the connected low-thickness regions are extracted combined with the designed thickness limit. Verified by 20 measuring points on a single roadway interface, the results show that the mean absolute error of FTP-AD is 4.52 mm and the root mean square error is 5.69 mm, both lower than the comparison configurations using traditional ICP, point-to-plane ICP and M3C2. The ablation results further indicate that both floor correction and principal normal translation preservation help to reduce the thickness measurement error. In this case, the proposed method realizes the spatial expression of the shotcrete thickness distribution and the concentrated low-thickness positions, and provides quantitative information for the quality evaluation of roadway shotcrete support.</jats:p>

title: Enhancing Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Image Quality Using Deep Learning-based Super-Resolution
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To develop deep learning super-resolution (SR) models for enhancing cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Seventy CBCT volumes (75 µm voxel size) served as references. Paired low-resolution (LR) volumes (300 µm) were simulated using physics-based degradation. Four architectures were each trained with three loss configurations (L1; L1+edge; L1+edge+perceptual): Swin Transformer for Image Restoration (SwinIR), Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT), Hybrid Multi-Axis Aggregation Network (HMA-Net), and Dense-Residual-Connected Transformer (DRCT). Performance was assessed with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS), and deep image structure and texture similarity (DISTS). Three dentists ranked the 12 configurations in 28 sets using blinded forced-choice pairwise comparisons. Correlations of metrics and expert ranks were assessed using Spearman correlation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>All configurations outperformed LR input and bicubic interpolation on every metric (p &lt; 0.05). HMA-Net trained with L1+edge+perceptual loss performed best on LPIPS (0.216) and DISTS (0.186). HAT with L1 loss achieved the highest PSNR (28.79 dB) and SSIM (0.820). Experts ranked DRCT and HAT with L1 loss, and DRCT with L1+edge loss, as the best configurations (p &lt; 0.001 versus others). Expert rank correlated moderately only with PSNR (rho = -0.65) and SSIM (rho = -0.60; both p &lt; 0.05).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Transformer-based SR improved the perceived quality of clinical CBCT images. HAT and DRCT trained with L1 pixel loss alone, and DRCT trained with L1 and edge loss, demonstrated superior performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Advances in knowledge</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Transformer-based super-resolution improved expert-perceived detail of simulated low-resolution in vivo CBCT scans without additional radiation dose, supporting further validation on directly acquired low-resolution scans.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Validation-aware interpretable machine learning for sustainability-oriented monitoring of monthly NDVI anomalies in an alpine basin of Qinghai, China
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    This study evaluates the accuracy and spatiotemporal generalization of machine-learning estimates of baseline-referenced monthly NDVI anomalies in an alpine study area in Qinghai, China. Pixel-wise reference anomalies were calculated from a 2006 to 2015 monthly climatology, and predictors from 2016 to 2025 included contemporaneous and lagged hydrothermal variables, antecedent NDVI anomalies, and terrain and soil attributes on a common 30 m grid. Target-month NDVI was used to define the observed response, not as a direct model predictor. Five algorithms were assessed using random-split and spatial-block validation, together with a 2025 withheld-year assessment that also informed model selection. Under predefined configurations, gradient boosting decision trees achieved the most favorable overall withheld-year validation performance. A reduced configuration combining month, contemporaneous hydrothermal variables, and lagged NDVI anomalies achieved R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.263 and RMSE = 1.145 in 2025, compared with R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.254 and RMSE = 1.152 for the full configuration. Lagged NDVI supplied the strongest predictive signal, whereas terrain and soil covariates added little skill. The results characterize same-month anomaly estimation under the evaluated conditions; applications to missing-data reconstruction and management decision-making require separate validation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Forecasting High Electricity Demand Using Explainable Machine Learning
journal: Balkan Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The objective of this study was to predict the onset of high demand, the highest half-hourly average power, and the total duration of high demand over the next two hours using historical electricity consumption data from residential households. Half-hourly measurements from 2013 for 200 standard-tariff residential households selected from the Low Carbon London dataset were used. High demand was defined as exceeding the 90th percentile of each household’s average power values during the January–February period. The models were developed using data from 160 households; transfer performance was evaluated on the 40 households not included in model training. The process was divided into a training period (March–June), model selection in July, calibration of prediction intervals in August, and a testing period (September–December). The selected models were retrained using March–July data. Separate models were built for the three targets; Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB), XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared against a weekly seasonal reference. Model selection was initially based on average precision (AP) for the target and mean absolute error (MAE) for power and duration. For the residential units used in the training, the HistGB model selected during the testing period produced an AP of 0.4183; the CatBoost models produced an MAE of 0.2704 kW for power and 9.2361 minutes for duration. The contributions of historical consumption and calendar features to the model predictions were examined using the SHAP method. In the early warning evaluation, 78.81% of relevant events in known residential units were detected in advance; 60.93% of early warnings were identified as false alarms. The improvement in duration prediction relative to a reference that yields a duration of zero in every window remained limited. The findings indicate that the approach could contribute to monitoring residential demand; however, the burden of false alarms and the limited success in duration prediction must be taken into account from a practical standpoint.</jats:p>

title: Feature Fusion for Winter Wheat SPAD Estimation Using Pooled Samples from Multiple Growth Stages: A Multi-Source Deep Learning Approach
abstract: <jats:p>SPAD values indicate relative leaf chlorophyll content and support winter wheat growth and nitrogen monitoring. This study evaluated spectral–texture feature fusion using pooled samples from multiple growth stages. UAV multispectral imagery and 288 SPAD samples were collected at jointing, booting, early and late grain filling in 2021 and 2022. Vegetation indices (VIs) and texture features (TFs) were calculated from the imagery. Multidimensional spectral feature combination indices (D-SFCIs) and multidimensional texture feature combination indices (D-TFCIs) were generated using combination formulas from previous studies, with 12 features selected for each group. A multi-source deep feature neural network (MSDNN) used separate fully connected branches for spectral and texture feature extraction, followed by deep feature fusion and joint training. It was compared with partial least squares regression (PLSR), random forest (RF), and a deep neural network (DNN). In the sample-level split, MSDNN achieved the highest accuracy among the four models using the same 48 spectral and texture features (R2 = 0.866, RMSE = 5.222, RRMSE = 14.9%). Feature screening preceded this split, and some plots contributed observations to both the training and test sets. In the primary evaluation on held-out plots, MSDNN achieved a lower test RMSE than DNN in one of three splits. Across the three splits, MSDNN performed similarly to DNN but did not outperform it on average (mean R2: 0.796 vs. 0.802, RMSE: 6.424 vs. 6.290, RRMSE: 17.8% vs. 17.4%). Because this evaluation used only fused inputs, the benefit of fusion over spectral or texture features alone remains to be tested on held-out plots.</jats:p>

title: Rapid prediction of microscale stress fields in fiber-reinforced composites from limited finite element data using a deep learning framework
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part L: Journal of Materials: Design and Applications
abstract:

                    Predicting transverse stress response of fiber-reinforced polymer composites at the microstructural level traditionally relies on finite element method (FEM) simulations of representative volume elements, which are computationally expensive and time-consuming. While deep learning offers a faster surrogate, most existing approaches require hundreds to thousands of FEM-generated training samples, creating a significant data bottleneck. The results demonstrate that accurate stress-contour prediction can be achieved using as few as 20 base representative volume element simulations, expanded to 80 training samples through rotation and reflection augmentation. To address this limited dataset and emphasize mechanically critical stress concentration regions, a two-stage U-Net framework with a dual-output head and a custom attention loss based on red–green–blue (RGB) pixel values was developed. The first stage trains the model on exaggerated stress contours to identify regions of peak stress, while the second refines predictions using standard stress contours to recover realistic stress magnitudes. title: Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation of AISI 316L Stainless Steel Parts Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite (
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF.
                  </jats:p>

Normalized RGB imaging and transfer learning predict surface moisture at exposed earthen sites
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Repeated assessment of moisture content is essential for the preventive conservation of open-air earthen sites, yet conventional contact-based methods cannot readily provide dense spatial coverage. This study proposes a non-destructive method that predicts surface moisture content from chromatic features. A laboratory reference model was first developed using normalized RGB features (R_norm, G_norm, B_norm) that are insensitive to illuminance variation, and the model was then adapted to complex field lighting conditions through transfer learning. The transferred model yielded high prediction accuracy for the silty clay and silt tested in this study under conditions of low surface roughness (PEDI ≤0.3). Within the tested conditions, this workflow enables low-cost, non-contact assessment of surface moisture content and offers a practical tool for the field investigation and preventive conservation of open-air earthen sites.</jats:p>

title: The Effect of Instructional Videos On Students’ Learning Outcomes In Cell Biology In Grade XI at SMA Negeri 6 Pematangsiantar
journal: International Journal of Science, Technology & Management
abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to determine the effect of instructional videos on students’ learning outcomes in cell biology, particularly animal and plant cells, among Grade XI students at SMA Negeri 6 Pematangsiantar. The study employed a quantitative experimental approach using a pre-test and post-test control-group design. The sample consisted of 71 students: 35 students in class XI M3 as the experimental group, which learned with instructional videos, and 36 students in class XI M4 as the control group, which learned without instructional videos. Data were collected through learning-outcome tests and analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U test because the normality results indicated that the data were not normally distributed. The thesis reports that the experimental group’s mean score increased from 26.57% on the pre-test to 79.00% on the post-test. The control group increased from 25.42% to 49.47% in the results section. The Mann–Whitney test produced U = 118.500, Z = −6.017, and an asymptotic two-tailed significance value reported as 0.000 (p < 0.001). These findings indicate a statistically significant difference in learning outcomes between the two groups and support the use of instructional videos in teaching cell biology. The control-group post-test percentage requires confirmation because the thesis conclusion gives a different figure (48.47%).</jats:p>

title: A Hybrid System for Network Traffic Forecast Using Firefly and Cortical Learning Algorithm
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>Network traffic forecast is a critical aspect of network management and cybersecurity,
encompassing the prediction and analysis of data transmission patterns within computer
networks. As the volume and complexity of network traffic continue to increase exponentially,
accurate forecasting becomes indispensable for ensuring efficient resource allocation,
optimizing network performance, and detecting potential security threats. Object Oriented
Analysis and Design (OOAD) was adopted as the research methodology, and python was used
as the programming language. An experiment was conducted to detect malicious traffic on
network systems using a hybrid approach of firefly algorithm and cortical learning,
encompassing two phases: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and training of the Random
Forest Classifier. In the EDA phase, techniques were employed to address dataset imbalance
in the NSL-KDD dataset through random oversampling, alongside identifying the ten most
important features using Isolation Forest. During the model training phase, parameters were
initialized for both algorithms, leading to iterative optimization to achieve an optimal balance
between exploration and exploitation crucial for capturing complex network traffic patterns.
Evaluation of the model's outcomes, including training and testing results, was conducted
using classification reports and confusion matrices. The model showcased promising results,
achieving an accuracy of 99.9% in detecting malicious network traffic, and significantly
outperformed existing systems, demonstrating the efficacy of the hybrid approach in network
intrusion detection. This study underscores the effectiveness of the hybrid approach, offering
superior performance compared to traditional methods.</jats:p>
