The Impact of Early Changes in Albumin Levels on Long-Term Kidney and Mortality Outcomes in Patients With Acute Kidney Injury Undergoing Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate the association between early changes in the levels of serum albumin during continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) and long-term dialysis dependence and mortality in patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 days or more days after CKRT initiation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A multicenter retrospective cohort study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Setting:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Eight university-affiliated tertiary hospitals in South Korea participating in the LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium cohort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Patients:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study involved 1087 adult patients with acute kidney injury who survived for 90 or more days after CKRT initiation between January 2017 and June 2022.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Interventions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>None.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Measurements and Main Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Based on albumin levels at CKRT initiation and on day 7, patients were categorized into the persistent, resolved, new-onset, and no hypoalbuminemia groups. A composite of progression to end-stage kidney disease and all-cause mortality within 365 days was the primary outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 33.4% (363/1087) of the patients. The adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for the primary outcome was significantly higher in all groups when compared with the no hypoalbuminemia group (persistent: aOR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.73–4.04;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>
                      < 0.001; resolved: aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.38–3.75;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>
                      < 0.001; new-onset: aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.06–2.68;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">p</jats:italic>
                      = 0.028). No hypoalbuminemia group was associated with the most favorable prognosis, whereas persistent hypoalbuminemia was associated with the worst outcomes.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>During CKRT, early albumin level changes are associated with long-term kidney failure and mortality risk. Persistent hypoalbuminemia predicts the worst outcomes. Even in patients without baseline hypoalbuminemia, early decline in albumin is associated with worse prognosis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

Metformin Attenuates Cardiac Developmental Toxicity in High-Glucose-Exposed Zebrafish Larvae: Oxidative Stress, Hif-1α-Associated Metabolic Gene Alterations, and Wnt Signaling Changes
abstract: <jats:p>Background: Maternal hyperglycemia is associated with embryonic developmental abnormalities and congenital heart defects, yet the mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. We examined high-glucose-induced cardiac developmental injury in zebrafish and whether metformin co-administered with high glucose is associated with protection. Methods: Wild-type AB and Tg(myl7:EGFP) zebrafish (Danio rerio) embryos were exposed to control medium, high glucose (150 mM), or high glucose plus metformin (0.75, 3.0, or 6.0 mM); metformin alone was not tested. Hatching and survival rates, cardiac morphology and function, larval locomotor activity, oxidative-stress markers, and cardiac developmental and pathway transcripts/proteins were assessed. Results: Under high-glucose exposure conditions (150 mM), hatching and survival were reduced, cardiac morphology/function and locomotor activity were altered, hand2, gata4, tbx1, and tbx5 were downregulated, Gata4 was decreased, oxidative stress was increased, and Hif-1α expression and downstream metabolic targets were increased. Wnt-related readouts were heterogeneous: Gsk3β Ser9 phosphorylation, β-catenin and Daam1 decreased, whereas Dvl2 increased. Metformin was associated with improved survival, cardiac phenotypes, and locomotor outcomes, together with partial molecular restoration. As an osmolarity-matched control was not included, these phenotypes cannot be attributed exclusively to glucose-specific effects. Conclusions: High-glucose exposure conditions are associated with cardiac developmental injury and pathway dysregulation, and metformin shows protective associations. These findings are not causal, do not distinguish glucose-specific effects from hyperosmotic stress, and require osmolarity-matched controls, functional metabolic assays, and Hif-1α/Wnt perturbation studies.</jats:p>

title:
High‐Performance 2D MXene‐Derived TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Integrated Optical Polarizers
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, 2D materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond the laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). The 2D TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal/chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers that achieve high polarizer FOMs of up to ∼19.3 (a record among 2D‐material‐coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield (∼98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios of up to ∼12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong potential for large‐scale manufacturing, these devices represent a solid step toward industrial implementation of 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers.
                  </jats:p>

Optimizing Multilinear Polynomial Representations of Boolean Functions for Neural Network Synthesis
journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We consider the problem of obtaining a neural network (NN) representation of a Boolean network (BN), where each Boolean network (BN) vertex is a
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">k</jats:italic>
                    -input Boolean function (BF) (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">k≤ K</jats:italic>
                    ). A neural network (NN) representation can be constructed by mapping each Boolean function (BF) to its multilinear polynomial (MP) representation and then to a two-layer sub-NN; composing sub-NNs completes the representation. In this article, we show that structural properties (number of neurons/connections, neuron in-degree) of such a NN representation can be efficiently optimized while maintaining functional equivalence with the original BN (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">lossless</jats:italic>
                    optimization). Our approach establishes a correspondence between multilinear polynomials (MPs) and their two-layer-NN representation, enabling sub-NN optimization by minimizing MPs under structural criteria. To accelerate optimization, we utilize criterion invariance under Negation-Permutation-Negation (NPN) transformations. This allows us to classify BFs into equivalence classes, optimize canonical representatives, and then derive optimal representations for remaining class members via Negation-Permutation-Negation (NPN) transformations. Since optimizing sub-NNs may affect the composed NN depth, we propose an algorithm for lossless optimization under depth constraints. Experimentally, across four control-oriented and cryptographic digital circuits, we achieve reductions of up to 59% in neurons and 69% in connections relative to non-optimized NNs. Under minimum-depth constraints, reductions of up to 23% in neurons and 50% in connections are obtained. We demonstrate minimization of mean and maximum in-degree, and that intermediate-depth solutions recover most of the size reduction. Our NPN-based acceleration reduces MP optimization time by up to 10.2× compared to a baseline caching solutions per BF. Overall, the proposed methods facilitate high-throughput BN simulation and neurosymbolic matrix-vector-multiplication architectures.
                  </jats:p>

Optimal Power Flow for Sustainable Operation of Transmission Systems with High Renewable Penetration
abstract: <jats:p>The paper presents an integrated approach to Optimal Power Flow (OPF) in transmission systems with a high share of renewable energy sources (RESs) supported by energy storage systems (ESSs). Unlike conventional approaches, the proposed integrated evaluation framework minimizes operating cost subject to technical (network and ESS) constraints, while separately reporting RES utilization/curtailment and CO2 outcomes as post-solve indicators. The model was implemented as a browser-based JavaScript application using a custom Big-M Simplex linear programming solver and tested on a 24 h horizon under multiple scenarios representing conditions informed by Baltic/Latvian load, generation, and price profiles, applied to a modified IEEE 9-bus test network, including standard operation, high price volatility, high RES penetration, and a transmission line outage (N-1 criterion). The results demonstrate that ESS integration together with RES usage maximization reduces total operating costs by up to 10.2% compared to the baseline strategy without ESS and optimization (about 4.7 percentage points of this saving come from the lower minimum output of the conventional unit alone), increases RES share by about 5 percentage points, and decreases RES curtailment to 0%, under a terminal state of charge condition that prevents the ESS from ending the horizon more depleted than it started (imposed in HiGHS runs of the same linear program). Under high RES scenarios, ESSs become essential for balancing variability, while in volatile markets they support stable dispatching within the model. A sensitivity analysis highlights the dominant influence of market price fluctuations, with smaller effects of ESS capacity and RES share on total operating cost. The findings indicate that, within the transportation-type network model used, the proposed approach improves economic efficiency and environmental performance, offering a practical decision-support tool for transmission system operators and energy planners.</jats:p>

title: Low-dose curcumin inhibits ferroptosis in human periodontal ligament stem cells via ROCK1 downregulation
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Periodontitis is pathologically characterized by impaired function of human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs). Curcumin has attracted considerable attention due to its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; however, its effects on ferroptosis in hPDLSCs and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of curcumin in hPDLSC ferroptosis and its potential regulatory mechanisms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Following curcumin treatment at various concentrations, cell proliferation was assessed by CCK-8 assay, ROCK1 expression was detected by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) and Western blotting, ferrous iron (Fe
                      <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                      ) and glutathione (GSH) levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits, and mitochondrial membrane potential was evaluated by JC-1 staining.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Low-dose curcumin (0.001–0.01 μM) significantly promoted hPDLSC proliferation, reduced intracellular Fe
                      <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                      levels, elevated GSH content, suppressed the aberrant expression of ferroptosis-related proteins, and restored mitochondrial membrane potential. Notably, ROCK1 overexpression effectively reversed these protective effects, indicating that the action of curcumin is ROCK1-dependent. Furthermore, under Erastin-induced ferroptotic stress, low-dose curcumin reversed the Erastin-induced increases in Fe
                      <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                      , ACSL4, and lipid peroxidation, restored GSH, Ferritin, and GPX4 levels, and rescued hPDLSC proliferation, with effects comparable to those of Ferrostatin-1.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Low-dose curcumin exerts cytoprotective effects on hPDLSCs by simultaneously promoting proliferation and suppressing ferroptosis via downregulation of ROCK1 expression. These findings unveil a novel mechanism by which curcumin modulates hPDLSC fate, provide a theoretical basis for hPDLSC-based protective strategies in periodontitis therapy, and highlight ROCK1 as a potential molecular target for periodontal regenerative intervention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: The Influence of Students' Perceptions of the Method Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) Towards English Language Achievement With Motivation to Study as a Mediator in Junior High School X
journal: Enrichment: Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development
abstract: <jats:p>English language achievement is associated with instructional experiences and students’ learning motivation; however, the mediating role of motivation in the relationship between perceptions of Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) and academic achievement requires further investigation. This study examined the direct and indirect relationships between students’ perceptions of CLT and English language achievement, with learning motivation serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative, nonexperimental research design employing path analysis was conducted at a private junior high school in Pantai Indah Kapuk, Indonesia. The participants included 120 eighth-grade students, while an additional 30 students participated in instrument testing. Data were collected using a 40-item CLT perception questionnaire, a 30-item learning motivation questionnaire, and second-semester English report card grades. Content validity was evaluated using Aiken’s V coefficient, while internal consistency reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. Data were analyzed using JASP statistical software. The results revealed positive associations between students’ perceptions of CLT and learning motivation (? = 0.978) and between CLT perceptions and English language achievement (? = 0.550). Learning motivation was also positively associated with English language achievement (? = 0.407), with a statistically significant indirect association (? = 0.398), indicating partial mediation. These findings suggest that favorable perceptions of communicative language instruction are associated with improved English language achievement, partly through learning motivation. Nevertheless, the exceptionally strong association between CLT perceptions and motivation suggests potential construct overlap, warranting cautious interpretation. The findings highlight the importance of communicative instructional practices and motivational support, while further longitudinal research is recommended to establish temporal relationships and examine the generalizability of these findings across diverse educational settings.</jats:p>

title:
An N-Heterocyclic
Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate
1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.</jats:p>

title: Effect of nonsurgical periodontal therapy on the salivary levels of maresin as an inflammatory indicator in periodontitis patients with or without type 2 diabetes mellitus: A pilot clinical trial
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Aims and Objectives</jats:bold>
                    : To assess the impact of non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT) on maresin (MaR1) salivary levels in individuals with periodontitis, whether or not they had type 2 diabetes, both at baseline and one month after NSPT treatment.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Materials and Methods</jats:bold>
                    : In a study involving 27 patients, two groups were evaluated . Group A had periodontitis without diabetes, but Group B had periodontitis with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Clinical measurements and saliva samples were taken at baseline and one month after treatment. Both groups received non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT), which consisted of scaling and root planing with no additional treatments. Salivary maresin levels were assessed using the sandwich ELISA technique to evaluate changes over time.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Results</jats:bold>
                    : Significant differences (p < 0.001*) in salivary MaR1 levels were observed in both groups after NSPT. Salivary MaR1 levels were significantly different in Group B (periodontitis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus) compared to Group A (periodontitis patients) both at baseline and one month after NSPT (p < 0.001*). The levels of MaR1 in saliva showed a positive correlation with clinical parameters such as plaque index (PI), gingival bleeding index (GBI), probing pocket depth (PPD), and clinical attachment level (CAL).
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Conclusion</jats:bold>
                    : According to the most recent clinical experiment, there is an imbalance in the amounts of MaR1 in the saliva of healthy people as opposed to those who have diabetes mellitus and periodontitis. The study also showed fluctuations in salivary maresin levels following NSPT, offering new insights into resolving the inflammation associated with these conditions. This groundbreaking discovery of a salivary biomarker could be utilized in personalized periodontal therapy.
                  </jats:p>

title: When Social Cues Ease the Pain of Paying: The Role of Self-Construal in Online Shopping
journal: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research
abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the effects of social cues in online shopping environments on consumer purchases, investigates the underlying psychological mechanisms, and examines the role of consumers’ self-construal. To this end, we conducted one field study in an actual online shopping environment and two experimental studies. The field study revealed increases in actual product purchases and sales revenue following the introduction of a purchase-count social cue. Study 1 (n = 83) supported a sequential indirect effect whereby additional social cues were associated with reduced perceived uncertainty, lower pain of paying, and higher purchase intention. Study 2 (n = 146), which examined the role of temporarily activated self-construal, revealed that these effects were stronger in the interdependent self-construal condition than in the independent self-construal condition. This study provides field evidence of changes in actual purchase behavior following the introduction of social cues and identifies perceived uncertainty and the pain of paying as underlying psychological mechanisms, alongside the role of self-construal, thereby offering both theoretical and practical implications for research on online consumer behavior.</jats:p>

title: Vertex-based Curvilinear OPC via Bezier Curves
journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) is a critical step in semiconductor manufacturing, as it mitigates lithographic distortions and improves the pattern transfer fidelity from masks to silicon wafers. With the adoption of multi-beam mask writers, mask geometries are evolving from traditional Manhattan shapes to curvilinear patterns, offering improved resolution and process robustness. However, existing curvilinear OPC methods still suffer from limited optimization efficiency and accuracy, largely due to the difficulty of contour parameterization. To address this issue, we propose a gradient-based framework for vertex-based curvilinear OPC, where the mask is represented by connected Bézier curve segments controlled by trainable vertices, and the resulting rasterized mask is optimized to reduce lithographic errors. We evaluate the proposed method on the industry-standard dataset. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">
                      L
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    </jats:italic>
                    , PVBand, and VPE, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed gradient-based curvilinear optimization framework.

Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Solid-State Sintered SiC Brazed with a Novel Si-Ti-Al/Mo Composite Filler
abstract: <jats:p>In this study, to advance the research on near-homogeneous welding technology for silicon carbide ceramics required for service in nuclear environments and to meet the high-performance welding and reliable service requirements of silicon carbide ceramic fuel elements, a novel Si-Ti-Al/Mo composite filler was employed to achieve the joining of solid-state sintered silicon carbide (SiC) via vacuum brazing, thereby providing an innovative technical solution for the integration of high-performance SiC components. The research systematically elucidated the interfacial metallurgical mechanism governed by this novel alloy, and comprehensively investigated the effects of brazing temperature on joint microstructure, room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical properties, as well as fracture morphology. In the filler metal design, the pre-added Mo served as a heterogeneous nucleating agent, preferentially reacting with Si, which effectively suppressed the extensive formation of the TiSi2 phase. Concurrently, the introduction of Mo significantly refined the grain structure within the joint region. Brazing at 1360 °C yielded a peak room-temperature shear strength of 144 MPa. Moreover, the joints exhibited excellent high-temperature service reliability, retaining a shear strength of 64 MPa at a test temperature of 1000 °C. This novel joining technology is expected to promote the widespread engineering application of high-performance SiC components in extremely harsh environments.</jats:p>

title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Nearby radio galaxies are among the most promising candidates for the acceleration of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). In this work, we develop a physically motivated, source-resolved framework to quantify the contribution of the three nearest Fanaroff–Riley Class I (FR-I) radio galaxies – Centaurus A, Virgo A, and Fornax A – to the UHECR flux measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory. Acceleration spectra derived from detailed jet-acceleration models are combined with numerical simulations of extragalactic propagation, while the more distant radio-galaxy population is treated as a continuous background. By fitting our simulation exclusively to the measured UHECR energy spectrum, we determine the relative contribution of each source and constrain the fraction of jet power converted into UHECR luminosity. We find that a small number of nearby radio galaxies can account for the highest-energy UHECR flux with acceleration efficiencies of order

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Organic semiconductors are key materials for high‐performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality‐induced crystallization and a subsequent COF‐to‐COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole‐linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N‐over‐N and S‐over‐S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10

Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tafolecimab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). Diarrhea is a recognized adverse reaction, but detailed post-marketing case descriptions with clear timing, differential assessment, and outcome remain limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Case Summary</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 51-year-old man hospitalized for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction received his first one-time 600-mg subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab (SINTBILO) at 15:14 on 13 July 2026. Approximately 7 h 46 min later, he developed abdominal pain and diarrhea occurring 5–8 times daily, with nausea and mild periumbilical pain but no fever, tenesmus, visible hematochezia or melena, dehydration, hypotension, rebound tenderness, or guarding. Stool testing showed loose yellow stool, positive occult blood and red blood cells, 0–1 white blood cells/high-power field, and a negative rotavirus test; electrolytes and liver and kidney function were normal. Stool culture and testing for Clostridioides difficile, norovirus, and adenovirus were not performed. Tafolecimab was not re-administered. After fluid replacement, montmorillonite, and loperamide hydrochloride, diarrhea decreased within 1 day and resolved after approximately 2 days, with no recurrence after discharge. Long-term stable acarbose therapy was continued without recurrence. The Naranjo score was 5, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case supports probable tafolecimab-associated acute diarrhea. New-onset diarrhea after PCSK9 inhibitor initiation should prompt precise temporal documentation, medication reconciliation, targeted microbiological evaluation, and pharmacovigilance reporting.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Forecasting High Electricity Demand Using Explainable Machine Learning
journal: Balkan Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The objective of this study was to predict the onset of high demand, the highest half-hourly average power, and the total duration of high demand over the next two hours using historical electricity consumption data from residential households. Half-hourly measurements from 2013 for 200 standard-tariff residential households selected from the Low Carbon London dataset were used. High demand was defined as exceeding the 90th percentile of each household’s average power values during the January–February period. The models were developed using data from 160 households; transfer performance was evaluated on the 40 households not included in model training. The process was divided into a training period (March–June), model selection in July, calibration of prediction intervals in August, and a testing period (September–December). The selected models were retrained using March–July data. Separate models were built for the three targets; Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB), XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared against a weekly seasonal reference. Model selection was initially based on average precision (AP) for the target and mean absolute error (MAE) for power and duration. For the residential units used in the training, the HistGB model selected during the testing period produced an AP of 0.4183; the CatBoost models produced an MAE of 0.2704 kW for power and 9.2361 minutes for duration. The contributions of historical consumption and calendar features to the model predictions were examined using the SHAP method. In the early warning evaluation, 78.81% of relevant events in known residential units were detected in advance; 60.93% of early warnings were identified as false alarms. The improvement in duration prediction relative to a reference that yields a duration of zero in every window remained limited. The findings indicate that the approach could contribute to monitoring residential demand; however, the burden of false alarms and the limited success in duration prediction must be taken into account from a practical standpoint.</jats:p>

Low accuracy and interobserver/intraobserver agreement for colorectal sessile serrated lesions: A multicenter diagnostic study
abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The accurate diagnosis of sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) and SSLs with dysplasia (SSL-D) is vital for preventing the occurrence of colorectal cancer but remains challenging because of inconsistent classification criteria.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To evaluate the diagnostic consistency for colorectal SSL and SSL-D among pathologists with different levels of experience in a multicenter setting.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Six gastrointestinal pathologists (stratified by experience) independently reviewed digitized whole-slide images of 1176 colorectal polyps across three rounds using the 2019 World Health Organization criteria. The accuracy and interobserver/intraobserver agreement were assessed. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors influencing SSL/SSL-D concordance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Overall diagnostic accuracy increased from 66% to 72% with clinical information (P  < 0.001), but accuracy for SSL (62%) and SSL-D (33%) remained suboptimal. Interobserver agreement was moderate for SSL (κ  = 0.301-0.441), whereas the highest agreement was observed for traditional serrated adenoma (κ  = 0.703). Senior pathologists outperformed junior pathologists in terms of the overall (accuracy: 76% vs  56%, P  < 0.001; κ : 0.517 vs  0.337) and SSL classification (69% vs  60%, P  < 0.001; κ : 0.601 vs  0.524). SSL-D showed the poorest performance regardless of experience (accuracy: 11%-21%; interobserver κ : 0.084-0.149). Multivariate analysis identified nuclear alteration [odds ratio (OR) = 10.45)] and cross-sectional crypt orientation (OR = 5.27) as risk factors for discordance, whereas > 3 serrated crypts (OR = 0.37) and serration extending to the crypt base (OR = 0.20) exhibited protective effects.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Suboptimal performance and high diagnostic variability highlight the morphological complexity of SSL/SSL-D classification. Standardized training and quantitative crypt-based criteria may improve diagnosis.</jats:p>

Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
abstract: <jats:p>Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Background: The longitudinal risk of asthma among children with developmental disabilities (DDs) remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between DD and subsequent asthma risk. Methods: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database from 2009 through 2019. Children younger than 18 years with a claims-based DD diagnosis were propensity-score-matched 1:1 with children without DD. Children with asthma before the index date were excluded. Incident recorded asthma was defined using ICD-9-CM code 493.- or ICD-10-CM code J45.-; ICD-10-CM J44.- was excluded. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs). Prespecified subtype analyses addressed DD heterogeneity. Results: The study included 213,759 children in each cohort. The DD cohort had 43,782 recorded asthma diagnoses during 1,503,077 person-years (29.13 per 1000 person-years), compared with 30,559 diagnoses during 1,620,645 person-years among controls (18.86 per 1000 person-years). DD was associated with a higher rate of subsequent recorded asthma diagnosis (aHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.67–1.72), with associations present in both sexes and all age strata. Subtype-specific aHRs ranged from 1.65 for developmental delay or speech and language disorders to 1.94 for autism spectrum disorder. Exploratory post-index therapy and medication estimates were not interpreted as causal treatment effects. Conclusions: In this administrative claims cohort, a pre-existing DD diagnosis was associated with an approximately 70% higher adjusted rate of a subsequent recorded asthma diagnosis. The finding may support careful respiratory assessment when symptoms occur. Prospective studies incorporating healthcare-utilization measures, standardized asthma confirmation, and objective pulmonary testing are needed.</jats:p>

title: Acute diarrhea following the first subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab: a case report of a probable adverse drug reaction
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tafolecimab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). Diarrhea is a recognized adverse reaction, but detailed post-marketing case descriptions with clear timing, differential assessment, and outcome remain limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Case Summary</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 51-year-old man hospitalized for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction received his first one-time 600-mg subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab (SINTBILO) at 15:14 on 13 July 2026. Approximately 7 h 46 min later, he developed abdominal pain and diarrhea occurring 5–8 times daily, with nausea and mild periumbilical pain but no fever, tenesmus, visible hematochezia or melena, dehydration, hypotension, rebound tenderness, or guarding. Stool testing showed loose yellow stool, positive occult blood and red blood cells, 0–1 white blood cells/high-power field, and a negative rotavirus test; electrolytes and liver and kidney function were normal. Stool culture and testing for Clostridioides difficile, norovirus, and adenovirus were not performed. Tafolecimab was not re-administered. After fluid replacement, montmorillonite, and loperamide hydrochloride, diarrhea decreased within 1 day and resolved after approximately 2 days, with no recurrence after discharge. Long-term stable acarbose therapy was continued without recurrence. The Naranjo score was 5, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case supports probable tafolecimab-associated acute diarrhea. New-onset diarrhea after PCSK9 inhibitor initiation should prompt precise temporal documentation, medication reconciliation, targeted microbiological evaluation, and pharmacovigilance reporting.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Three-Year Polymerase Chain Reaction-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Tract Infections in Adults and Seasonal Patterns
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Objective: This study investigated the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of adult respiratory tract infections in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023–2025. Methods: A total of 8,493 adults (≥18 years) with respiratory symptoms were enrolled from a tertiary hospital during 2023–2025. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression. Results: The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter–spring (December–March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78–3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89–3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24–2.01) were independent risk factors. Conclusion: Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter–spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance – with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter–spring months – and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.</jats:p>

Identification
and
Reaction Analysis of Antibiotic
Transformation Products in an Urban River via Suspect and Nontarget
Screening with a Self-Curated Library
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Antibiotics enter urban river basins mainly through sewage effluent. They undergo transformation during treatment and in river systems, generating transformation products (TPs) that may still have ecological effects. Yet, identifying these TPs by high-resolution mass spectrometry is hindered by the scarcity of reference standards and comprehensive MS/MS spectral libraries. To overcome this, we constructed a dedicated MS/MS library containing over 6,500 MS/MS spectra for 244 parent antibiotics and 362 TPs, thereby enabling rapid suspect screening through spectral matching. For novel TPs beyond library coverage, we integrated diagnostic fragment searching and seed-driven molecular networking to propagate annotations to structurally related unknowns. Applying this workflow to water, sediment, and effluent samples from an urban river system in Beijing, we identified 39 parent antibiotics and 158 TPs, of which 20 TPs are not previously documented in environmental samples. The major transformation reactions were cleavage, dealkylation, and hydrolysis, alongside compound-specific pathways like hemiacetal formation for erythromycin. These reactions differentially affect the environmental properties of antibiotics, and some reactions (e.g., dehydrogenation and dehydration) showed potential to enhance ecotoxicity. These results confirm that transformation substantially diversifies antibiotic signatures in urban aquatic environments and underscore the necessity of including TPs in environmental monitoring and risk assessment.</jats:p>

title: Which Definition Is the Gold Standard? Reference-Standard Choice and the Reported Accuracy of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Diagnostic Tests: A Meta-Epidemiological Systematic Review
abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) has no gold standard. Accuracy studies borrow one of several composite definitions instead, and these definitions do not label the same patients as infected. We asked how often accuracy studies say which definition they used, and how far the choice moves the numbers they report. Methods: In this systematic review, we searched PubMed on 20 October 2026 for primary accuracy studies of PJI tests and classified each abstract by the reference definition it named. Studies that applied two or more definitions (MSIS 2011/2013, ICM 2018, IDSA 2013, EBJIS proposed or 2021) to the same cohort were assessed further, and accuracy was extracted per definition. Ratios of PJI cases and the change in sensitivity of the alpha-defensin test were pooled with random-effects models. Results: Of 1744 accuracy studies, 437 (25%) named a reference definition in the abstract. The share rose from none before 2012 to 35% from 2021 onward. Seventeen studies reported accuracy under more than one definition in the same patients. EBJIS classified 1.47 times as many patients as infected as MSIS (95% CI 1.33–1.62; 6 cohorts; I2 = 4%) and 1.26 times as many as ICM 2018 (1.08–1.46; 6 cohorts; I2 = 58%). The pooled sensitivity of the alpha-defensin test was 85.6% (76.9–91.4) against MSIS and 56.3% (48.6–63.7) against EBJIS in the same three cohorts, while specificity stayed between 89% and 100%. Across 13 test–cohort pairs, the median change in sensitivity when the reference moved to EBJIS was −18.5 percentage points (IQR −29.0 to −4.9); sensitivity fell in 10 pairs and changed by less than 3 points in three. Conclusions: For several PJI tests, the reported sensitivity depends substantially on the reference definition chosen. A definition that labels more patients as infected is not, for that reason, a more accurate one. Accuracy figures obtained under different definitions should not be pooled or compared as if they measured the same thing, and every accuracy study should name its reference definition in the abstract.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>У статті досліджується реакція політичних сил єврейської, польської та російської меншин України на Закон про національно-персональну автономію протягом 1917–1919 рр. Особливу увагу приділено тому, що саме ці три спільноти отримали право на автономію автоматично на відміну від менш чисельних етнічних груп. Методологічну основу дослідження становить історико-порівняльний аналіз, поєднаний із проблемно-хронологічним підходом та критичним опрацюванням архівних документів, опублікованих джерел і наукової літератури. Наукова новизна роботи полягає у комплексному порівняльному дослідженні ставлення трьох основних національних меншин до Закону та його практичної реалізації у різні періоди української державності: добу УЦР, Гетьманату та Директорії. З’ясовано, що єврейські політичні сили виявили найбільш послідовну підтримку національно-персональної автономії та максимально використали її можливості. Польські організації загалом підтримали Закон, однак їхня позиція залишалася стриманою через земельне питання та міждержавний контекст. Російські політичні сили поставилися до Закону пасивно і майже не реалізували надані права. Доля Закону у 1918–1919 рр. відобразила зміни політичного курсу українських урядів та різний рівень готовності меншин до національного самоврядування в рамках української державності</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthcare contributes 4.4%–5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) requires repeated diagnostic investigations throughout a patient's lifetime, adding to healthcare's environmental footprint. However, the carbon footprint and cost of IBD diagnostic modalities have not been systematically compared</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Aims</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To quantify per‐procedure emissions and relative costs of IBD diagnostics and model potential savings from intestinal ultrasound (IUS) when clinically appropriate.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This prospective observational study quantified operational emissions at AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad, India, during December 2025 using the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, institutional data, and a three‐state power model. Procedures included laboratory tests (27,330), colonoscopy/enteroscopy (1290), CT (1520), MRI (589), and IUS (923). Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of emission estimates by varying assumptions regarding infrastructure allocation, equipment power consumption, procedure volumes, and electricity grid emission factors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Emissions ranged from 0.462 kg CO
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      e per laboratory test to 21.25 kg CO
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      e per MRI. IUS (0.850 kg CO
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      e) was the lowest‐carbon imaging modality, with 4.6‐, 6.8‐, and 25.0‐fold lower emissions than colonoscopy/enteroscopy, CT, and MRI, respectively. Cross‐sectional imaging contributed 53.7% of total emissions (39,778 kg CO
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      e), versus 2.0% for IUS. Costs increased with emissions. When clinically appropriate, substituting IUS for colonoscopy or MR enterography could reduce per‐procedure emissions by 78.0% and 96.0%, respectively.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Carbon emissions and cost rise together across IBD diagnostics; when clinically appropriate, IUS is the lowest‐carbon, lowest‐cost imaging modality. Patient‐level studies are needed to confirm modelled savings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Circulating miR-10b-5p drives Kawasaki vasculitis via endothelial reprogramming and nominates CXCL8 as an early diagnostic biomarker
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis and the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, yet no specific biomarker enables early diagnosis at emergency department presentation. We aimed to define the molecular mechanisms driving KD vasculitis and to identify a clinically actionable early diagnostic marker. Whole microRNA sequencing of buffy coat specimens from patients with KD and febrile controls identified 68 upregulated microRNAs, of which 13 were prioritized. Candidates were validated in two KD-like vasculitis mouse models, and miR-10b-5p was consistently elevated. Inhibition of miR-10b-5p by a miRCURY locked nucleic acid inhibitor attenuated aortic root inflammation in vivo. In human coronary artery endothelial cells from adult donors, miR-10b-5p directly suppressed marker of proliferation Ki-67 (
                    <jats:italic>MKI67</jats:italic>
                    ) and chromobox 5 (
                    <jats:italic>CBX5</jats:italic>
                    ), driving a transition from proliferative and metabolic programs toward a proinflammatory phenotype, as confirmed by single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing. Chromatin accessibility profiling revealed increased accessibility at the C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (
                    <jats:italic>CXCL8</jats:italic>
                    ) promoter, and motif analysis identified CCAAT enhancer binding protein alpha (
                    <jats:italic>CEBPA</jats:italic>
                    ) as the key transcriptional activator;
                    <jats:italic>CEBPA</jats:italic>
                    knockdown abrogated miR-10b-5p-induced
                    <jats:italic>CXCL8</jats:italic>
                    upregulation, and direct binding was confirmed by binding assays and chromatin immunoprecipitation. Serum CXCL8 was markedly elevated in patients with KD relative to febrile controls at first presentation before definitive diagnosis and declined significantly at the 8-week follow-up. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated diagnostic utility, with sensitivity and specificity of 83.3% at an optimal cut-off of 20.91 pg/ml. In conclusion, we define a miR-10b-5p–
                    <jats:italic>MKI67</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>CBX5</jats:italic>
                    –CEBPA–CXCL8 axis driving endothelial reprogramming and neutrophil-recruiting inflammation in KD and identify serum CXCL8 as a candidate biomarker for timely KD recognition.
                  </jats:p>

Effect of Implant Surface and Radiation Dose on Crestal Bone Loss in Irradiated Patients: 1-Year Preliminary Outcomes
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Implant-supported prosthetic rehabilitation is frequently required in head and neck cancer patients but carries an elevated risk of impaired osseointegration and peri-implant bone loss. Hydrophilic implant surfaces have demonstrated improved early osseointegration in preclinical studies. However, clinical evidence, especially in irradiated patients, remains limited. This study aimed to compare short-term clinical and radiologic outcomes of hydrophilic implants versus conventional implants placed in irradiated bone.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, 107 implants (conventional surface: n=53; hydrophilic surface: n=54) were placed in 21 irradiated patients with head and neck cancer using a split-mouth design. Panoramic radiographs were obtained at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months, and mesial and distal crestal bone loss was assessed. Further, effects of implant surface and implant-specific radiation dose were evaluated.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      At 12 months, hydrophilic implants demonstrated significantly reduced crestal bone loss compared with conventional implants both mesially (0.6±0.7 versus 0.9±0.7 mm;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                      <0.001) and distally (0.5±0.4 versus 0.9±0.6 mm;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                      <0.001). Implant location and radiation-dose category did not show statistically significant associations with bone loss over time.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Hydrophilic implant surfaces were associated with reduced early crestal bone loss in irradiated patients, while radiation dose exhibited no measurable impact within the first year. This study is the first to demonstrate a potential benefit of hydrophilic implants in irradiated patients, including those with autologous bone grafts. Hydrophilic implants may represent a promising option for implant rehabilitation in this high-risk patient population.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Plasmablastic lymphoma of maxillary gingiva: A diagnostic conundrum
abstract: <jats:p>Plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL) is very rare aggressive variant of B-cell lymphoma, characterized by plasmablastic morphology associated with immunodeficiency. It has strong and common association with HIV and EBV positive individuals. Subsequently, the spectrum of the disease has widened to include extraoral and nodal sites, as well as cases without mucosal involvement, EBV infection, or HIV association, leading to atypical presentations. These variations pose significant diagnostic challenges, particularly in differentiating PBL from other hematolymphoid malignancies with plasmablastic features, such as ALK1-positive large B-cell lymphoma, HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma not otherwise specified (NOS), and the solid variant of primary effusion lymphoma, as well as from plasmablastic plasma cell myeloma. Additionally, poorly differentiated carcinoma and amelanotic melanoma should be excluded during differential diagnosis. This article presents a rare case of PBL involving the maxillary gingiva and discusses its histogenesis, key differential diagnoses, and the critical role of clinical evaluation, histopathological features, and immunohistochemical profiling in establishing an accurate diagnosis.</jats:p>

Osteoarticular Infection in Immunocompromised Children and Neonates: A Retrospective Case Series Emphasising Diagnostic Challenges and Multimodal Management
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Osteoarticular infections (OAIs) in neonates and immunocompromised children present distinct diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Atypical clinical presentations, attenuated inflammatory responses, and a broader spectrum of pathogens complicate early recognition and management. This study characterizes the clinical presentation, microbiology, management, and outcomes of OAIs in this highly vulnerable population.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a retrospective case series of patients younger than 16 years with osteomyelitis and/or septic arthritis managed at a tertiary pediatric center between February 2017 and February 2024. The cohort comprised neonates and children with primary or secondary immunodeficiency. Clinical presentation, inflammatory markers, microbiology, antimicrobial and surgical treatment, immune-directed therapy, and outcomes were analyzed descriptively. Ethical approval was obtained from the SingHealth Centralized Institutional Review Board (CIRB Ref: 2023-2559).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Eighteen patients were included; 6 (33.3%) were neonates. All patients had reduced active limb mobility, and 14 (77.8%) had localized swelling. Twelve patients (66.7%) had fever, whereas 6 (33.3%), predominantly neonates, remained afebrile. CRP was elevated in all patients despite variable white blood cell responses.
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">Staphylococcus aureus</jats:italic>
                      was the most frequently identified pathogen [6/18 (33.3%)]; other organisms included
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">S</jats:italic>
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">treptococci, Mycobacteria, Candida tropicalis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and Bacillus</jats:italic>
                      spp. Fifteen patients (83.3%) underwent surgical intervention, and 6 (33.3%) received immune-directed therapy. At last follow-up, 14 patients (77.8%) had complete resolution, 2 died from causes unrelated to the OAI, 1 was lost to follow-up, and 1 had persistent or recurrent infection. Two patients developed chronic musculoskeletal sequelae.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>OIAs in this heterogeneous cohort were frequently accompanied by attenuated systemic features and diverse microbiology. Fever and leucocytosis were not invariably present, whereas CRP was elevated in all cases and provided supplementary information alongside clinical assessment. Favorable outcomes were observed in the context of multidisciplinary, multimodal management, but the retrospective design, small sample, and population heterogeneity preclude causal or subgroup-specific conclusions. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Level of Evidence:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Level IV—retrospective case series.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

Cerebral perfusion SPECT in the diagnostic framework of degenerative dementias: still useful after all these years
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Introduction: The clinical distinction between the different types of dementia is a clinical challenge and establishing an accurate diagnosis is essential for guiding treatment. We aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of cerebral perfusion SPECT in the diagnostic framework of dementias. Methods: We included patients with cognitive disorders who underwent a cerebral SPECT between 2013-2019. Medical data for all participants were collected, and clinical diagnosis were established independently of the SPECT findings. All SPECT images were blindly analysed, by describing the topographical patterns of hypoperfusion. Results: We included 51 patients: typical Alzheimer’s disease (AD; n=24), behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD, n=15), primary progressive aphasia (PPA, n=6), and atypical AD (logopenic aphasia and behavioral/dysexecutive variant AD, n=6). SPECT achieved 72% and 66% for distinguishing typical AD from bvFTD and AD (typical and atypical cases) from FTD (PPA and bvFTD), respectively. Compared to bvFTD, hypoperfusion in inferior parietal (p &lt; 0.002), in the superior parietal (p &lt; 0.01) and in the lateral temporal (p &lt; 0.018) regions were more frequent in the typical AD group. Considering all AD cases (typical and atypical presentations) and FTD (PPA and bvFTD), hypoperfusion in the anterior temporal (p &lt; 0.03) and in basal ganglia (p &lt; 0.026) were more frequent in the FTD group. On the contrary, hypoperfusion in inferior parietal (p &lt; 0.0001), in the superior parietal (p &lt; 0.004) and in the lateral temporal (p &lt; 0.03) cortex were more common in AD than in FTD patients. Conclusion: The diagnostic value of a SPECT for differentiating dementias is limited, but specific topographical patterns of hypoperfusion may be useful for distinguishing AD from bvFTD.  </jats:p>

Spatiotemporal Assessment of Optimized Solar Radiation for Photovoltaic Applications Across Nigeria: Optimal Tilt Angles, Long-Term Trends, Change Points, and Associations with Climatic Variables
abstract: <jats:p>Accurate characterization of solar energy is crucial for PV implementation; however, existing studies in Nigeria have focused on horizontal radiation, site selection, or optimal tilt angle, but not on the combined effects of trends, structural changes, and meteorological factors. This work bridges this gap by conducting a comprehensive spatiotemporal analysis of optimized solar radiation across all 37 administrative regions of Nigeria using NASA POWER data from 1984 to 2025. Thus, this study aims to mathematically determine the optimal tilt angle that achieves the best total solar radiation in different regions of Nigeria. Furthermore, the temporal trends of the maximum total radiation at the optimal angle were analyzed using linear regression and Mann–Kendall tests. The Pettitt, Buishand, and Standard Normal Homogeneity Tests and Segmented Regression were used to detect structural changes, while Spearman’s correlation was used to measure association with meteorological and atmospheric factors. Optimal tilt angles per year were relatively high in northern states of Nigeria, with values of 15.3° in Sokoto and 14.7° in Yobe, while southern states had values of about 9–10°. Optimum annual radiation was highest in Yobe and Sokoto (22.9 MJ m−2 day−1), as against 17 MJ m−2 day−1 in Rivers and Bayelsa. Trends in annual radiation declined in all 37 regions, significantly declining in 33 (89.2%) regions. Change point analysis yielded a total of 29 regions (78.4%), mostly occurring within the 2003–2004 period. The results demonstrate that the amount of cloud cover was the main factor with a negative correlation to solar radiation, while wind variables showed a strong positive correlation. Furthermore, circular-linear regression showed statistically significant regional correlations between wind direction and solar radiation. The current findings have important implications for urban planning and city planning in Nigeria, as data on the availability and variability of solar energy resources, precisely defined in terms of geographical location, can be used in designing and determining the sizes of rooftop solar power plants, as well as in integrating renewable energy sources within urban areas, which is a key pillar for the sustainability of cities. Moreover, these results could also form the basis for incorporating solar energy resource trends into urban energy plans in Nigeria, particularly with regard to cities experiencing rapid growth and increasing energy demand. The novelty of this study is a comprehensive framework that unites the orientation of PV, the quantity of resources, temporal variations, regime shifts, and atmospheric variables in Nigeria.</jats:p>

title: Genetic background of heat tolerance in maternal pig lines based on reaction norm models for reproductive performance traits
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding the genetic background of heat tolerance in maternal pig lines is important since reproductive performance is directly affected by increased thermal load. In this context, the main objective of this study was to evaluate how alternative environmental gradients (EGs) and critical periods affect genetic parameter estimates, environmental sensitivity, genomic estimated breeding values, and animal ranking for heat tolerance based on reproductive traits and reaction norm models. Records from 24,970 Landrace (LR) and 30,754 Large White (LW) animals were analyzed, including 17,141 and 27,419 genotyped individuals, respectively. Traits evaluated included number of piglets born alive (NBA), stillborn (SB) and mummified (NM) piglets, litter birth weight (LBW), average piglet birth weight (APBW), number of piglets weaned (NW), and litter weaning weight (LWW). Eight environmental gradients were evaluated (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_DEW, THI_MEAN, THI_MAX, THI_P95, DH, and HrsAbove) over 7-, 15-, and 30-day periods before trait measurement. Heritability estimates ranged from 0.02 (NM) to 0.50 (APBW) in LR and 0.02 (NW) to 0.36 (APBW) in LW. Slope additive genetic variance ratios (indicator of environmental sensitivity) ranged from 0.003 (NW) to 0.078 (LBW). Genetic correlations between intercept and slope varied in magnitude and direction across traits and breeds such as negative for LWW (-0.25) in LR and APBW (-0.18) in LW, indicating greater environmental sensitivity among animals with higher genetic merit for these two traits, and positive for LBW and NW in LR and for NW (0.67), LBW (0.46), and LWW (0.16) in LW. Genetic correlations across EG levels were high for most traits (0.88-0.99 in LR; 0.80-0.99 in LW), but lower minimum values for LBW (0.41) and NW (0.46) in LR and LBW (0.38) and LWW (0.11) in LW indicated greater genotype-by-environment interaction (G×E). G×E was also reflected in re-ranking: between low and high EG levels, the overlap among top-ranked animals decreased from 78% to 54% for NW in LR, and from 71% to 39% for LBW and from 74% to 27% for LWW in LW. The choice of EG influenced most analyses, and the strongest G×E effects were captured by DH-based gradients, with additional evidence for THI and T2M_DEW, especially for 7- and 15-day periods. These results indicate that thermal gradients should be incorporated into genetic evaluations to identify animals with greater robustness or adaptation to thermal load, especially for LBW, NW, and LWW.</jats:p>

title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Posture-Adjustable Cable-Based Clamping–Cutting End-Effector for Safflower Filaments
abstract: <jats:p>Safflower filaments grow in random directions, whereas rigid-cutter picking end-effectors have large front ends and a fixed approach posture. To address these problems, a posture-adjustable cable-based clamping–cutting end-effector for safflower filaments was designed. Carried by a Delta parallel robot, it uses a two-axis deflection platform to align its axis with the flower growth direction and replaces rigid jaws and blades with twisted cable clamping and staggered twin-wire cutting. Twisted-string clamping and cutting-stroke models were established to determine the parameters of the guide orifice and the clamping and cutting mechanisms, and an end-effector–flower axis-angle test and a field picking test were conducted. The projected front-end area was 69.1% smaller than that of the previous-generation rigid-blade picking head. In single-attempt picking of 136 safflowers in the field, the complete clamping rate was 95.6%, the cutting success rate after complete clamping was 99.2%, and the clamping–cutting success rate was 94.9%. With the axes aligned (0–10°), the mass picking rate was 90.39%, within the range of values in the literature for rigid-blade end-effectors; at 30–40°, it decreased to 62.07%. The cable-based end-effector reliably clamps and cuts filaments with a small front end, and the end-effector–flower axis angle significantly affects the mass picking rate. These results provide a reference for the development of selective safflower picking equipment.</jats:p>

title: Comparative Metabolic, Antioxidant, and Histopathological Effects of Agrimonia pilosa, Calendula arvensis, and Polygonum hydropiper Extracts in Streptozotocin-Induced Diabetic Mice
abstract: <jats:p>Background: Oxidative stress, dyslipidemia, weight loss, and tissue injury accompany sustained hyperglycemia and provide complementary endpoints for evaluating botanical interventions. This study compared hydroalcoholic extracts of Agrimonia pilosa, Calendula arvensis, and Polygonum hydropiper with Vaccinium myrtillus as a positive botanical control in a mouse model of streptozotocin-induced diabetes. Methods: Thirty male CD1 mice aged 4–6 weeks were studied in six groups of five animals. Diabetes was induced by a single intraperitoneal administration of streptozotocin at 180 mg/kg body weight. Fasting blood glucose was measured before streptozotocin administration, 72 h and one week after injection. Animals showing fasting blood glucose concentrations >300 mg/dL, confirmed by repeated measurement, were considered diabetic and included in the chronic treatment experiment. Following confirmation of diabetes, hydroalcoholic tinctures were administered orally once daily for 35 days at the previously selected doses: A. pilosa 200 mg/kg, C. arvensis 150 mg/kg, P. hydropiper 100 mg/kg, and V. myrtillus 100 mg/kg as an active botanical comparator. Glycemia and body mass were followed longitudinally; food and water intake were recorded weekly. Whole-blood lipids, malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GPx), albumin, and creatinine were assessed, together with histopathology. Animal-level between-group comparisons used two-sided Welch independent-samples t-tests; glycemic treatment-versus-untreated-STZ comparisons were Bonferroni-adjusted. Food and water intake were summarized descriptively because they were recorded at cage level. Results: At day 35, mean glycemia was 358.60 mg/dL in untreated diabetic mice and 122.00, 177.20, 252.20, and 174.80 mg/dL after A. pilosa, P. hydropiper, C. arvensis, and V. myrtillus, respectively. A. pilosa had the lowest glucose mean among survivors, but two animals died, leaving n = 3 at days 28 and 35 and a potential for survivor bias. P. hydropiper showed higher SOD and GPx activities in exploratory pairwise analyses, whereas C. arvensis had the lowest day-35 triglyceride mean. Histopathology revealed hepatic alterations in several treatment groups and myocardial interfascicular edema in P. hydropiper and V. myrtillus; these findings were descriptive and were not used for between-group severity ranking. Conclusions: The extracts showed distinct exploratory activity profiles. P. hydropiper was associated with a numerical glycemic reduction and higher SOD and GPx activities in exploratory pairwise analyses, whereas C. arvensis produced the lowest day-35 triglyceride concentration. A. pilosa showed the largest numerical reduction in glycemia among the surviving animals; however, mortality observed in the A. pilosa group during treatment and the resulting final sample of three animals precluded firm conclusions regarding comparative efficacy.</jats:p>

title:
High‐Performance 2D MXene‐Derived TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Integrated Optical Polarizers
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, 2D materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond the laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). The 2D TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal/chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers that achieve high polarizer FOMs of up to ∼19.3 (a record among 2D‐material‐coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield (∼98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios of up to ∼12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong potential for large‐scale manufacturing, these devices represent a solid step toward industrial implementation of 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers.
                  </jats:p>

title: Optimizing Multilinear Polynomial Representations of Boolean Functions for Neural Network Synthesis
journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We consider the problem of obtaining a neural network (NN) representation of a Boolean network (BN), where each Boolean network (BN) vertex is a
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">k</jats:italic>
                    -input Boolean function (BF) (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">k≤ K</jats:italic>
                    ). A neural network (NN) representation can be constructed by mapping each Boolean function (BF) to its multilinear polynomial (MP) representation and then to a two-layer sub-NN; composing sub-NNs completes the representation. In this article, we show that structural properties (number of neurons/connections, neuron in-degree) of such a NN representation can be efficiently optimized while maintaining functional equivalence with the original BN (
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">lossless</jats:italic>
                    optimization). Our approach establishes a correspondence between multilinear polynomials (MPs) and their two-layer-NN representation, enabling sub-NN optimization by minimizing MPs under structural criteria. To accelerate optimization, we utilize criterion invariance under Negation-Permutation-Negation (NPN) transformations. This allows us to classify BFs into equivalence classes, optimize canonical representatives, and then derive optimal representations for remaining class members via Negation-Permutation-Negation (NPN) transformations. Since optimizing sub-NNs may affect the composed NN depth, we propose an algorithm for lossless optimization under depth constraints. Experimentally, across four control-oriented and cryptographic digital circuits, we achieve reductions of up to 59% in neurons and 69% in connections relative to non-optimized NNs. Under minimum-depth constraints, reductions of up to 23% in neurons and 50% in connections are obtained. We demonstrate minimization of mean and maximum in-degree, and that intermediate-depth solutions recover most of the size reduction. Our NPN-based acceleration reduces MP optimization time by up to 10.2× compared to a baseline caching solutions per BF. Overall, the proposed methods facilitate high-throughput BN simulation and neurosymbolic matrix-vector-multiplication architectures.
                  </jats:p>
