title: Optimal design of multiphase interface synergistic lubrication: molecular dynamics insights into DLC films under oil lubrication
journal: Modelling and Simulation in Materials Science and Engineering
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study employed molecular dynamics simulations to systematically investigate the microscopic friction mechanisms of a sealing pair consisting of diamond-like carbon (DLC) coated plungers and nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) under oil-lubricated conditions. A friction model comprising base oil and the DLC-NBR interface was first constructed, and four different quantities of oil molecules (
                    <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>oil</jats:sub>
                    ) were set to analyze the effects of lubrication status on friction behavior, structural evolution, stress transmission, and temperature evolution of the system. The results indicate that the interfacial friction behavior initially improves and deteriorates with increasing oil content. When the
                    <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>oil</jats:sub>
                    is just sufficient (15CH), the oil lubrication effect reaches its optimal state. At this point, the oil molecule adsorption layer transforms the friction interface from solid-solid contact to solid-liquid contact, inhibiting the migration of molecular chains on the NBR surface. The oil molecule adsorption layer acts as a stress buffering layer, reducing the shear stress and normal stress of the friction pair by approximately 50% respectively, thereby lowering the friction force to 28.6 nN. Meanwhile, the oil film blocks the transfer of interfacial frictional heat to the NBR substrate and absorbs heat continuously, reducing the temperature of NBR from 380 to 340 K. When the oil content is too high (25CH), not only will the adsorption strength at the interface be enhanced, and the available space for oil molecules is compressed, raising the short-range repulsive force. Eventually, this leads to an increase in the sliding resistance. However, an excessively high oil content (25CH) will increase the viscosity of the adsorption layer and the adsorption strength at the solid-liquid interface, thereby reducing the lubrication performance and consequently increasing the sliding resistance. This study elucidates the oil-content-dominated multiphase interfacial lubrication mechanism and provides a molecular-level theoretical basis for the optimized design of DLC-coated plunger seals.
                  </jats:p>

title: The Molecular Potassium Code: Extracellular K+ Sensing, Allosteric Ion Selectivity, KCC2 Thermodynamics, and the Dynamic Control of Neural Inhibition
abstract: <jats:p>Neuronal excitability can be controlled by the level of potassium (K+) outside a neuron through both its effects on the cell membrane’s electrical properties and its influence on ion transport across the membrane. Recent studies have also shown that certain ligand-gated ion-channel receptors can be modulated by the levels of K+ outside the neuron. Therefore, understanding how each mechanism contributes to the generation of inhibitory signals requires the ability to differentiate between them. This study represents a review that integrates evidence using various methods, including electrophysiology, structural studies, thermodynamics, and optical measurements, to propose a framework called the molecular potassium code that explains how neurons respond to varying levels of K+ in their environment. The framework describes three ways that neurons interact with changing levels of K+: how these changes shift their K+ equilibrium potential and membrane voltage; how they alter the thermodynamic driving force for KCC2-mediated cotransport of K+ and Cl−; and how receptor-dependent modulation occurs at specific receptors when documented. Changes in activation, desensitization, pharmacological sensitivity, and permeation characteristics have been measured in Drosophila DmAlka channels; however, the atomic details of K+ recognition by these channels remain unclear. Human GlyRα2 variants engineered or edited to allow for assessment of K+-associated responses under elevated K+ conditions did not provide sufficient evidence for physiological recruitment of these receptors in mammals. Additionally, the presence and function of astrocytes, as well as geometric factors such as size, shape, and orientation, affect local concentrations of K+. Therefore, the framework described here provides multiple approaches that scientists can use to measure and interpret different mechanisms contributing to the generation of inhibitory signals in the nervous system.</jats:p>

title: Highly Efficient Functionalization of hBN With Lithium Oxalate: A Multifunctional Platform for Composites, Ion Transport, and Spin Labeling
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Multifunctional solid‐state materials are crucial for enabling safer and simpler lithium battery architectures. Here we report a scalable, solvent‐free mechanochemical strategy to overcome the chemical inertness of hexagonal boron nitride and produce  (LBNCO), a lithium‐rich boron nitride nanostructure. High‐energy milling simultaneously exfoliates hBN and induces robust covalent oxalate functionalization, yielding a nanocrystalline lamellar compound with intrinsically incorporated lithium. LBNCO exhibits  ionic conductivity, electronic insulation, and thermal stability exceeding . Additional mechanochemical processing enables further lithium enrichment without compromising chemical stability, allowing tunable ionic conductivity. By integrating ion transport, mechanical robustness, and thermal stability within a single material, LBNCO establishes a new platform for solid‐state lithium batteries and related technologies.</jats:p>

title: M2iOR: a quantitative, context-resolved atlas of insect odorant receptor-odorant interactions
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Olfactory detection in insects relies on interactions between odorant molecules and odorant receptors (ORs) expressed in olfactory sensory neurons. Although numerous studies have characterized insect OR-ligand interactions, these data remain scattered across the literature and heterogeneous in terms of species, experimental systems, and reporting standards, limiting their systematic analysis. Here, we present the Molecule to Insect Odorant Receptor database (M2iOR, https://m2ior.chemsensim.fr/), a curated, publicly accessible resource designed to centralize and standardize odorant-receptor interaction data. In its current release, M2iOR compiles 35 891 bioassay experiments describing 30 348 distinct insect OR-molecule pairs, extracted from 41 peer-reviewed publications and public databases. The resource integrates ligand structures, receptor sequences, species names, mixture information, and detailed experimental metadata. M2iOR provides flexible query tools allowing users to retrieve activity profiles for individual molecules or compound sets, and identify agonists and nonagonists for specific insect ORs, enabling comparative analyses across receptors, species, or bioassay systems. Advanced filtering based on curated metadata and batch search functionality support high-throughput analyses. For each query, users can visualize and download a curated aggregation of experimental results, including a binarized combinatorial representation of olfactory coding suitable for downstream computational studies. M2iOR provides a comprehensive framework for data-driven research in insect olfaction and comparative chemosensory biology.</jats:p>

                    Subtext remains a vital yet underexplored frontier in research on theatre translation. This study revisits debates

title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in Thermal Runaway Prevention and Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: <jats:p>Widespread deployment of lithium-ion batteries in energy storage and transportation increases the need to prevent and control thermal runaway and associated hazards. Focusing on energy storage systems using lithium iron phosphate batteries while drawing on other battery chemistries, this review examines failure mechanisms, hazard evolution, mitigation technologies, and engineering applicability. It analyzes coupled interfacial reactions, material transformations, and structural failure, alongside the effects of chemistry, state of charge, capacity, and aging. Multisignal warning and intervention, passive thermal barriers, active fire suppression and cooling, and combined strategies are compared in terms of mechanisms and operating conditions. Engineering assessment addresses experimental comparability, maturity, scalability, cost, and environmental safety. The synthesis identifies flame extinguishment, cell thermal stabilization, and propagation prevention as distinct objectives requiring complementary indicators. Warning effectiveness depends on timely intervention, whereas barrier–cooling integration depends on heat-transfer pathways, agent accessibility, and sustained supply. Technology selection therefore requires validation at the intended scale under relevant application constraints. Future priorities include linking warning to intervention, integrating barriers with sustained cooling, and developing evaluation frameworks with clearly defined applicability. Engineering validation should also incorporate long-term reliability, life-cycle costs, environmental impacts, and personnel safety to support application-specific mitigation strategies.</jats:p>

title: Vertex-based Curvilinear OPC via Bezier Curves
journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) is a critical step in semiconductor manufacturing, as it mitigates lithographic distortions and improves the pattern transfer fidelity from masks to silicon wafers. With the adoption of multi-beam mask writers, mask geometries are evolving from traditional Manhattan shapes to curvilinear patterns, offering improved resolution and process robustness. However, existing curvilinear OPC methods still suffer from limited optimization efficiency and accuracy, largely due to the difficulty of contour parameterization. To address this issue, we propose a gradient-based framework for vertex-based curvilinear OPC, where the mask is represented by connected Bézier curve segments controlled by trainable vertices, and the resulting rasterized mask is optimized to reduce lithographic errors. We evaluate the proposed method on the industry-standard dataset. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">
                      L
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    </jats:italic>
                    , PVBand, and VPE, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed gradient-based curvilinear optimization framework.

title: A pilot classroom intervention using project-based learning for steel framing design in a civil engineering course
abstract: <jats:p>Project-based learning in Civil Engineering can connect structural modelling, standards application, and technical communication through an authentic design task. This descriptive educational case study documents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a semester-long steel-framing redesign project. It examines what its collective output reveals about the traceability of calculations and collective assessment. Twenty-five seventh-semester students worked in five groups for approximately 16 weeks and consolidated their contributions into a single redesign project. The activity combined interpreting reference documents, structural configuration, modelling in SAP2000, verification against regulations, preparing drawings, receiving tutor feedback, and preparing the calculation report. The lecturer assessed the integrated project using a weighted rubric comprising eight criteria. The project achieved a total score of 85 per cent, with 100 per cent for structural configuration, application of standards, and presentation, but 60 per cent for the calculation report. The technical results characterised the collective output and, together with the rubric, enabled a distinction between the project's computational execution and the traceability of the documented calculations. The case study identifies calculation traceability and the limitations of collective assessment as teaching issues. For future implementations, it is proposed to introduce staged calculation logs and direct assessment of individual reasoning.</jats:p>

title: Soberania digital em disputa: governança dos territórios, colonialismos e design tecnológico no Sul Global Soberanía digital en disputa: gobernanza de los territorios, colonialismos y diseño tecnológico en el Sur Global Souveraineté numérique en dispute : gouvernance des territoires, colonialismes et design technologique dans le Sud Global Contested Digital Sovereignty: Territorial Governance, Colonialism, and Technological Design in the Global South
journal: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade
abstract: <jats:p>Este artigo discute a tecnopolítica em torno do conceito de soberania digital a partir de perspectivas críticas ao colonialismo, problematizando seus significados e valores segundo dois eixos: a relação entre Norte e Sul Global, e a tensão entre os âmbitos nacional e popular. Identifica a origem da noção de soberania no pensamento europeu moderno com os processos históricos de colonização e a persistência da colonialidade do poder nas tecnologias de informação e comunicação (TIC) e em seu design. A partir de autores como Álvaro Vieira Pinto, Frantz Fanon e Aníbal Quijano, sustenta-se que a soberania dos países periféricos não pode ser compreendida nos mesmos termos do Norte Global, exigindo uma rearticulação entre soberania nacional e soberania popular como condição para processos efetivos de descolonização. O artigo propõe a discussão sobre uma soberania digital que tensione os âmbitos nacional e popular, fundamentada na mobilização social e na construção de uma consciência crítica coletiva. Analisa-se como as TICs reconfiguram as dinâmicas de poder global, dando origem a novas estratégias de colonização, como o colonialismo digital e a colonialidade do fazer. Discute-se como a concentração tecnológica nas grandes corporações do Norte Global reforça a dependência do Sul Global, mas também revela brechas para práticas situadas e contra-hegemônicas. Por fim, são apresentadas iniciativas de soberania digital popular, com destaque para experiências de movimentos sociais brasileiros, que evidenciam possibilidades de apropriação crítica das tecnologias e seu design, capazes de tensionar estruturas existentes e produzir alternativas a partir de suas próprias realidades.</jats:p>

title: The Impact of Lean Principles on the Design and Improvement of Emergency Department Performance
journal: HERD: Health Environments Research & Design Journal
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Emergency departments (EDs) constitute essential components of most healthcare systems; However, in many countries, its efficiency has diminished due to the reliance on outdated guidelines and flawed operational systems. Redesigning the ED through modern approaches, such as Lean, can enhance process flow and service delivery. The purpose of this study is to apply Lean principles to improve ED performance through optimized design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methodology</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A comprehensive literature review, combined with a comparative, analytical, and synthetic approach to evaluate ED design guidelines, was conducted to examine new systems related to patient stratification, triage, and process flow. In addition, the field method and direct observation (Gemba), along with a Fishbone diagram, were employed to understand treatment processes and identify bottlenecks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The Lean approach influences access and the layout of ED spaces, resulting in substantial modifications. Key differences include the use of an Intake system (a combination of First Look and Rapid Medical Evaluation), result waiting and results/ECG rooms in the shared zone, internal waiting areas within the emergency and outpatient zones, standardized dimensions of examination rooms and acute and observation cubicles, among others.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, we established a revised operational process flow and a concise set of ED design guidelines. The study recommends maintaining flexible shift scheduling and staffing levels during periods of crisis and peak patient volume, with staff overlap extended to 2 hr to better manage patient flow and operational demands.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: In-situ hydrothermal synthesis of a bifunctional composite material multiwalled carbon nanotubes/cobalt phosphate for heavy-metal ion removal and supercapacitor electrode
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part L: Journal of Materials: Design and Applications
abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the drawbacks of existing bifunctional materials for adsorption-supercapacitor applications, including limited adsorption capacity and weak synergistic effect, a hydroxylated multi-walled carbon nanotubes/cobalt-phosphate (MWCNTs/CoTEDA-DAP) bifunctional composite was facilely fabricated via an in-situ hydrothermal strategy for aqueous Hg(II) (divalent mercury ion)/Pb(II) (divalent lead ion) removal and for use as supercapacitor electrodes. The adsorption behaviours towards Hg(II) and Pb(II), including kinetics, isotherms, thermodynamics and selectivity were systematically investigated. Box-Behnken response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimise adsorption parameters. Meanwhile, the electrochemical performance of MWCNTs/CoTEDA-DAP (hydroxylated multi-walled carbon nanotubes/cobalt-triethylenediamine-diammonium phosphate coordination phosphate) as supercapacitor electrode material was evaluated. The adsorption processes of Hg(II) and Pb(II) followed the Elovich and pseudo-second-order kinetic models, which demonstrates that chemisorption dominated the adsorption mechanism. The Langmuir isotherm model well described the monolayer adsorption behaviour. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG < 0, Gibbs free-energy change, ΔH > 0, enthalpy change, ΔS > 0, entropy change) verified that the adsorption was spontaneous, endothermic and entropy-increasing. Under the optimised RSM conditions, the maximum adsorption capacities attained 1345.24 mg/g for Hg(II) and 1521.83 mg/g for Pb(II). When deployed as a supercapacitor electrode, the composite achieved a specific capacitance of 181 F/g at 1 A/g. The synergistic effect originating from chelation of -OH, -NH- and phosphate groups as well as the conductive network of MWCNTs (hydroxylated multi-walled carbon nanotubes) contributes to the desirable bifunctional performance. This study provides a feasible strategy for designing integrated materials toward environmental remediation and energy-storage applications.</jats:p>

title: Drug Repurposing in Pre‐Eclampsia: Maternal Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Considerations for Clinical Trial Design
abstract: <jats:p>Pre‐eclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy affecting 3–8% of pregnancies worldwide, with no disease‐modifying therapy currently available. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy, yet no candidate has been validated to date. Pregnancy‐associated physiological changes alter drug pharmacokinetics (PK), and pre‐eclampsia itself may further modify drug disposition, complicating dose selection and contributing to inconclusive clinical trial outcomes. A structured literature search identified six prospective or randomized controlled trials of repurposed drugs for established pre‐eclampsia: esomeprazole, omeprazole, sulfasalazine, pravastatin, recombinant antithrombin, and metformin. All drugs were well tolerated, with metformin the one to show promising clinical benefit by prolonging gestation; the remaining five drugs yielded inconclusive or null efficacy outcomes. Critically, PK sampling was conducted in only three trials, and none systematically characterized exposure–response relationships using key pre‐eclampsia biomarkers, including soluble fms‐like tyrosine kinase‐1, soluble endoglin, and placental growth factor. Further common methodological limitations included small sample sizes (12–120 participants), heterogeneous gestational age eligibility criteria, and dosing regimens extrapolated from non‐pregnant populations without pregnancy‐specific optimization. These shortcomings likely contributed to the translational gap between promising preclinical findings and positive clinical trial outcomes. Model‐informed drug development (MIDD) approaches, including physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) and population pharmacokinetic (popPK) modeling, optimal sampling strategies, and simulation‐based dose selection, offer a framework to improve pre‐eclampsia trial design. Future studies should integrate these approaches with biomarker‐guided exposure–response analyses and prediction of fetal exposure throughout pregnancy to enhance therapeutic development, optimize maternal–fetal safety, and accelerate the identification of effective disease‐modifying therapies for pre‐eclampsia.</jats:p>

title: Your Future Is Whatever You… Generate It? GenUI as a New Challenge in Inclusive User Experience Design
abstract:
<jats:p>AI-based technologies shape the future of interface and user experience design (UI and UX). 
Recently, the industry dictionary has added a new term: GenUI (Generative UI – Generative User Interface). Rather than to AI-assisted interface design, it refers to a new way of interaction, in which the interface is not rigid and static (formed by a designer), but dynamically created by AI in real time, in response to the user’s needs and preferences. 
The new UI paradigm changes the user–system relationship. It shifts from accurate commands to communicating intentions and goals, while the system decides how to execute them.
Customised interfaces seem to be a great opportunity for designing more inclusive digital experience. The revolutionary vision of UI future, however, carries serious risks. Personalisation does not equal inclusiveness, and the current discourse around GenUI does not pay sufficient attention to accessibility. If GenUI future is dominated by the logic of profit-driven economy and capitalistic optimisation, existing inequalities may exacerbate. 
The article studies the notion of generative systems and tries to answer the question whether they can support care and agency, and not only efficiency, and to what extent designers are accountable for the developed generative systems. 

Keywords: GenUI, artificial intelligence (AI), digital accessibility, UX design</jats:p>

title: Why risk‐based premiums will not close the catastrophe protection gap: Conventional pricing, reinsurance capacity, and public scheme design
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Only about one‐fifth to one‐quarter of the economic losses caused by natural catastrophes in the European Union are insured, and the gap is widening as climate‐related losses grow. EIOPA and the ECB have proposed an EU‐level scheme combining a public–private reinsurance pool, funded by risk‐based premiums, with a public disaster fund. This paper asks whether risk‐based pricing at a public layer can close a gap that risk‐based pricing at the private layer has not. The capital‐market‐imperfections account of catastrophe insurance failure presupposes a knowable loss distribution; climate non‐stationarity removes that condition, and catastrophe pricing is better understood as conventional valuation under fundamental uncertainty. A five‐equation model of conventional pricing, with a demand side, makes reinsurance capacity endogenously cyclical and generates a rationing ratchet whose threshold is derived analytically and verified by simulation: prices soften within a few periods of a market break while attachment points and terms do not, and once climate‐driven model revisions recur before risk‐adjusted prices recover, rationing ratchets up and the insured share falls persistently. Simulated coverage is 15 points lower under conventional pricing with drifting losses than under a constant‐load benchmark, and the model reproduces the documented moments of the 2022–2026 cycle. Drawing on the French and Spanish schemes, the paper sets out the design features a workable public layer requires: solidarity pricing, an explicit public tail guarantee, and countercyclical funding.</jats:p>

title: Effect of Zwitterionic Comonomer Content on Room-Temperature Ion Transport in Fluorinated Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: <jats:p>Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) require high room-temperature ionic conductivity and stable electrochemical properties to replace conventional liquid electrolytes. In this study, the content of 3-(1-vinyl-3-imidazolio)propanesulfonate (VIPS) was varied from 0 to 10 wt.% in a fluorinated gel polymer electrolyte with a fixed poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) and 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl methacrylate (TFEMA) host. Adding 5 wt.% VIPS increased the temperature at which the gel lost 10% of its initial mass from 238 to 266 °C. Also at 25 °C, the ionic conductivity increased from 2.10 mS cm−1 for the VIPS-free gel to 4.88 mS cm−1 at 5 wt.% VIPS and the oxidative onset potential also improved from 4.80 to 5.15 V (vs. Li/Li+). The optimized GPE with 5 wt.%, named ZF-GPE-V5, shows stable lithium plating and stripping behavior over 1000 h. An LFP|ZF-GPE-V5|Li cell recovered 99.50% of its initial low-rate discharge capacity after operation at 1.0 C and retained 87.16% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 0.2 C. These results suggest that the appropriate application of zwitterion-functionalized monomers can serve as a bridging technology between conventional batteries and future all-solid-state batteries.</jats:p>

title: Design and Validation of a Hardware-in-the-Loop Platform for SAC-Based Covert UAV Redirection via GNSS Spoofing
abstract: <jats:p>Global navigation satellite system (GNSS) spoofing has emerged as an effective countermeasure to address the growing threat posed by the malicious use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) against military and civilian infrastructure. Previous UAV redirection spoofing approaches relied on internal target information state or were limited to verification through software simulations. This study integrates a Zynq UltraScale+ radiofrequency (RF) system-on-chip multi-constellation GNSS spoofer with a soft actor–critic covert spoofing policy based on a dual-normalized innovation squared reward, providing an RF-level hardware-in-the-loop simulation closed-loop platform within an anechoic chamber and enabling real-time integration of an actual PX4-based Pixhawk flight control computer with a commercial GNSS receiver. Operating solely on external radar observations without internal-target UAV information, the policy redirects the UAV within a 20 m capture radius of the fake destination across three scenarios. During this process, the manipulated measurements do not violate the innovation gate of the extended Kalman filter (EKF) even when the GNSS spoofing signal deceives the receiver. Experiments confirmed that the EKF continues to fuse these spoofed signals with normal measurements, demonstrating that, in a physical hardware closed-loop environment, a learning-based covert spoofing policy can bypass flight control computer integrity checks and successfully redirect the UAV.</jats:p>

title: Defect‐Conditioned Machine Learning for Molecular Passivator Design in Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dynamic defects, mobile ions, and evolving interfaces remain major obstacles to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics. Molecular passivation can mitigate these losses, but its efficacy is a conditional response rather than an intrinsic molecular property. It depends on defect identity and charge state, molecular conformation, adsorption geometry, interfacial composition, processing history, and operating conditions. This review therefore defines a defect‐molecule‐interface configuration as the learning object for machine‐learning‐assisted passivator design. We show how molecular, defect, interface, process, and device variables can be encoded without conflating passivation with platform‐dependent changes in film quality or architecture. Representative studies are compared by dataset size and scope, representation, prediction target, internal data split, external validation, and prospective experimental evidence. We further establish practical requirements for group‐aware validation, uncertainty calibration, applicability‐domain testing, and physics‐constrained learning. This framework positions machine learning as a decision tool for defect‐selective and experimentally verifiable interface design rather than as a ranking engine for isolated molecules.</jats:p>

title: Guidelines development for design reviews with advanced collaboration tools
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Design Reviews (DRs) function as formal governance checkpoints within the product development process where cross-functional stakeholders evaluate design proposals against product requirements to determine their readiness for progression. As design teams become increasingly global, they rely heavily on remote and digital workflows to conduct DRs. While research explores the implementation of new tools to enhance collaboration in DRs, studies often focus on technical feasibility or interaction effects in isolated settings rather than on how these technologies can be embedded in actual industrial processes. In this study, we examine the use of advanced collaboration tools, defined here as digital systems that provide shared spatial environments, in-scene deictic referencing, and independent navigation. Currently, organizations lack actionable guidance on integrating these tools into their DR processes. Thus, this paper develops an evidence-informed set of procedural guidelines for planning, conducting, and documenting DRs using advanced collaboration tools. Working with two automotive companies, we conducted a multi-phase study where two real industrial cases (one per company) were reconstructed to facilitate collaborative workshops aimed at mapping technological capabilities to procedural rules. The analysis draws on established accounts of grounding, workspace awareness, distributed cognition, and organizational routines to interpret the coordination breakdowns observed and the routines that address them. By analyzing verbal data and interaction logs, we developed a set of guidelines grounded in the specific coordination problems identified by practitioners and the technological capabilities required to resolve them. The resulting guidelines identify five domains, including pre-read and preparation, attention management, documentation and traceability, integration and handoff, and modality and role distribution. The guidelines provide a transferable structure for organizations to transform advanced collaboration tools from isolated visualizers into reliable, managed elements of the DRs workflow.</jats:p>

title: A Study of the Design Space of Motion and Disocclusion Control in Video Generation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Disocclusion occurs when object movement reveals previously hidden content. Existing image‐to‐video methods provide different forms of motion and disocclusion control, yet the design space they span remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically explore an algorithmic design space spanning motion specification (text‐based versus tracking‐based) and dis‐occlusion specification (text‐based versus image‐based). To facilitate this study, we construct a benchmark consisting of both synthetic scenes and captured scenes, covering rigid and deformable motions, as well as static and dynamic disoccluded objects. We compare existing and adapted methods across this design space to analyze the strengths and limitations of different control strategies for handling disocclusions during motion. Our study reveals that tracking‐based guidance improves motion accuracy, while image‐based guidance improves the fidelity of newly revealed content. However, jointly controlling the appearance and dynamics of disoccluded objects remains a challenging open problem, particularly in scenarios where newly revealed objects undergo their own motion after becoming visible.</jats:p>

title: Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation of AISI 316L Stainless Steel Parts Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite (
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF.
                  </jats:p>

title: Exact Solution of the Direct and Inverse Quasi‐Stationary Dynamo Problem in the Expanding Plasma Ball
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>It is shown that differential equation of the quasi‐stationary dynamo effect (i.e., generation of the electric fields and currents) in a uniformly‐expanding plasma ball with strongly anisotropic conductivity possesses the unique mathematical property: namely, the spectrum of its eigenvalues is universal and independent of physical parameters of the medium. As a result, it becomes possible to introduce a special set of eigenfunctions—which we called the generalized spherical functions—that can be used to solve the dynamo problem in exactly the same way as ordinary spherical functions are used to solve the Laplace equation. The corresponding exact solutions should be especially valuable for treating the inverse dynamo problem, that is, determination of the plasma parameters from the experimentally measured electric fields and currents.</jats:p>

title: ASIA: adaptive single-diffusion-stage inference acceleration for diffusion-based virtual try-on
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Virtual try-on synthesises an image of a person wearing a chosen garment. Diffusion models give the most realistic results, but remain too slow for interactive use. The leading method, TPD, runs its diffusion network twice: a first pass predicts a pair-specific mask locating where the garment belongs, and a second pass renders the garment into that region. Each pass takes about 100 denoising steps, so one image needs roughly 200, half of them producing only a binary shape. This first stage does not justify a diffusion model. We propose Adaptive Single-Diffusion-Stage Inference Acceleration (ASIA), which replaces diffusion-based mask generation with a lightweight convolutional network. Using DensePose and the flat garment mask as structural priors, ASIA predicts the pair-specific mask in one forward pass, reducing that stage from seconds to milliseconds. Try-on then needs a single diffusion stage, whose input block alone is finetuned to the new mask distribution. On VITON-HD, inference falls from 15.4 to 7.5 seconds per image, a 2.05-fold speedup. Under a controlled reproduction of TPD, paired structural (SSIM) and perceptual (LPIPS) similarity both improve while the Fréchet Inception Distance rises slightly (9.04 against 8.78). Removing an entire diffusion stage thus trades a small FID increase for a large speedup and improved paired fidelity.</jats:p>

title: Development of one-dimensional plasma transport code and the application to MPS-LD linear plasma device
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>To investigate plasma transport in the Multiple Plasma Simulation Linear Device (MPS-LD), a one-dimensional (1D) finite-volume (FV) fluid code LDPFT1D for edge plasma transport along the magnetic field is developed and coupled with a Monte Carlo (MC) code MCNT for neutral-particle transport. The coupled code LDPFT-MCNT1D is highly modular and extensible, allowing it to be flexibly adapted to various physical problems. LDPFT1D is benchmarked against the BOUT++ LPD module, and LDPFT-MCNT 1D is compared against experimental measurements from hydrogen plasma discharges in MPS-LD. Overall agreement is obtained in both comparisons, supporting the numerical implementation and physical model. Using LDPFT-MCNT 1D, the effects of H⁻ mediated dissociative attachment molecular activated recombination (DA-MAR) on plasma transport are investigated. The results show that DA-MAR provides an additional H⁺ loss channel in the near target region through dissociative attachment and mutual neutralization. The resulting reduction in the local net particle source decreases the electron density, ion flux, and heat flux at the target. Within the parameter range considered in this study, the contribution of DA-MAR to the total volumetric loss of H⁺ exhibits a pronounced dependence on the electron temperature. DA-MAR is primarily active in the low-temperature range 2 eV < Te < 4.5 eV, where it accounts for approximately 20%–30% of the total volumetric loss of H⁺. These results demonstrate that DA-MAR is an important molecular process affecting hydrogen plasma transport.</jats:p>

A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.</jats:p>

title: Study of the ionization in air-breathing electric rockets with VLEO atmospheric propellants and typical laboratory mixtures
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This work investigates the ionization of atmospheric propellant in air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) systems for satellites operating in Very-Low Earth Orbit (VLEO).  Plasma formation inside the ionization chamber of an air-breathing thruster is studied to gain insights on physical phenomena involved in ABEP technology. A time-dependent zero-dimensional model of the plasma chamber is formulated, that accounts for a comprehensive set of reactions for nitrogen, oxygen and argon. This model is implemented within a numerical framework to simulate plasma ignition at different operating parameters defined to describe geometry, intake behaviour, input power, magnetic field interactions, acceleration mechanism, and VLEO environmental conditions. The simulation results include the evolution in time of plasma density, composition and reaction rates during the ignition transient until stationary conditions.  The study identifies the plasma ignition envelope by analysing the dependencies of plasma properties on mass flow rate, electron temperature, and ion-to-neutral residence times' ratio. The composition and density of the plasma are characterized across different regimes, revealing a transition between molecular and atomic ions dominance. NO+ ion is observed as an important constituent for low-plasma-density regimes, where molecular ions dominate. Comparison between results on different mixtures are performed and approximation laws to facilitate experimental validation are derived, which can help improving the accuracy of plasma diagnostic measurements for experimental conditions relevant to ABEP testing.&#xD;Furthermore, it is shown that the use of argon as substitute of atomic oxygen in low-density air-like mixture plasma does not provide representative results.</jats:p>

title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
abstract: <jats:p>Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.</jats:p>

title:
A Single Water Molecule
Drives a 20-Fold Acceleration
in the Gas-Phase Reaction of Iodide with Ozone
journal:
Journal of
the American
Chemical Society
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Iodine chemistry has an outsized role in the atmosphere and environment due to its highly reactive nature. Unlike chlorine and bromine, around 80% of atmospheric iodine is emitted directly from the ocean through the reaction of iodide and ozone at the sea surface. Uncertainties remain, however, in the effects of hydration, salinity, temperature, and other factors on this globally significant reaction. Using linear ion-trap mass spectrometry, a single water molecule is shown here to provide a 23 (±6)-fold acceleration to the rate of iodide oxidation. The first step in reaction of both I– and I–·H2O with ozone is oxidation to IO– with subsequent fast reactions to yield IO3–. No evidence is found for direct routes from I–·H2O to IO2– nor any incorporation of the water oxygen into ionic products. Ab initio calculations show that the initial rate-determining step for both reactions proceeds on the singlet surface with water playing an active role to lower the barrier through hydrogen bonding. Kinetic modeling based on the computed energetics is in excellent agreement with experimental measurements and enables extrapolation of this reaction to lower temperatures relevant to polar regions and the ozone layer. This analysis shows that (i) I– may outcompete I• for ozone destruction as temperature decreases, and (ii) I–·H2O reacts more than an order of magnitude faster than I• over 350 to 230 K. This work demonstrates that iodide has a previously underappreciated role in multiphase ozone destruction in the atmosphere and lays the foundation for understanding microscopic environmental influences in salt clusters and nanodroplets.</jats:p>

title:

                    <sub>2</sub>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, 2D materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond the laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). The 2D TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal/chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers that achieve high polarizer FOMs of up to ∼19.3 (a record among 2D‐material‐coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield (∼98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios of up to ∼12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong potential for large‐scale manufacturing, these devices represent a solid step toward industrial implementation of 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers.
                  </jats:p>

Neighborhood Exposome at Birth and Trajectories of Epigenetic Age Acceleration Across Childhood
abstract:
<jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-4">
                    <jats:title>Importance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has been linked to increased disease risk in adults, yet its developmental trajectories and early-life neighborhood determinants remain poorly understood.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-5">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To examine whether there are associations between the neighborhood exposome at birth and EAA trajectories from early childhood through adolescence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-6">
                    <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This longitudinal cohort study used data from Project Viva, a prebirth cohort that enrolled pregnant women in eastern Massachusetts from April 22, 1999, to July 31, 2002. Participants included 570 children with available peripheral blood DNA methylation data, complete neighborhood characteristics, and complete covariates. Data were analyzed from August 19, 2024, to August 21, 2026.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-7">
                    <jats:title>Exposures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Neighborhood exposome profiles at birth derived from 22 census tract–level characteristics across 4 domains (area deprivation, social fragmentation, population density, and environmental quality) using self-organizing maps.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-8">
                    <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>EAA was calculated at 3, 8, and 13 years of age using the Horvath, Skin &amp;amp; Blood, and Wu epigenetic clocks. Trajectories were identified using latent class linear mixed models. Associations between neighborhood profiles and EAA trajectories were estimated using multinomial mixed models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-9">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among 570 children (mean [SD] age at early childhood, 3.2 [0.4] years; 305 [53.5%] male), 3 EAA trajectory groups (stable, increasing, and decreasing for the Horvath and Skin &amp;amp; Blood clocks or low-baseline for the Wu clock) and 3 neighborhood profiles were identified. Compared with profile 1 (suburban, lowest adverse exposures [n = 278]), children born into profile 2 (urban, high residential instability and single-person households, and highway proximity [n = 168]) had greater odds of increasing EAA for the Wu clock (adjusted odds ratio, 1.67 [95% CI, 1.03-2.69]). Profile 3 (urban, high socioeconomic deprivation and pollution [n = 124]) showed no associations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-10">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this longitudinal cohort study, birth into neighborhoods characterized by high residential instability and single-person households and highway proximity was associated with increasing Wu EAA trajectories across childhood. These findings suggest that early-life neighborhood conditions, encompassing both social and physical environmental factors, may represent targets for interventions aimed at reducing long-term disease risk. Further research is needed to clarify the implications of these findings for later health and prevention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: An in situ atmospheric-pressure dielectric barrier discharge setup for time-resolved synchrotron characterisation of cerium metal-organic frameworks
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In situ investigation of plasma-material interactions are essential for understanding material stability and transformation mechanisms under non-thermal plasma (NTP) conditions. Nevertheless, such studies remain challenging due to the limited availability of plasma reactors compatible with synchrotron-based structural and spectroscopic techniques. Here, we present the design, construction, and characterisation of a dedicated in situ atmospheric-pressure dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) reactor enabling quasi-simultaneous X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) during plasma exposure.The compact reactor integrates a quartz discharge tube, an exchangeable powder sample holder, a controlled gas-flow system, and aligned driven and grounded electrodes. The geometry ensures that the reactive gas stream passes directly through the sample while maintaining optical and X-ray access. Stable plasma operation is achieved at 20.8 kHz and peak-to-peak voltages up to 14 kV with various gas mixtures. Electrical diagnostics based on current-voltage measurements and Lissajous analysis quantify discharge power, transferred charge, and effective plasma capacitance, confirming reproducible and tunable plasma conditions. Optical imaging and thermocouple measurements further validate discharge position in relation to the sample and provide temperature control up to 200 °C. &#xD;Compatibility with synchrotron radiation investigation is demonstrated at a dedicated beamtime at ESRF (BM23) through time-resolved transmission XAS and XRD measurements. As a proof of concept, cerium-based metal–organic frameworks, Ce-CAU-41 and -44, were investigated, illustrating the capability of the setup to track plasma-induced structural and chemical changes in real time. The developed reactor provides a robust and flexible tool for in situ synchrotron studies of plasma-driven processes and enables mechanistic investigations of material transformations under atmospheric-pressure plasma conditions.</jats:p>

title: Impairment-aware WDM–CPDM laser VLC with adaptive coherent DSP
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Laser-based visible-light communication (VLC) can exploit wavelength and polarization multiplexing, but amplifier, channel, and coherent-receiver impairments interact. This paper develops an impairment-aware simulation of an eight-wavelength, dual-circular-polarization link carrying a 380.16-MHz occupied orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) resource grid within a nominal 400-MHz fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR)-aligned channel. The model includes laser-diode/semiconductor-optical-amplifier (LD–SOA) saturation and amplified spontaneous emission, wavelength-dependent gain ripple, Lambertian line-of-sight loss, residual wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) crosstalk, polarization mixing, coherent-receiver noise, phase/frequency offsets, and quadrature imbalance. The receiver combines covariance whitening, pilot-estimated 2 × 2 regularized multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) separation, pilot-assisted phase correction, and damped decision-directed refinement. With quadrature phase-shift keying, the nominal net payload rate after applying a 7 % FEC-overhead factor for rate reporting is 8.527 Gb/s. In the controlled reference realization, the proposed receiver remains below the 3.8 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    pre-FEC bit-error-rate screening level through 50 m. A receiver ablation shows that both Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization and symmetric covariance whitening remove most of the reference I/Q-imbalance penalty, while the decision-directed update provides a smaller incremental improvement near the reach boundary. A separate sweep gives 17.054 Gb/s with 16-level quadrature-amplitude modulation through 16 m. The results provide a traceable baseline for joint optical-front-end and coherent-receiver design.
                  </jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Excess fat mass is causally linked to multiple diseases, but the use of existing therapies, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, is limited by varying effects and common side effects, including loss of fat-free mass. We aimed to identify proteins associated with fat mass, but ideally not also associated with fat-free mass, as potential drug targets for alternative therapeutic strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We used UK Biobank data on plasma levels of 3K proteins (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 35K) and fat and fat-free mass (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 368K). We applied a machine learning procedure to select proteins for downstream
                      <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>
                      Mendelian randomisation analyses, which estimated associations of genetically predicted protein levels with fat mass. These were followed by colocalisation analyses to assess shared causal genetic variants and further
                      <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>
                      Mendelian randomisation analyses to assess associations with fat-free mass.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Here we present evidence on the associations of genetically predicted levels of 21 proteins with fat mass, including five which also colocalise with the trait (AGER, CRIM1, DNER, NEFL, and PRRT3). Seven of the 21 proteins have no clear association with fat-free mass, and ADM has an association with fat-free mass opposite in direction to its association with fat mass, suggesting that modulating these proteins may be less likely to also lower fat-free mass. Two proteins, AGER and ADM, have been investigated in advanced-stage clinical trials for indications unrelated to adiposity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings support prioritising several proteins for further research as potential drug targets for fat mass reduction. They highlight proteins that may help diversify therapy options beyond glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and suggest possible repurposing opportunities.</jats:p>

title: LoKI-GM: a global model framework for plasma chemistry studies
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Global (zero-dimensional or spatially averaged) models are widely employed to study complex chemistries in low-temperature plasmas (LTPs). By adopting a spatially average description of the plasma, they substantially reduce the computational cost while still providing reliable and detailed insight into the key processes taking place in the plasma. In their most general formulation, global models involve the coupled solution of a Boltzmann solver (to describe the electron kinetics) and a Chemistry solver (to describe the heavy-species kinetics).  &#xD;This paper presents a tutorial on the LisbOn Kinetics Global Model (LoKI-GM) framework, developed in MATLAB and available as open-source code. The framework couples the Boltzmann solver LoKI-B, which solves the space-independent form of the two-term electron Boltzmann equation for non-magnetised non-equilibrium LTPs, excited by DC/HF electric fields or time-dependent (non-oscillatory) electric fields, and the Chemistry solver LoKI-C, which solves the system of zero-dimensional rate balance equations for the main charged and neutral species in the plasma and at the surface, receiving as input the kinetic schemes for the gas/plasma/surface system under study. Distinctive features of LoKI-GM include the closure of the model through charge neutrality, which yields the self-consistent maintenance field of DC and HF discharges, and the availability of several transport models for charged and neutral species. LoKI-GM can also couple a microkinetic mesoscopic surface model and a gas thermal model to the volume kinetics. We briefly present the formulation of LoKI-GM, including its numerical solution strategy, input/output parameters, and calculation workflow for both active discharges and afterglow plasmas. The main differences with respect to existing global models are highlighted, and the flexibility of the code for plasma chemistry studies is demonstrated through representative simulation results obtained across a range of gas discharge configurations and operating conditions.</jats:p>

PLASMA RICO EN PLAQUETAS ACTIVADO COMO ADYUVANTE A LA DILATACIÓN ENDOSCÓPICA EN ESTENOSIS ESOFÁGICAS BENIGNAS
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Introducción:</jats:bold>
                    Las estenosis esofágicas benignas pueden recurrir tras la dilatación endoscópica por inflamación y remodelación fibrótica, condicionando nuevas sesiones. El plasma rico en plaquetas (PRP) aporta mediadores de reparación tisular y podría modular la cicatrización esofágica.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Objetivos:</jats:bold>
                    Describir factibilidad técnica, eventos adversos y evolución clínica y endoscópica tras dilatación con Savary-Gilliard sobre guía Savary e infiltración submucosa de PRP autólogo activado con gluconato de calcio al 10%.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Métodos:</jats:bold>
                    Estudio observacional retrospectivo, descriptivo y unicéntrico de cinco adultos con estenosis benignas: tres pépticas, una cáustica y una postquirúrgica por ascenso gástrico secundario a estenosis cáustica. La dilatación se realizó con Savary-Gilliard sobre guía Savary. El PRP se obtuvo de 20 mL de sangre citratada mediante doble centrifugación (1500 rpm/8 min y 2500 rpm/5 min); se recuperaron 8 mL, activados con 0,20 mL de gluconato de calcio al 10% e infiltrados submucosamente en cuatro cuadrantes post dialtacion. Se evaluaron disfagia (Mellow-Pinkas), número de dilataciones, cicatrización endoscópica a 8 semanas despues de la última sesión, recurrencia y eventos adversos mediante análisis descriptivo.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Resultados:</jats:bold>
                    Tres mujeres y dos hombres; edad media 43 años (22–63). El diámetro inicial fue 8–10 mm en cuatro pacientes y 2 mm en uno. La mediana de disfagia disminuyó de 3 (2–4) a 0; todos alcanzaron Mellow-Pinkas 0. Tres pacientes requirieron dos sesiones, uno tres y el caso de 2 mm, ocho. A las 8 semanas hubo cicatrización mucosa adecuada en 5/5 y no se observaron perforación, sangrado significativo ni otros eventos adversos relacionados. El seguimiento mediano fue 70 semanas (35–144); dos pacientes presentaron recurrencia tardía de disfagia a las 70 y 72 semanas.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Conclusión:</jats:bold>
                    La dilatación con Savary-Gilliard sobre guía Savary seguida de PRP activado fue factible y no presentó eventos adversos relacionados. La mejoría clínica, la cicatrización endoscópica y las recurrencias tardías respaldan estudios prospectivos controlados para determinar eficacia.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Palabras clave:</jats:bold>
                    Estenosis Esofágica; Endoscopía Gastrointestinal; Plasma Rico en Plaquetas; Trastornos de Deglución.
                  </jats:p>

Saha ionization equation in its new perspective: An astrochemical equilibrium and plasma chemistry framework
journal: International Journal of Modern Physics D
abstract: <jats:p>The Saha ionization equation, originally formulated within the framework of stellar astrophysics, is reinterpreted in this work as a high-temperature extension of classical chemical equilibrium theory. Ionization is treated as a reversible chemical reaction whose equilibrium state is governed by temperature, electron pressure, and the thermodynamic properties of the participating species. By employing the formalism of Gibbs free energy, equilibrium constants, and molecular partition functions, we demonstrate that the Saha relation is mathematically equivalent to the canonical expression [Formula: see text] used in physical chemistry. Building on this equivalence, we introduce a quantitative Van’t Hoff-style analysis of the Saha equilibrium, showing that the characteristic curvature of [Formula: see text] versus [Formula: see text] is a direct, measurable signature of the translational entropy carried by the liberated electron. Worked numerical examples for hydrogen and calcium connect this thermodynamic treatment directly to the Balmer-line maximum in A-type stars and the Ca II H&K lines of solar-type stars. The electron number density is identified as a chemical control parameter analogous to pressure in Le Chatelier’s principle. The implications of this framework are discussed in the context of astrochemistry: ionization balance governs spectral classification across the Harvard O–M sequence, structures the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram as a plasma-chemical phase space, and determines astrochemical reaction pathways in diffuse interstellar clouds and cold molecular cloud environments. This work establishes a quantitative, chemistry-first conceptual bridge between laboratory plasma chemistry and astrophysical stellar behavior.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) has reported anti-atherosclerotic effects and may alter the gut microbiota, but its relationship to the microbial choline–trimethylamine (TMA)–trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) axis remains unclear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this exploratory pilot, twelve male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to Control, 1% choline (Model), or 1% choline plus AS-IV (40 mg/kg/day) groups (n = 4 each) for 28 days. Caecal 16S rRNA profiles, plasma choline/TMA/TMAO, and a sensitivity-tested CutC docking analysis were evaluated. The four mice in each group shared one cage, so cage and treatment were completely confounded.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Bray–Curtis community composition differed among groups (PERMANOVA R2 = 0.619, P = 0.001), although the small sample and one-cage-per-group design preclude population-level or causal inference. High-choline exposure was associated with a 10.7-fold higher mean plasma TMAO than Control (668.3 vs. 62.3 ng/mL); mean TMAO remained high with AS-IV (709.8 ng/mL; AS-IV vs. Model P = 1.000). TMA and choline showed similar group patterns, but several measurements exceeded the vendor-reported quantification range and are exploratory. Taxonomic functional predictions were hypothesis-generating only. Docking scores for AS-IV and cycloastragenol were strongly dependent on search-box size and were not interpreted as evidence for or against CutC inhibition.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>AS-IV treatment was associated with a different caecal microbial composition without an observed reduction in high-choline-associated plasma TMAO. These findings generate hypotheses but require replication in a powered, multi-cage study including both sexes and direct functional measurements.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Performance of surface dielectric barrier discharge plasma actuators at different ambient conditions
journal: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of the influence of ambient air temperature and pressure on the performance of a surface dielectric barrier discharge plasma actuator. The analysis focuses on key discharge and flow characteristics, including the discharge current, power consumption, electric body force, and the resulting induced airflow. The temperature and pressure effects were examined independently to isolate their respective contributions to actuator behavior. A two-dimensional, self-consistent plasma–fluid model is employed, incorporating transport equations for electrons, positive ions, and negative ions, coupled with the Poisson equation for the electric field. The resulting electrohydrodynamic body force is introduced into the Navier–Stokes equations to resolve the induced flow field. The model is implemented using the finite-element method. The results demonstrate that gas pressure is the dominant parameter affecting discharge characteristics. Increasing pressure significantly reduces discharge current, power consumption, and ionization intensity due to reduced electron and ion mobilities. In contrast, temperature variations within the range 240–330 K have a comparatively weaker influence on discharge behavior. Despite these pronounced changes in electrical characteristics, the total electric force exhibits relatively low sensitivity to environmental conditions. The electric body force is found to be highly nonuniform and results in a wall-jet flow structure with peak velocities on the order of 9 m·s⁻¹. Flow characteristics show moderate dependence on ambient conditions, with pressure primarily affecting velocity decay and temperature influencing peak velocity magnitude. Comparison with experimental data shows good agreement in the core flow region, confirming the validity of the model.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a simulation-based study of an erbium-doped-fibre-assisted random distributed-feedback (rDFB) Raman amplifier for long-haul wavelength-division multiplexed transmission. The proposed architecture combines distributed Raman amplification over a 50 km standard single-mode-fibre span with a 25 cm terminal erbium-doped fibre (EDF) section pumped only by the residual 1460 nm rDFB field. The terminal EDF is intended to compensate span-end connection losses without a dedicated 980 nm or 1480 nm pump source. The model is calibrated against an experimentally measured optical-time-domain-reflectometer (OTDR) power profile, and an additional 2 dB EDF-gain margin is introduced to represent inter-span losses. The study considers a single 2 dB net-gain operating point, selected by minimizing signal-power variation along the span. The optimized configuration is applied to a 50-channel C-band WDM system over an equivalent 150-span, 7500 km link with idealized per-span power reset. The simulated central-channel OSNR reaches approximately 18.9 dB after 7500 km, while the channel OSNRs remain between about 17.5 and 19 dB. However, central-channel optimization produces a strongly nonuniform gain profile, increasing from approximately 2 dB near the band centre to 6.5 dB at the long-wavelength edge. The Kerr nonlinear-product power also increases by about 30 dB between one span and 7500 km. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed architecture for span-end loss compensation, while showing that gain flattening, multi-channel optimization, system-level nonlinear analysis, and experimental validation are required before practical deployment.</jats:p>

title: Defending ontic structural realism in quantum field theory
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Ontic structural realism</jats:italic>
                    (OSR) has been suggested as a metaphysics for quantum field theory (QFT). A common objection to OSR highlights the presence of fundamental intrinsic properties in physical theories (such as QFT) as undermining OSR. As there are purported examples of fundamental intrinsic properties possessed by fields in QFT, OSR is purportedly refuted in QFT (Berghofer, 2018). This article defends OSR from this argument. There are two possible strategies for responding to this argument: (1) denying that Berghofer’s counterexamples to OSR are intrinsic properties, and (2) finding a means of accommodating intrinsic properties in OSR. I consider the first strategy and discuss several possible arguments why the purported cases of fundamental intrinsic properties in QFT are non-intrinsic. Additionally, as there are a number of means available for OSR to accommodate intrinsic properties, the second strategy also succeeds.
                  </jats:p>

title: The Gravitational Constant G and the Confinement of the Strong Force: Proton Quantum Dynamics Within the Baryonic Expansion Framework
journal: PHYSICS Journal: Theoretical and Experimental Studies
abstract:
<jats:p>Newton’s gravitational constant G is measured but has never been derived from more fundamental quantities. Within the
baryonic expansion framework developed by the author since 1990, we examine how G is related to the proton’s mass,
radius and internal pressure. The principal findings are three. (i) Applying the author’s 1993 expansion equation to the
proton and comparing the result with the acceleration its internal pressure (≈1035 Pa) would produce in the absence of
confi nement defines a confinement leakage factor k ≈ 3 × 10-40.
(ii) G is then bound to proton quantities by the exact relation G = 4π k Pp rp
4
 / mp
2
. (iii) Because Pp rp
4
 ≈ 1.6 h-bar c, the
leakage factor equals the proton’s gravitational coupling αG ≈ 6 × 10-39 divided by a geometric factor of about 20. As
defi ned here, k contains G, so these relations are consistency relations and not yet a derivation of G. We state the condition
under which they become one, an independent determination of k or of the proton surface expansion rate from confinement
physics or from the Dirac Sea energy source, and identify two routes toward it. We propose, as an interpretation to be
tested, that gravity is the residual leakage of the strong force through quark confi nement.</jats:p>

title: New Projection Operators for Planar Electrodynamics
journal: International Journal of Modern Physics A
abstract: <jats:p>In this article, we provide a new construction of a set of projection operators and apply it to obtain the propagator of three-dimensional models of electrodynamics; in particular, we consider the Maxwell-Lee-Wick-Chern-Simons, Maxwell-Deser-Jackiw electrodynamics and nonlocal infinite derivative electrodynamics. In order to prove the efficacy of these operators, we perform a causality and unitarity analysis to investigate the presence of ghosts and tachyons.</jats:p>

title: Quantum Machine Learning: An Experimental Survey
abstract: <jats:p>Quantum machine learning (QML) is advancing rapidly, yet it remains unclear which artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities benefit from quantum approaches, how strong the supporting evidence is, and whether reported gains justify claims of practical quantum advantage. This bounded critical survey introduces the Quantum AI Stack (QAIS), a capability-centered framework covering ten functional areas, and applies it to 107 experimental studies first released from 2024 to 6 August 2026, identified through keyword searches of arXiv, IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library and reported following PRISMA 2020. Each study was appraised on seven weighted criteria, including comparison fairness, statistical practice, reproducibility and hardware realism, and each capability was assigned a level in a five-level maturity model. Within this corpus, quantum feature learning, quantum neural networks, hybrid quantum AI and quantum optimization have the most thoroughly corroborated evidence, much of it establishing parity rather than advantage, and no capability is deployable. Benefits that survive fair classical comparison are narrow and study-specific, including benchmark-specific accuracy gains and improvements in parameter efficiency, robustness, throughput and energy. None establishes practical quantum advantage, and null or negative findings occur at every level of evidence quality. Because inter-rater agreement was limited, the maturity assignments are provisional.</jats:p>
