title: Maternal plasma cell-free RNAs and sonographic parameters for predicting spontaneous preterm birth in twin pregnancies: A prospective cohort study
abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: To evaluate whether cervical length (CL), uterocervical angle (UCA), and five maternal plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNAs) markers can predict spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) before 37 and 34 weeks in twin pregnancies.
Methods: This prospective study included 80 twin pregnancies examined at 14 - 24 weeks’ gestation at Hai Phong Medical University Hospital, from February 2023 to February 2025. CL and UCA were measured by transvaginal ultrasonography, and plasma cfRNA concentrations of PSME2, NAMPT, APOA1, APOA4, and Hsa-let-7g were quantified using droplet digital PCR. Participants were followed until delivery. Associations with sPTB were assessed using multivariable binary logistic regression, and predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
Results: Women who delivered preterm had a significantly larger UCA and shorter CL than those delivering at term. Among the five RNA markers, only Hsa-let-7g differed significantly between women with sPTB before 34 weeks and those delivering at or after 34 weeks (1.89 ± 0.51 vs. 1.03 ± 0.54, p = 0.024). After adjusting, UCA was independently associated with sPTB before 37 weeks (OR 1.042, 95% CI 1.005 - 1.081) and before 34 weeks (OR 1.056, 95% CI 1.004 - 1.111). Hsa-let-7g was associated with sPTB before 34 weeks (OR 3.391, 95% CI 1.089 - 10.556). Area under the curve for predicting sPTB before 34 weeks was 0.799 for UCA, 0.712 for Hsa-let-7g, and 0.829 for their combination.
Conclusion: Second-trimester UCA and plasma Hsa-let-7g showed potential as non-invasive markers for predicting sPTB in twin pregnancies. Their combined use may improve the prediction of sPTB before 34 weeks.</jats:p>

title: Development of one-dimensional plasma transport code and the application to MPS-LD linear plasma device
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>To investigate plasma transport in the Multiple Plasma Simulation Linear Device (MPS-LD), a one-dimensional (1D) finite-volume (FV) fluid code LDPFT1D for edge plasma transport along the magnetic field is developed and coupled with a Monte Carlo (MC) code MCNT for neutral-particle transport. The coupled code LDPFT-MCNT1D is highly modular and extensible, allowing it to be flexibly adapted to various physical problems. LDPFT1D is benchmarked against the BOUT++ LPD module, and LDPFT-MCNT 1D is compared against experimental measurements from hydrogen plasma discharges in MPS-LD. Overall agreement is obtained in both comparisons, supporting the numerical implementation and physical model. Using LDPFT-MCNT 1D, the effects of H⁻ mediated dissociative attachment molecular activated recombination (DA-MAR) on plasma transport are investigated. The results show that DA-MAR provides an additional H⁺ loss channel in the near target region through dissociative attachment and mutual neutralization. The resulting reduction in the local net particle source decreases the electron density, ion flux, and heat flux at the target. Within the parameter range considered in this study, the contribution of DA-MAR to the total volumetric loss of H⁺ exhibits a pronounced dependence on the electron temperature. DA-MAR is primarily active in the low-temperature range 2 eV < Te < 4.5 eV, where it accounts for approximately 20%–30% of the total volumetric loss of H⁺. These results demonstrate that DA-MAR is an important molecular process affecting hydrogen plasma transport.</jats:p>

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.</jats:p>

title: Study of the ionization in air-breathing electric rockets with VLEO atmospheric propellants and typical laboratory mixtures
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This work investigates the ionization of atmospheric propellant in air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) systems for satellites operating in Very-Low Earth Orbit (VLEO).  Plasma formation inside the ionization chamber of an air-breathing thruster is studied to gain insights on physical phenomena involved in ABEP technology. A time-dependent zero-dimensional model of the plasma chamber is formulated, that accounts for a comprehensive set of reactions for nitrogen, oxygen and argon. This model is implemented within a numerical framework to simulate plasma ignition at different operating parameters defined to describe geometry, intake behaviour, input power, magnetic field interactions, acceleration mechanism, and VLEO environmental conditions. The simulation results include the evolution in time of plasma density, composition and reaction rates during the ignition transient until stationary conditions.  The study identifies the plasma ignition envelope by analysing the dependencies of plasma properties on mass flow rate, electron temperature, and ion-to-neutral residence times' ratio. The composition and density of the plasma are characterized across different regimes, revealing a transition between molecular and atomic ions dominance. NO+ ion is observed as an important constituent for low-plasma-density regimes, where molecular ions dominate. Comparison between results on different mixtures are performed and approximation laws to facilitate experimental validation are derived, which can help improving the accuracy of plasma diagnostic measurements for experimental conditions relevant to ABEP testing.&#xD;Furthermore, it is shown that the use of argon as substitute of atomic oxygen in low-density air-like mixture plasma does not provide representative results.</jats:p>

ESCRT-III assembly restores membrane tension in micron-scale plasma membrane repair
abstract: <jats:p>Plasma membrane integrity is essential for cellular survival, yet how cells repair micron-scale plasma membrane ruptures remains poorly understood. Here, using the genetically tractable Caenorhabditis elegans epidermis, we combine live imaging, genetics, super-resolution microscopy, and biophysical approaches to define a size-dependent role for endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT)-III in large-scale membrane repair. Small wounds induce transient, focal VPS-32 accumulation, whereas large wounds trigger the formation of a persistent but dynamic, circumferential ESCRT-III assembly that remains associated with the wound during repair. Formation of this assembly requires conserved ESCRT regulators, including ALX-1, TSG-101, and VPS-4, together with VPS-32 polymerization. The wound-associated ESCRT-III assembly is required for membrane tension restoration and efficient membrane repair, while disrupting VPS-32 polymerization impairs tension recovery, reduces vesicle recruitment and wound closure, and consequently compromises axon regeneration and organismal survival following injury. Together, our findings suggest that large plasma membrane wounds induce a persistent, dynamic ESCRT-III assembly that restores membrane tension and facilitates vesicle-mediated membrane addition to promote wound repair.</jats:p>

title: Monte Carlo simulations as the cornerstone of next-generation patient-specific quality assurance in particle therapy
abstract: <jats:p>Phantom-based Patient-Specific QA (PSQA) methods are resource-intensive and lack sensitivity, especially for Intensity Modulated Particle Therapy (IMPT) with steep dose gradients. To address these challenges, the European Particle Therapy Network (EPTN/ESTRO) has developed guidelines for phantom-less PSQA methods, including Monte Carlo (MC)-based Independent Dose Calculation (IDC) and log file-based QA. Although IDC can be standardized across clinics, the quality and availability of machine log files vary significantly by vendor, underscoring the need for manufacturers to standardize log file information and accessibility for the user community. Rapid Particle Therapy (PT) advancements (e.g. Linear Energy Transfer (LET) painting, Particle Arc Therapy (PAT), Multi-Ion Therapy (MIT), FLASH, Spatially Fractionated Radiation Therapy (SFRT), etc.) are reshaping established treatment paradigms. The future prescription may include not only dose, but also LET, dose rate, spatial dose modulation and biological information. Once treatment quality depends on quantities that cannot be measured in patient-specific phantoms, computational verification becomes unavoidable. To ensure the safe integration of these innovations, MC-based PSQA becomes essential, releasing machine and human resources, providing more time for patient treatment and substantially reducing the ecological impact of PSQA.</jats:p>

Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Power Distribution Network Reconfiguration using Hybrid Particle Swarm and Genetic Algorithm
journal: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
abstract: <jats:p>Power distribution networks are a critical component of the electric power distribution system. Hence, numerous research has focus on distribution network reconfiguration systems, intending to minimize power losses and interruptions, namely, Customer Average Interruption Index (CAIDI), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), Energy Not Supplied (ENS), and Voltage Profile (VP) improvement, either by Genetic Algorithm (GA) or Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Nonetheless, existing research has not simultaneously employed a hybrid of GA and PSO optimization methods to ascertain which optimization method is better in terms of improving the reliability indices, such as CAIDI, SAIFI, and ENS, while minimizing power losses and improving the VP, thus leaving a gap in the literature. Hence, the proposed research work seeks to utilize the synergy of GA and PSO optimization techniques on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems with the aforementioned reliability targets to unearth which of the optimization techniques is better than the other. Meanwhile, the obtained results indicate that the GA exhibits a higher voltage level enhancement of 2.75% with a corresponding SAIFI reduction of 33%. Nonetheless, the PSO unveils superior or enhanced power loss reduction of 61.75%, ENS reduction of 48%, and CAIDI reduction of 30% with a corresponding computational speed of 0.24 seconds. Hence, based on the aforementioned analysis of the results, it can be concluded that the selection of the optimization algorithm depends on the network's specific operational requirements, as no single algorithm performs optimally across all parameter measurements. Besides, while the PSO performs excellently in terms of loss, ENS, and CAIDI reduction, the GA performs well in terms of voltage enhancement and SAIDI reduction.</jats:p>

title: CCR1 silencing in macrophage-like cells reduces alveolar epithelial cell death and junctional protein loss
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Macrophage activation accompanies epithelial injury in acute inflammatory lung disease, but the receptors linking inflammatory signaling to epithelial cell death remain incompletely characterized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We analyzed five public transcriptomic cohorts comprising 158 clinical profiles, including bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and peripheral-blood single-cell datasets and three whole-blood cohorts. Cell composition, cell-death and stress programs, pseudobulk expression, pathway enrichment, and sample-specific cell-cell communication were integrated to nominate a receptor for perturbation.
                      <jats:italic>CCR1</jats:italic>
                      was silenced in LPS/ATP-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells, and their conditioned medium was applied to primary human pulmonary alveolar epithelial cells.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The BALF atlas contained 86,315 cells. Increasing disease severity was accompanied by higher neutrophil, injury-transitional epithelial, and interferon-state macrophage fractions. Epithelial autophagy, necroptosis, and hypoxia/glycolysis scores increased with severity, whereas the autophagy score was the principal severity-associated macrophage program. Three retained chemokine interactions converged on CCR1, supported by receptor expression, pseudobulk analysis, and its association with macrophage autophagy. Whole-blood module effects varied across cohorts.
                      <jats:italic>CCR1</jats:italic>
                      silencing reduced macrophage inflammatory transcripts and IL-1β and
                      <jats:italic>TNF</jats:italic>
                      -α release. Conditioned medium from
                      <jats:italic>CCR1</jats:italic>
                      -silenced macrophage-like cells reduced epithelial Annexin V positivity from 39.0% ± 1.73% to 16.9% ± 1.69%, lowered LDH release, and preserved junction-related transcripts and proteins.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Transcriptomic analyses and cellular perturbation support a contribution of macrophage
                      <jats:italic>CCR1</jats:italic>
                      to inflammatory activation, epithelial cell death, and junctional injury in the tested acute lung-injury model.
                    </jats:p>

title: Decoding the human bone metastatic niche at single-cell resolution: convergent ecosystems, therapeutic vulnerabilities, and the spatial frontier
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Bone metastases arise from biologically diverse solid malignancies but develop within a shared and highly specialized skeletal microenvironment. Recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics have enabled direct characterization of human bone metastatic lesions and have shifted the field from tumor-specific descriptions toward cross-cancer ecosystem models. Emerging pan-cancer atlases reveal partial convergence across malignancies, including recurrent suppressive myeloid states, transcriptionally defined T Cell exhaustion programs, remodeled stromal and osteolineage compartments, specialized endothelial niches, and distinct malignant-cell programs observed in bone. Several of these ecosystem features nominate candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities rather than established dependencies. Combined immune-checkpoint blockade, modulation of osteoimmune macrophage states, and disruption of stromal chemokine signaling have each received different levels of support, ranging from transcriptomic or spatial association to
                    <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                    perturbation, while prospective clinical validation is lacking. Because recurrence across analytical studies is not equivalent to independent replication or bone specificity, we distinguish cross-cancer recurrence from bone enrichment and from mechanistically supported skeletal-niche adaptation. Current datasets also reveal substantial heterogeneity between patients, tumor types, anatomical compartments, treatment exposures, and analytical frameworks, arguing against a single universal bone metastatic niche. This mini review synthesizes the rapidly evolving human single-cell literature on established bone metastases, evaluates candidate niche-associated therapeutic vulnerabilities, and outlines the spatial and functional validation required for clinical translation.
                  </jats:p>

title: An in situ atmospheric-pressure dielectric barrier discharge setup for time-resolved synchrotron characterisation of cerium metal-organic frameworks
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In situ investigation of plasma-material interactions are essential for understanding material stability and transformation mechanisms under non-thermal plasma (NTP) conditions. Nevertheless, such studies remain challenging due to the limited availability of plasma reactors compatible with synchrotron-based structural and spectroscopic techniques. Here, we present the design, construction, and characterisation of a dedicated in situ atmospheric-pressure dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) reactor enabling quasi-simultaneous X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) during plasma exposure.The compact reactor integrates a quartz discharge tube, an exchangeable powder sample holder, a controlled gas-flow system, and aligned driven and grounded electrodes. The geometry ensures that the reactive gas stream passes directly through the sample while maintaining optical and X-ray access. Stable plasma operation is achieved at 20.8 kHz and peak-to-peak voltages up to 14 kV with various gas mixtures. Electrical diagnostics based on current-voltage measurements and Lissajous analysis quantify discharge power, transferred charge, and effective plasma capacitance, confirming reproducible and tunable plasma conditions. Optical imaging and thermocouple measurements further validate discharge position in relation to the sample and provide temperature control up to 200 °C. &#xD;Compatibility with synchrotron radiation investigation is demonstrated at a dedicated beamtime at ESRF (BM23) through time-resolved transmission XAS and XRD measurements. As a proof of concept, cerium-based metal–organic frameworks, Ce-CAU-41 and -44, were investigated, illustrating the capability of the setup to track plasma-induced structural and chemical changes in real time. The developed reactor provides a robust and flexible tool for in situ synchrotron studies of plasma-driven processes and enables mechanistic investigations of material transformations under atmospheric-pressure plasma conditions.</jats:p>

Engineered to Trigger Virus-like Particle
Disassembly
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>A molecular delivery system needs to release, as well as package, cargo. In previous work, technology has been described for packaging cargo into virus-like particles (VLPs) based on the Hepatitis B Virus capsid. Here, we describe a panel of dansyl maleimides (DM) designed to trigger VLP disassembly in response to a reducing environment. The VLP is stabilized by protein–protein interactions and also disulfide cross-links between the C-terminal cysteine of each capsid protein (Cp). The DM molecules react with a second cysteine, buried at the Cp-Cp interface. The DMs, of varying size, disrupt Cp-Cp interactions, leaving VLPs held together primarily by disulfide cross-links. Introduction of β-mercaptoethanol (βME), emulating the reducing environment of the cytoplasm, results in the disassembly of the DM-labeled VLPs. The most effective DM binds VLPs slowly, destabilizes them more than other DMs, and leads to rapid disassembly; with this DM, labeling as few as 50% of available sites led to disassembly. Cargo-loaded DM-labeled VLPs also showed complete disassembly when incubated with βME. This work outlines a strategy for future development of VLPs as nanocontainers that are responsive to the environment.</jats:p>

title: Plasmin promotes human dendritic cell endocytosis of dead cancer cells and T cell activation
abstract: <jats:p>Presentation of antigen from necrotic cancer cells within tumour microenvironments to T cells requires efficient uptake by DCs. However, intact necrotic tumour cells present physical barriers to direct endocytosis. Here, we investigate the non-canonical role of the serine protease plasmin and its regulatory network in tumour cell endocytosis by human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (mDCs) and downstream T cell stimulation. Pre-treating heat-killed melanoma cells with plasmin significantly enhanced their endocytosis by mDCs, an effect reversed by the physiological inhibitor α2-antiplasmin. Live-cell imaging and flow cytometry demonstrated that mDCs predominantly internalise micron-scale cellular debris rather than whole cells, and that plasmin activity “digests” dead-cell particles, thereby enabling uptake of particles of optimal diameter (∼1-3 μm). Enhanced endocytosis directly translated to increased CD4+ T cell activation. Furthermore, both heat-killed melanoma cells and mDCs functioned as lysine-dependent plasminogen-binding surfaces capable of generating localised proteolytic activity. Plasmin treatment modestly reduced DC cell-surface PD-L1 expression and altered specific inflammatory cytokines. These findings reframe plasmin as a modulator of immune-tumour interactions and highlight important methodological considerations regarding serum-derived proteases in experimental immunology.</jats:p>

title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes attenuate fibrotic stricture remodeling through the let-7i -5p/TGFBR1 axis
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Urethral stricture is a common and debilitating urological condition in which fibrosis narrows the urethral lumen. Recurrence after surgical repair is frequent, and no antifibrotic pharmacotherapy has been established. Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) show antifibrotic activity in several organ systems, but whether they act in urethral fibrosis, and by what mechanism, had not been examined.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We isolated and characterized hUC-MSC-EVs and tested them in primary human urethral fibroblasts (UFBs) stimulated with TGF-β1 and in a rat model of trauma-induced urethral stricture. Small RNA sequencing was used to profile the EV miRNA cargo, and the role of let-7i-5p was examined by gain- and loss-of-function experiments, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and let-7i-5p-depleted EVs (KD EVs), both
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      .
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      hUC-MSC-EVs dose-dependently suppressed TGF-β1-induced UFB proliferation, migration and myofibroblast differentiation and lowered α-SMA and Collagen I expression, with reduced Smad2/3 phosphorylation. Periurethral injection in rats significantly reduced urethral wall hyperechogenicity, luminal narrowing, submucosal collagen deposition and profibrotic protein expression at the 4-week postoperative endpoint. Small RNA sequencing placed let-7i-5p among the most abundant miRNAs packaged in hUC-MSC-EVs, and this miRNA was efficiently transferred to recipient UFBs. let-7i-5p bound the 3′-UTR of TGFBR1 and suppressed TGFBR1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels. Depleting let-7i-5p from EVs with an inhibitor largely abolished their antifibrotic activity
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      , linking EV-delivered let-7i-5p to suppression of the TGFBR1/Smad2/3 signaling axis.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results identify hUC-MSC-EVs as an injectable, cell-free antifibrotic candidate for urethral stricture and let-7i-5p as a cargo on which their activity depends.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Pseudocapacitive Charge Storage in Perovskite Oxides as a Function of Particle Size: Case Study of SrFe0.5Co0.5O3–δ
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Systematic trends in anion-based pseudocapacitive properties are demonstrated for a perovskite oxide SrFe0.5Co0.5O3–δ, prepared using four different synthesis methods that result in a gradual decrease of the particle size. The mechanism of the pseudocapacitive charge storage, involving the hydroxide adsorption and oxide anion intercalation, is confirmed using ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and X-ray diffraction. The latter shows a decrease in the unit cell volume of the material in the charged state compared to the zero-potential state, as confirmed by Rietveld refinements. The XPS studies at both the zero-potential and charged states demonstrate the oxidation of iron and cobalt upon charging, consistent with the oxide intercalation. The essential role of hydroxide adsorption in initiating the oxide intercalation process is confirmed by comparative experiments in KOH and KNO3. The four synthesis methods lead to products that show a systematic increase in pseudocapacitive properties as the particle size decreases progressively from the solid-state synthesis (SS) product to those of sol–gel (SG), autocombustion (AC), and polymeric-steric entrapment (PSE). The contributions from diffusive and capacitive processes to electrochemical properties are also evaluated for the four samples. We note that this study is not aimed at maximizing the reported capacity; instead, its objectives are the elucidation of fundamental mechanisms and the impact of synthetic control of the particle size on pseudocapacitive properties, providing foundational insight into this process.</jats:p>

title:
Properties of Ω
                    <sub>ccb</sub>
                    and Ω
                    <sub>bbc</sub>
                    baryons in a quark-diquark model
journal: Journal of Physics G: Nuclear and Particle Physics
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this work, we investigate the mass spectra and radiative transitions of Ω
                    <jats:sub>ccb</jats:sub>
                    and Ω
                    <jats:sub>bbc</jats:sub>
                    baryons within a relativistic screened potential model using the quark-diquark approximation to capture key aspects of their internal structure. The model describes the S-, P -, and D-wave excitations, provides corresponding mass predictions, and offers a comparison with other theoretical approaches. Our findings suggest that excitations involving the diquark occur at lower energies than those requiring relative motion between the quark and diquark, challenging conventional assumptions about the rigidity of heavy diquark systems. Analysis of radiative decays of these states, shows that spin-flip transitions within the same orbital multiplet are suppressed, while transitions involving orbital or radial changes dominate with significantly larger widths. The model offers subtle distinctions in excitation dynamics and highlights its value for future studies and for interpreting potentially upcoming experimental results on triply heavy baryons.
                  </jats:p>

title: Cell Wall Polymers Exert Distinct Effects on Mucilage Architecture and Adhesion to Help Seeds Attach to Substrates
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Reforestation efforts are often constrained by low seed survival under harsh environmental conditions due to seed displacement from suitable microsites. Myxospermous seeds produce mucilage that promotes post‐dispersal attachment and water retention, thereby enhancing seed establishment. Here, we investigated the biological factors governing mechanical attachment across four myxospermous species,
                    <jats:italic>Ocimum basilicum</jats:italic>
                    (basil),
                    <jats:italic>Salvia hispanica</jats:italic>
                    (chia),
                    <jats:italic>Plantago ovata</jats:italic>
                    (psyllium), and
                    <jats:italic>Linum usitatissimum</jats:italic>
                    (flax), which occupy diverse ecological environments. We used light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy, enzymatic treatments, physical characterization methods, and functional attachment assays to investigate the mechanisms underlying mucilage‐mediated seed attachment on heterogeneous surfaces. We found variation among mucilage‐mediated seed attachments under applied hydrostatic pressure. Enzymatic treatments revealed that pectin removal causes a marked loss of adhesion across all species. However, psyllium mucilage, which possesses hemicellulosic networks, showed stronger attachment than pectin‐rich flax mucilage on rough and porous substrates. Notably, mucilage could be transplanted to non‐myxospermous seeds, conferring functional attachment capabilities. Together, our results show that species‐specific mucilage properties generate distinct modes of attachment across diverse substrates, driven by differences in polysaccharide composition and fibrillar architecture. These findings link mucilage molecular structure to seed resilience and reveal an adaptive mechanism enabling seeds to persist in heterogeneous environments.
                  </jats:p>

Multi-omics analysis and experimental validation identify ARG2 as a potential metabolic regulator linking metabolic dysregulation to inflammatory cell death in sepsis-induced acute lung injury
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (SI-ALI) is a life-threatening complication of sepsis that is often difficult to diagnose early due to the lack of effective diagnostic methods. Although a strong link has been established between metabolic reprogramming and immune dysfunction, the role of metabolic changes in inflammatory cell death and pulmonary immune dysregulation in SI-ALI remains unclear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We analyzed transcriptomic datasets from multiple cohorts in the GEO database and applied Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) to identify pathway alterations. Three machine learning algorithms were utilized to screen for metabolism-related genes (MRGs) with diagnostic potential. To further investigate the core diagnostic gene, we performed virtual knockout analyses, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Finally,
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                      experiments, coupled with lipidomic analysis, were conducted to validate gene expression patterns, functional mechanisms, and the efficacy of targeted drug interventions.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      GSEA revealed prominent changes in metabolic pathways and cell death-related processes in SI-ALI. A four-gene signature comprising ARG2, FTH1, TSC1, and GNMT was established, which demonstrated good diagnostic performance and was validated in clinical samples. ARG2 was identified as the core gene of the diagnostic signature, and its expression was positively correlated with pro-inflammatory immune cell populations in SI-ALI. Virtual knockout analyses of ARG2 revealed alterations in inflammatory pathways, particularly those related to neutrophil chemotaxis and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. Tacedinaline was identified as a potential ARG2-targeting compound, with interactions supported by molecular docking and dynamics simulations. Experiments demonstrated that ARG2 inhibition and Tacedinaline treatment attenuated inflammatory responses and pulmonary endothelial barrier dysfunction
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      , while reducing lung injury and neutrophil infiltration
                      <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                      . Additionally, lipidomic analysis showed that ARG2 knockdown reduced inflammatory responses and intracellular ceramide accumulation, suggesting an association between ARG2 and sphingolipid remodeling.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Overall, we identified a novel four-gene metabolic signature with diagnostic potential for SI-ALI. Our findings indicate that ARG2 is closely associated with cell death-related processes and immune dysregulation. These results not only provide new insights into the metabolic and immune mechanisms underlying SI-ALI but also highlight ARG2 and its targeted compound, Tacedinaline, as promising avenues for therapeutic intervention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Analyses of plasma protein levels in relation to body composition in the UK Biobank
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Excess fat mass is causally linked to multiple diseases, but the use of existing therapies, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, is limited by varying effects and common side effects, including loss of fat-free mass. We aimed to identify proteins associated with fat mass, but ideally not also associated with fat-free mass, as potential drug targets for alternative therapeutic strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We used UK Biobank data on plasma levels of 3K proteins (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 35K) and fat and fat-free mass (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 368K). We applied a machine learning procedure to select proteins for downstream
                      <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>
                      Mendelian randomisation analyses, which estimated associations of genetically predicted protein levels with fat mass. These were followed by colocalisation analyses to assess shared causal genetic variants and further
                      <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>
                      Mendelian randomisation analyses to assess associations with fat-free mass.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Here we present evidence on the associations of genetically predicted levels of 21 proteins with fat mass, including five which also colocalise with the trait (AGER, CRIM1, DNER, NEFL, and PRRT3). Seven of the 21 proteins have no clear association with fat-free mass, and ADM has an association with fat-free mass opposite in direction to its association with fat mass, suggesting that modulating these proteins may be less likely to also lower fat-free mass. Two proteins, AGER and ADM, have been investigated in advanced-stage clinical trials for indications unrelated to adiposity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings support prioritising several proteins for further research as potential drug targets for fat mass reduction. They highlight proteins that may help diversify therapy options beyond glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and suggest possible repurposing opportunities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

Physics-Based Calibration of the Fiber Bragg Grating Temperature Response via Particle Swarm Optimization
journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Engineering & Technology
abstract: <jats:p>Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors are widely used for temperature monitoring because of their compact size, wavelength-encoded response, corrosion resistance, multiplexing capability, and immunity to electromagnetic interference. However, the accuracy of physics-based FBG models depends strongly on the thermal and optical parameters adopted in the simulation. This study developed a MATLAB-based physics-driven framework for calibrating the temperature response of a uniform silica FBG using particle swarm optimization (PSO). The model was formulated from the Bragg condition and incorporated temperature-dependent variations in effective refractive index and grating period through the thermo-optic and thermal-expansion coefficients. A published 17-point temperature–wavelength dataset spanning approximately 9.49–90.34 °C was digitized for model calibration and comparison. The extracted experimental sensitivity was 9.9450 pm/°C, compared with 10.13 pm/°C reported in the source study. The baseline model predicted a sensitivity of 14.1799 pm/°C, with RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R² values of 0.20353 nm, 0.17446 nm, 43.90%, and 0.3151, respectively. Following PSO calibration, the predicted sensitivity decreased to 9.8888 pm/°C, differing by only 0.57% from the extracted experimental value. The calibrated model achieved an RMSE of 0.00521 nm, MAE of 0.00405 nm, MAPE of 1.38%, and R² of 0.99955. These results demonstrate that bounded PSO calibration can substantially improve agreement between a transparent physics-based FBG model and experimental data. Because the same dataset was used for parameter estimation and performance assessment, the results represent in-sample calibration performance rather than independent predictive validation.</jats:p>

title: Clinicopathologic significance of PD-L1 expression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      Programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a protein that, when interacting with its receptor programmed cell death protein 1, functions as a negative regulator of the antitumor T-cell-mediated immune response. The prognostic significance of PD-L1 expression in renal cell carcinoma has been examined in previous studies; however, the results remain controversial. The clinicopathologic associations of PD-L1 expression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma were evaluated in 242 cases. PD-L1 immunoreactivity (using anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody, clone ZR3) was assessed separately in tumor cells and tumor-infiltrating immune cells (TIICs). PD-L1 positivity in cancer cells was defined as the presence of a membranous immunostaining pattern of any intensity in ≥ 1% of the corresponding cells, while PD-L1 positivity in TIICs was defined as membranous or cytoplasmic staining observed in ≥ 1% of the immune cells at any intensity. Associations with prespecified clinicopathologic variables were analyzed with appropriate categorical or continuous-data tests and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan–Meier analysis. PD-L1 positivity was detected in tumor cells in 26.4% of specimens and in TIICs in 48.3% of specimens. After false-discovery-rate correction, tumor cells PD-L1 status was associated with tumor-size category, pathologic T stage, WHO/International Society of Urological Pathology grade, tumor necrosis, and sarcomatoid and rhabdoid transformation, while TIICs PD-L1 status was associated only with WHO/International Society of Urological Pathology grade. Kaplan–Meier analysis showed no significant difference in OS according to tumor cells PD-L1 expression (log-rank
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = .2925) or TIICs PD-L1 expression (log-rank
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = .9748). Compartment-specific PD-L1 expression showed exploratory associations with selected clinicopathologic characteristics; however, neither tumor cells nor TIICs PD-L1 expression was associated with OS. These findings do not establish an independent prognostic role for PD-L1 expression and warrant external validation.
                    </jats:p>

title: Impact of non-Maxwellian κ velocity distributions on the direct detection of light dark matter
journal: Journal of Physics G: Nuclear and Particle Physics
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We investigate the impact of non-Maxwellian dark matter velocity distributions on the direct detection of light dark matter particles using silicon and germanium solid-state detectors at the Modane underground laboratory. Deviations from thermal equilibrium in the  galactic dark matter halo are modeled with a generalized kappa distribution, and we calculate annual modulation signals and predicted mean interaction event rates for dark matter masses. We find that the interaction event rate depends strongly on both the dark matter mass and the $\kappa$ index, especially in the sub-GeV regime where detectable nuclear recoils are highly sensitive to the high-velocity tail of the velocity distribution. Finite kappa distributions yield higher interaction event rates for low-mass dark matter particles, whereas the Maxwellian limit becomes increasingly favored as the dark matter mass increases. The predicted interaction event rate in the nearly Maxwellian limit ($\kappa=60$) is approximately 5.8 times larger than that obtained for a strongly non-equilibrium halo ($\kappa=1.6$). We identify an optimal $\kappa$ value, denoted by $\kappa_{\rm max}$, that maximizes the interaction event rate. It follows the empirical relation $\kappa_{\rm max}=\frac{a}{\left(1-\frac{m_D}{m_{\rm as}}\right)^\beta}$, for both silicon and germanium detectors. These masses mark the transition above which the Maxwellian distribution provides the highest interaction event rate. Our results demonstrate that realistic non-equilibrium halo models can significantly modify predicted interaction rates and should be incorporated into the interpretation and design of current and future direct dark matter detection experiments.</jats:p>

title: Relativistic medium effects and spectroscopic factor systematics in proton radioactivity near the drip line
journal: Journal of Physics G: Nuclear and Particle Physics
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Proton radioactivity provides a powerful probe of nuclear structure beyond the proton drip line and offers stringent tests for nuclear interaction models. We demonstrate that the relativistic density-dependent DDR3Y interaction, combined with Relativistic Hartree Bogoliubov (RHB) densities obtained with the DD-ME2 parameter set, yields the lowest MSE among the examined folding approaches in reproducing experimental proton-decay half-lives across 43 distinct measured states in the range 53 ≤ Z ≤ 83. Nuclear potentials are constructed within the single-folding model using Skyrme density distributions (SLy7, BSk14, and SkM*) folded with the M3Y–Paris interaction, alongside RHB densities folded with the density-dependent DDR3Y interaction. Proton decay half- lives are calculated using the WKB approximation. The role of the attractive component of the NN interaction in determining the depth of the potential pocket is analyzed in detail, with particular attention to high-angular-momentum (lp = 5) emitters for which the Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization condition provides a consistency check on independently assigned proton configurations and potential pockets, with renormalization defined relative to the adopted unscaled interaction and no universal upper bound of unity. A new empirical spectroscopic factor (Sp) formula incorporating four variables (decay energy, angular momentum, isospin asymmetry, and quadrupole deformation) is proposed as a principal result of this work. The formula is calibrated empirically within the DDR3Y(DD-ME2) framework and introduces a term coupling angular momentum to the decay-energy scale, with deformation dependence that may include omitted barrier effects. When applied to DDR3Y half-lives, the formula achieves training MSE = 0.1393 and SD = 0.3777; fixed-form leave-one-out cross-validation gives MSE = 0.1616, compared with 0.2304 for the Universal Decay Law for Protons (UDLP). The Qp-value sensitivity is reported for each measured state, spanning 0.63–2.37 decades per 0.1 MeV, identifying three sensitivity groups and the mass measurements most critical for improving predictive power. Half-lives for 12 unobserved or unquantified proton emitters near the drip line are predicted, with local barrier uncertainty estimates derived from Qp-value sensitivity.</jats:p>

title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cell Therapy for Acute Graft-Versus-Host Disease: Timing, Disease Context, and Biomarkers as Determinants of Clinical Response
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose of Review</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is a therapy for hematological malignancies and inherited disorders. However, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as a cellular therapy because of their immunomodulatory and tissue-repair properties, although clinical responses have been inconsistent. This review examines evidence supporting MSC use for GVHD, focusing on treatment timing, disease stage and severity, patient characteristics, MSC product properties, and biomarkers predicting response.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Recent Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>MSCs modulate innate and adaptive immunity, including T cells, B cells, natural killer cells, dendritic cells, and macrophages, through paracrine mediators, extracellular vesicles, and cell-cell interactions. Clinical studies have reported activity in GVHD prophylaxis and treatment, particularly in selected patients with steroid-refractory acute GVHD (SR-aGVHD), whereas randomized studies have not consistently demonstrated benefit across unselected populations. The clinical development of remestemcel-L provided important translational evidence, culminating in FDA approval of remestemcel-L-rknd (Ryoncil) in December 2024 for pediatric patients aged 2 months and older with SR-aGVHD, the first FDA-approved MSC-based therapy for GVHD. Biomarkers including ST2, REG3α, elafin, CXCL10, IL-7, FGFR1, and immune-cell phenotypes may aid risk stratification and treatment monitoring.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Summary</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Evidence supports a context-dependent model of MSC efficacy rather than a uniform therapeutic effect. Clinical activity may depend on disease stage, inflammatory burden, patient characteristics, MSC source and quality, dosing, and timing. Future studies should clarify which patients benefit, when treatment should be administered, and which cellular or molecular characteristics predict response.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: When neuroscience meets machine learning: a taxonomic scoping review of machine and statistical learning approaches in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: <jats:p>In high-resource economies, computational neuroscience research frequently employs machine learning (ML) and statistical learning (SL) techniques. While these methods provide effective ways to analyse multimodal, high-dimensional, and complex data they are underexplored in low resource settings. This taxonomic scoping review uses a systematic methodological approach to synthesise the application of ML and SL techniques in neuroscience research in sub-Saharan Africa. In addition to discussing findings, strengths, limitations, and future prospects, the work classifies current research by neuroscience domains, applications, learning tasks, datasets, tools, and techniques. In order for African researchers to contribute to and benefit from the global computational neuroscience landscape, our review contends that low- and middle-income countries must create and augment context-specific and representative datasets and incorporate appropriate features for model training. Future studies should focus on pragmatic rather than complex modelling, external validation, reproducibility, interpretability, and utilise real-world data to determine clinical utility.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning: Emerging Techniques, Applications, and Future Trends-A Comprehensive Review
abstract: <jats:p>Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have emerged as powerful paradigms in artificial intelligence, enabling systems to learn patterns from data and automate complex decision-making processes. This paper presents a comprehensive review of machine learning and deep learning approaches, focusing on their fundamental principles, commonly used techniques, and diverse real-world applications. The study discusses core ML algorithms, neural network architectures, and the role of deep learning models in solving complex problems such as image recognition, natural language processing, healthcare analytics, and recommendation systems. Furthermore, the paper highlights the key differences between traditional machine learning methods and deep learning models, emphasizing their strengths and limitations. Recent research trends, including explainable AI, transfer learning, and large-scale data-driven modeling, are also examined to provide insights into the evolving landscape of intelligent systems. By synthesizing findings from recent literature, this review aims to offer researchers and practitioners a clearer understanding of current developments and future opportunities in machine learning and deep learning technologies.</jats:p>

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Comparison for Employee Performance Prediction: Implications for Decision Support in Corporate Learning
abstract: <jats:p>Identifying employees who may need additional professional-learning support could help organisations allocate training resources, but model comparisons in this area often omit trivial baselines and class-specific metrics. We compare seven classifiers (decision tree, random forest, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbours, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) with a rule-based and a majority-class baseline under one protocol: stratified hold-out, the same tuning procedure, paired bootstrap confidence intervals, a descriptive repeated cross-validation check, and SHAP and LIME explanations. Experiment 1 predicts a KPI label of undocumented origin for 17,415 employees (35.9% positive); it is an illustrative comparison using the label as distributed, not validated evidence about KPI attainment. Experiment 2 predicts promotion for 54,808 employees (8.5% positive), a related task from the same public source and not an external validation. In Experiment 1, learning models reached macro-F1 of 0.628 to 0.663, against 0.590 for the rule-based baseline; a depth-5 decision tree was 0.005 below the reference random forest (95% bootstrap CI −0.016 to +0.005) but was not shown non-inferior at a 0.01 margin. In Experiment 2, boosting models were best (macro-F1 0.734 to 0.739), the decision tree was clearly worse (−0.030), and only about 35% of promoted employees were identified. Associations with training indicators are not causal, and no effect on decisions was tested.</jats:p>

title: Symmetric PSO Tuning of Deep Tabular Networks versus Grid-Search-Optimized Gradient Boosting for FAO-56 Surrogate Modeling of Reference Evapotranspiration under Progressive Climatic Input Scarcity: A Case Study in Bechar, Algeria
abstract: <jats:p>Irrigated agriculture in arid regions have increased demand for accurate, low-cost estimation of reference evapotranspiration (ET0). Although the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith equation remains the reference method, its reliance on a complete meteorological record limits its applicability at automated stations with partial instrumentation, motivating machine-learning alternatives combined with metaheuristic tuning, such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). However, comparative studies typically fine-tune only the proposed model, leaving baselines at their default settings. In order to close this gap, this study creates a transparent benchmarking protocol wherein Random Forest and XGBoost baselines are independently optimized via grid search, and the two deep tabular architectures, TabNet and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KAN), receive an identical, symmetric Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) budget. Daily meteorological data from an arid-zone station in Bechar, Algeria, are used to assess the models in three more enriched input scenarios: temperature alone, temperature and radiation, and the complete climatic set. Friedman-Nemenyi rank-based testing, ten random seeds, and a single chronological split were utilized in the primary comparison. Mean test R² rose from 0.843 to 0.894 to 0.993 across the three scenarios. Adding wind speed, wind direction, and relative humidity jointly reduced mean RMSE by 75%, compared with 18% for solar radiation alone; a feature ablation of three models attributed most of this gain to wind speed, with relative humidity contributing mainly in combination with it and wind direction giving no benefit. Friedman and Nemenyi tests ranked XGBoost first in S1 and S2. Under the full feature set, PSO-tuned TabNet matched XGBoost's average rank exactly (1.9 for both), and their pairwise comparison was non-significant (p = 1.000), indicating no detected difference in central tendency rather than demonstrated equivalence. These rank-based results are conditional on the seed set. An expanding-window diagnostic (one pass per fold) revealed that both top performing models gave strong performance with a mean R2 value of 0.972 for XGBoost and 0.907 for the PSO tuned TabNet model. However, PSO tuning led to an obvious decrease in accuracy for the first fold compared to XGBoost (R² =0.663 vs. 0.952). These findings indicate that a grid-search-tuned gradient boosting model remains difficult to outperform under constrained inputs, and that metaheuristic tuning benefits deep tabular architectures conditionally rather than universally.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning Enabled System for Health Impact Assessment of Soft Drink Consumption Using Ensemble Learning Technique
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>Soft drinks, often high in added sugars, have raised significant public health concerns due to
their association with adverse health effects such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and
cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study is to investigate the health impact of soft drink
consumption, particularly focusing on the implications of excessive sugar intake. To address
this concern, we employed four Ensemble Learning approaches to assess the health risks
associated with soft drink consumption, specific Ensemble Learning approaches such as
LightGBM, CatBoost, XGBoost, and Random Forest we adopted. Our findings indicate that
older individuals may not require as much soft drink consumption, and the general population
should limit their daily intake to a single bottle, approximately 35g per day. The study reveals
that using Ensemble Learning techniques, including LightGBM, CatBoost, XGBoost, and
Random Forest, yielded promising results, with CatBoost emerging as the top-performing
model with a model accuracy score of 97%, surpassing the performance of Random Forest and
XGBoost algorithms. The research reveals the importance of limiting the consumption of
sugary beverages and opting for healthier alternatives to mitigate the risk of adverse health
outcomes associated with excessive sugar consumption. Overall, our findings contribute
valuable insights into understanding the health implications of soft drink consumption and
highlight the efficacy of Ensemble Learning approaches in assessing and addressing public
health concerns. This study provides actionable recommendations for individuals and health
organizations to promote healthier dietary habits and mitigate the risk of sugar-related health
complications, emphasizing the importance of evidence-based interventions in safeguarding
public health.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction and Optimization of Mechanical Specific Energy in Drilling Operations: A Gas Field Case Study in Romania
abstract: <jats:p>Drilling optimization in complex geological environments requires efficient control of operational parameters and energy consumption. This study presents a data-driven workflow for Mechanical Specific Energy (MSE) prediction and optimization using Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) models applied to drilling data from a gas field in southwestern Romania. Operational parameters, including weight on bit (WOB), rotary speed (RPM), flow rate, torque, and rate of penetration (ROP), were integrated to capture the nonlinear relationship between drilling conditions and MSE behavior. The results demonstrated that all developed models successfully predicted MSE under variable drilling conditions. Among the evaluated models, the Random Forest model achieved the highest prediction accuracy, while the ANN model showed strong generalization capability. Furthermore, an optimal operational window associated with reduced MSE, improved drilling efficiency, and stable drilling conditions was identified. The proposed workflow provides a practical framework for drilling optimization and supports the implementation of intelligent real-time drilling advisory systems for operational decision-making.</jats:p>

title: Deep-Feature Fusion and Hybrid Machine Learning for Canine Dermatological Image Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Automated classification of canine dermatological images is challenging because visually overlapping lesions, uncertain repository labels, and repeated or transformed source photographs can influence performance estimates. This study evaluated fixed ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet201, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0 features, alone and in fusion, with support vector machine (SVM), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and logistic regression classifiers for six repository-provided categories. Transformation-robust source auditing yielded 3088 images: 2862 development images from 864 source groups and a source-group-separated held-out internal test set of 226 images from 226 groups. Model selection used five-fold source-group-aware outer cross-validation with source-group-aware inner grid search. DenseNet201–EfficientNetB0 + SVM achieved the highest mean outer-fold balanced accuracy (0.9462 ± 0.0174), while triple fusion was comparable (0.9449 ± 0.0142) with a larger feature representation. On the held-out internal test set, accuracy was 0.8319 (95% CI 0.7832–0.8805), balanced accuracy was 0.7806 (0.7219–0.8384), and macro F1 was 0.7871 (0.7234–0.8432). Independent, clinically annotated external validation remains necessary to assess generalizability. These findings highlight the value of source-aware evaluation and parsimonious feature fusion when assessing multiclass canine dermatological image classification using repository-based datasets.</jats:p>

title: Forecasting High Electricity Demand Using Explainable Machine Learning
journal: Balkan Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The objective of this study was to predict the onset of high demand, the highest half-hourly average power, and the total duration of high demand over the next two hours using historical electricity consumption data from residential households. Half-hourly measurements from 2013 for 200 standard-tariff residential households selected from the Low Carbon London dataset were used. High demand was defined as exceeding the 90th percentile of each household’s average power values during the January–February period. The models were developed using data from 160 households; transfer performance was evaluated on the 40 households not included in model training. The process was divided into a training period (March–June), model selection in July, calibration of prediction intervals in August, and a testing period (September–December). The selected models were retrained using March–July data. Separate models were built for the three targets; Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB), XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared against a weekly seasonal reference. Model selection was initially based on average precision (AP) for the target and mean absolute error (MAE) for power and duration. For the residential units used in the training, the HistGB model selected during the testing period produced an AP of 0.4183; the CatBoost models produced an MAE of 0.2704 kW for power and 9.2361 minutes for duration. The contributions of historical consumption and calendar features to the model predictions were examined using the SHAP method. In the early warning evaluation, 78.81% of relevant events in known residential units were detected in advance; 60.93% of early warnings were identified as false alarms. The improvement in duration prediction relative to a reference that yields a duration of zero in every window remained limited. The findings indicate that the approach could contribute to monitoring residential demand; however, the burden of false alarms and the limited success in duration prediction must be taken into account from a practical standpoint.</jats:p>

title:
Disentangling the Effects of Sea Surface Temperature and CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    in Global Machine Learned Weather‐Climate Emulators
journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    While previous versions of the Ai2 Climate Emulator (ACE) have been trained with CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    as a forcing, they are only accurate within a narrow range of scenarios, for example, climate over the last 80 years forced by observed sea surface temperature (SST), sea ice, and CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (AMIP), or equilibrium or near‐equilibrium climates with CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    concentrations ranging from 1× to 4× that of the present day. Attempting to simulate climate forced by AMIP SST perturbed by +4 K, or the response to an abrupt quadrupling of CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , results in unphysical behavior. We attribute this to these models being trained on data sets where the SST and CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    are correlated, limiting their ability to accurately learn their separate effects. In this study we introduce a new class of “random‐CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ” reference simulations where the SST and CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    are prescribed to vary independently. We train ACE on a balance of AMIP, equilibrium‐climate, and random‐CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    data, with a total energy conservation constraint for improved interpretability. It is data‐efficient and not only accurately emulates its reference model in scenarios in which previous models excelled, but also scenarios like AMIP +4 K and slab‐ocean‐coupled abrupt 4 × CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    where they did not. However, it is not yet a full‐fledged AI climate model; it has simplified or prescribed representations of other Earth system components like the ocean, land, and sea ice, and it does not expose other known climate drivers as forcings. As configured here, it also relies solely on physics‐based model output for training data, inheriting that model's observational biases.
                  </jats:p>

title: Proxy-Label Reconstruction and Baseline Testing in LPBF Thermography Machine Learning
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Image-based machine learning is now common in additive manufacturing moni- toring, but high accuracy is hard to interpret when the label is computed from the same image given to the model. This paper studies that problem with the public NIST AM-Bench 2022 Time-Above-Melt (TAM) thermography data for LPBF of IN718. We define a two-class Low-Coverage/High-Coverage task from the fraction of nonzero TAM pixels and build 936 layer images from three repeat builds. The primary split keeps builds separate: B6 for training, B7 for validation, and B8 for testing. Deep image classifiers are compared with shallow scalar-feature mod- els and with a deterministic reconstruction rule that applies the original coverage threshold directly. On B8, Swin-Small at 512 pixels and the deterministic rule each make 0 errors (macro-F1 1.000), while a linear SVM using five descriptors, two of which jointly encode coverage, makes 1 error (macro-F1 0.997). In a five-seed cyclic repeat-build analysis, Swin-Small was repeated with five random seeds for each train/validation/test assignment; the three fold mean macro-F1 values were 0.997 ± 0.003, 0.996 ± 0.004, and 0.991 ± 0.005. The result is simple but important for reporting: a build-wise split can remove same-build image leakage, yet it does not make a proxy label independent of the input image. For this task, near-perfect accuracy means recovery of a visible coverage statistic, not defect prediction or part-quality assessment.</jats:p>

title: Lassa Fever Predictive Model Using Machine Learning Techniques
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>Lassa Fever, a severe hemorrhagic fever caused by the Lassa virus, is notably prevalent in
West Africa and can be fatal if not managed properly. Effective outbreak control and mitigation
rely heavily on early detection. This study introduces a predictive model for forecasting Lassa
Fever using machine learning techniques. The research employs an extensive dataset that
includes epidemiological and environmental data collected over multiple years to construct a
reliable predictive model. Several machine learning algorithms, such as Random Forest,
Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Gradient Boosting, are utilized to analyze historical data
and predict potential Lassa Fever outbreaks. To improve model accuracy and minimize false
positives, feature engineering and data preprocessing methods are applied. The dataset was
divided into 80% for training and 20% for testing, with various algorithms—including SVM,
K-Nearest Neighbor, Naïve Bayes, and Logistic Regression—tested to build the predictive
models. The performance of these models was assessed using metrics like accuracy, precision,
recall, and F1 score. The SVM model demonstrated the highest performance, achieving
accuracy, precision, and F1 scores of 90%, 91%, and 96%, respectively. Consequently, SVM
was selected as the preferred algorithm for this research. The study recommends the use of this
model in Nigeria's medical industry to enhance diagnostic speed and reduce medical errors in
healthcare settings. Keywords: Lassa Fever, Predictive Model, Machine Learning, Support
Vector Machines (SVM), and Healthcare Diagnostics</jats:p>

title: Benchmarking Wearable Bioelectronics: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework Integrating Parametric Regression, Machine Learning, and Fuzzy Logic Across Domain Applications
abstract:
<jats:p>This paper examines how a range of factors, including hardware architecture, sensor accuracy, battery lifetime, and user satisfaction, influence the performance and applicability of wearable technology. Through a study of 29 hardware and more than 2,300 hardware-enabled outcomes, we present a comprehensive analytical model, which includes ordinary least squares regression, nonlinear Random Forest feature extraction, and Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy logic inference. The models indicate that the four main performance indicators are heart rate accuracy, sleep tracking accuracy, battery life, and consumer satisfaction. Sensitivity analysis reveals that the hardware form factor is a unique technological architecture that no other hardware form factor can substitute for. People believe that denser hardware improves electronic quality; however, our analysis revealed that the more sensors a piece of hardware has, the lower its performance is (𝛽 = −0.542, p < .001). To facilitate the practical application of the study, we have created an application suitability matrix and rules for the decision-making process across four realms of study: clinical remote patient monitoring, longitudinal sleep research, military activities, and consumer wellness. While smart rings maximize sleep compliance through lower sensor density and longer battery life, smartwatches aim to deliver higher diagnostic output with more sophisticated systems. These results show that the effectiveness of wearables depends more on application-specific sensors than on high feature versatility, which guides the design of wearable bioelectronics.

title: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Lassa Fever Prediction
journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
abstract:
<jats:p>Lassa fever is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness endemic in parts of West Africa, primarily
transmitted through contact with infected rodent excreta. Early detection and accurate diagnosis
are critical to reducing mortality and controlling outbreaks. In recent years, machine learning
(ML) has shown great potential in enhancing disease prediction and diagnostic accuracy. This
study evaluates the performance of various ML models, including Logistic Regression, K-Nearest
Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, and Naïve Bayes, in predicting Lassa fever infection. The
models were trained and tested on a dataset comprising clinical and demographic features of
patients. Key evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall (sensitivity), F1-score, macroaverage, and weighted-average were employed to assess model performance. The Support Vector
Machine (SVM) model outperformed others with an accuracy of 90%, precision of 91%, recall of
96%, and an F1-score of 93%. The findings underscore the effectiveness of SVM in developing a
diagnostic model for Lassa fever, providing a foundation for deploying AI-driven diagnostic tools
in resource-limited settings. Future research should explore integrating more diverse datasets and
incorporating additional clinical parameters to enhance prediction accuracy further. .</jats:p>

title: Modelling Loan Default Data of German Customers: Predictive Machine Learning Studies
abstract: <jats:p>This study considered logistic regression and random forest models in modelling the loan default data of German Customers. The data were randomly partitioned into an 80% training set and a 20% test set. The train set was used to fit the data, while the test set served as the out-of-sample data used to evaluate the performance of the model. On the train set, the random forest performs better than the logistic regression model across all the evaluation metrics. On the test dataset, the random forest has superior specificity, precision, accuracy, and F1-score, but the logistic regression model produced a better sensitivity. This means that the model was better at identifying a bad loan; this is, in fact, the desire and priority of every financial institution – a model that is capable of detecting the risk of loan default. In terms of efficiency, the logistic regression model produced lower variance than the random forest, which had high variance.</jats:p>

Causal Machine Learning for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity: Interpretation, Benchmarking, Validation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Causal machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach for predicting individualized treatment effects and advancing precision medicine, moving beyond the limitations of conventional one-variable-at-a-time subgroup analyses of randomized trials. A recent benchmarking study by Chen and colleagues evaluated several causal ML learners across two large trials and concluded that current methods do not yet demonstrate reliable performance for clinical application. While such applied methodological investigations are valuable, this conclusion warrants a more nuanced examination. Multiple independent research groups have successfully applied causal ML across respiratory medicine and critical care, identifying clinically meaningful treatment effect heterogeneity that prior subgroup analyses had not resolved, although these applications have methodological limitations and do not yet establish that the detected heterogeneity is robust across internal and external validation. We outline four sequential and iterative dimensions central to credible causal ML analyses: choice of learner, model training with cross-fitting, internal validation using calibration-for-benefit and rank-weighted metrics, and external validation aligned with the original causal question. With careful methodological execution, causal ML holds considerable promise for personalized treatment decisions and warrants continued development; dismissing the field prematurely risks overlooking a powerful tool for personalized treatment decisions.</jats:p>

title: AI-Based Spacecraft Health Monitoring System: A Machine Learning Approach for Telemetry-Based Health Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Spacecraft continuously generate telemetry data from onboard sensors and subsystems to support monitoring of health, performance, and operational status. Manual observation of large volumes of telemetry can be difficult and may delay recognition of abnormal conditions. This paper presents an AI-Based Spacecraft Health Monitoring System developed during a research internship at Acceleron Aerospace. The proposed prototype combines ESP8266-based sensor acquisition, synthetic telemetry generation, Python-based data processing, a Random Forest machine learning classifier, and an interactive Streamlit dashboard. The dataset contains temperature, humidity, light, three-axis acceleration, and three-axis gyroscope measurements, with spacecraft health classified into HEALTHY, WARNING, and CRITICAL states. A balanced synthetic dataset of 3,000 samples was generated and divided into training and testing subsets. The trained model was integrated into the monitoring application to provide rapid health classification and graphical telemetry visualization. The work demonstrates a modular foundation for AI-assisted spacecraft monitoring and can be extended toward real telemetry, anomaly detection, fault diagnosis, predictive maintenance, and intelligent alerting.</jats:p>

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Experimental Electronic Nose Measurements for Biopesticide Treatment Discrimination in Tomatoes
abstract: <jats:p>This study evaluated whether a compact electronic nose could distinguish intact tomatoes treated with wood vinegar or neem oil from those without experimental biopesticide application. The dataset comprised 38 tomatoes and 228 technical runs, including six additional controls measured in triplicate initially and after 16 h: three untreated and three water-sprayed. Six commercial SnO2 sensors recorded voltages during a 180 s cycle. Six classifiers were compared using identical tomato-wise nested cross-validation with three outer folds, two inner folds, and five repetitions. With 54 full-cycle features, linear discriminant analysis (LDA) achieved 97.02% accuracy and 95.72% balanced accuracy; an artificial neural network (ANN) achieved 96.93% and 95.14%, respectively. Paired conditional intervals did not establish superiority of either model. Models trained on the original 32 fruits produced false biopesticide alarms in the new controls, including 17/36 ANN predictions. Incorporating eligible control fruit into training improved matched held-out performance, mainly under the new negative conditions. The separate two-treatment task included 32 fruits. These findings support exploratory recognition of patterns associated with application and show the value of procedural controls. Small control groups, unlogged chamber conditions, and missing chemical reference measurements limit chemical attribution and external screening claims.</jats:p>
