title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Flow-Level Multi-Class Darknet Traffic Classification
journal: Asian Journal of Research in Computer Science
abstract: <jats:p>Encrypted traffic classification is a key problem in network security because encryption and anonymity technologies limit access to packet contents used for monitoring and intrusion detection. This study compares six machine-learning and deep-learning models for classifying Layer 2 darknet traffic, distinguishing among Freenet, I2P, Tor, VPN, and ZeroNet traffic using the SafeSurf dataset. After removing duplicate records and observations with missing or infinite values, the final dataset comprised 75,201 flows described by 79 flow-level features, including port and protocol fields. Random Forest, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and CNN-LSTM models were evaluated using identical stratified training, validation, and test partitions. Source and destination IP addresses and timestamps were excluded to avoid potential collection-specific information leakage. XGBoost achieved the highest test accuracy (94.78%), macro-F1 (0.9440), and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC; 0.9308), followed by Random Forest (93.50% accuracy, 0.9299 macro-F1, and 0.9136 MCC). MLP achieved 87.74% accuracy, followed by CNN-LSTM (84.84%), CNN (79.16%), and LSTM (77.13%). I2P and Tor were frequently confused, whereas tree-based models classified minority-class VPN traffic effectively. Removing the port fields lowered tree-model accuracy by 1.3 to 1.61 points without changing their ranking. McNemar’s tests on paired test-set predictions showed significant differences (all p < 0.001) for XGBoost versus Random Forest, XGBoost versus MLP, XGBoost versus CNN-LSTM, and MLP versus CNN-LSTM. These findings demonstrate the potential of flow-level features for five-class darknet technology classification, identify persistent classification challenges, and provide a baseline for evaluating generalisation to independent network environments.</jats:p>

title: Quantum Machine Learning: An Experimental Survey
abstract: <jats:p>Quantum machine learning (QML) is advancing rapidly, yet it remains unclear which artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities benefit from quantum approaches, how strong the supporting evidence is, and whether reported gains justify claims of practical quantum advantage. This bounded critical survey introduces the Quantum AI Stack (QAIS), a capability-centered framework covering ten functional areas, and applies it to 107 experimental studies first released from 2024 to 6 August 2026, identified through keyword searches of arXiv, IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library and reported following PRISMA 2020. Each study was appraised on seven weighted criteria, including comparison fairness, statistical practice, reproducibility and hardware realism, and each capability was assigned a level in a five-level maturity model. Within this corpus, quantum feature learning, quantum neural networks, hybrid quantum AI and quantum optimization have the most thoroughly corroborated evidence, much of it establishing parity rather than advantage, and no capability is deployable. Benefits that survive fair classical comparison are narrow and study-specific, including benchmark-specific accuracy gains and improvements in parameter efficiency, robustness, throughput and energy. None establishes practical quantum advantage, and null or negative findings occur at every level of evidence quality. Because inter-rater agreement was limited, the maturity assignments are provisional.</jats:p>

title: Performance of Machine Learning Models in Predicting Hospital Readmissions and Subsequent Mortality of Patients ≥65 Years
abstract: <jats:p>Introduction: In an earlier retrospective cohort study of 129,433 patients aged ≥65 years admitted to one or more of four hospitals in Calgary, Alberta, between 2013 and 2021, we identified a large number (139,829) of second through 39th readmissions. Furthermore, we also identified that mortality rates rose with repeated readmissions: within six months after the fifth readmission (12,271), the mortality rate was 60%. This article reports the next step in our research, which is to conduct a literature search to identify which machine learning methods best predict which patients are at the highest risk of readmission and death. Objectives: Our goal was to identify which machine learning methods have both the highest sensitivity in predicting the likelihood of readmission and the highest specificity in predicting a low likelihood of readmission and death. We also wished to identify which machine learning model best identifies readmissions in the subsets of patients who receive the most frequent diagnoses at discharge so that discipline-centred preventive teams can optimise care and achieve the lowest possible readmission rates. Methods: We conducted searches in Medline and Embase on 2 September 2026 with the search terms Patient Readmission/or exp Hospitalization/or rehospitalisation.mp. AND Machine Leaning OR AI AND age 65 years or older. The search was then conducted separately for cardiac, COPD, pneumonia, diabetes, stroke, abdominal surgery and hip and knee surgery. A separate search was conducted for Patient Readmission/or exp Hospitalization/or rehospitalisation.mp. AND Systematic Review OR meta-analysis AND Machine Leaning OR AI and 65 years and older. We pragmatically selected AUC scores ≥ 0.800 to identify those machine learning methods which achieved AUCs with high sensitivity in identifying the cohorts of patients that were most likely to require readmission, were at high risk of mortality, and thus were most in need of additional interventions to prevent readmission. Results: The machine learning models with AUCs ≥ 0.800 were Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, GBDT, Support Vector Machine, Graph Convolutional Network, Polynomial-SVM, Linear-SVM and Sigmoid-SVM. Conclusions: Machine learning models with AUC scores ≥ 0.800 and with high sensitivity could facilitate the identification of patients at the highest risk of readmission and subsequent mortality within six months, allowing prevention teams of family physicians, relevant consultants and visiting nurses to augment care in collaboration with patients and caregivers using interventions tested in RCTs with a low risk of bias to prevent rehospitalisation. However, even patients with lower risk of readmission have risk factors of concern. Next steps in research are: (1) Search the literature to identify studies of readmission prevention at a low risk of bias to enable readmission prevention teams of family physicians, involved consultants and a visiting home nurse to design care plans and increase care that supports patients at home and thus avoids readmissions. (2) Increase the database to 437,000 admissions between 2013 and 2024 to provide more patients on which to test the models.</jats:p>

title: Predictive Modeling for Early Detection of Cardiovascular Diseases Using Machine Learning
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death globally. Early diagnosis and
intervention are crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study explores the development and
evaluation of machine learning models for predicting CVD. The research employed a retrospective
cohort design, analyzing electronic health records (EHRs) to identify patients with and without
CVD. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, were
compared for their effectiveness in predicting CVD based on patient data. The analysis involved
pre-processing the data to ensure quality and then training and evaluating the models.
Performance metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were used to assess the models'
ability to identify patterns and predict CVD risk. The results revealed that both Random Forest
and Gradient Boosting models achieved promising results in predicting CVD. The models were
able to classify patients into high-risk and low-risk categories based on their characteristics. This
study suggests that machine learning has the potential to be a valuable tool for supporting CVD
diagnosis and risk assessment. Further research is needed to validate these findings in larger and
more diverse populations.</jats:p>

title: Comparative and Explainable Machine Learning for Coronary Artery Disease Classification
abstract: <jats:p>Accurate and interpretable classification of angiographically defined coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a relevant benchmark for clinical machine-learning research. This study compares eight supervised-learning models using the Cleveland Heart Disease dataset. After complete-case exclusion, 297 records with 13 clinical and diagnostic predictors were analyzed. Nominal predictors were one-hot encoded, binary predictors were retained in their original coding, and continuous predictors were standardized for scale-sensitive models. Preprocessing parameters were estimated using training data only and re-estimated within each cross-validation fold. Logistic Regression, a Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, a Multilayer Perceptron, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, a Support Vector Machine, and an equal-weight Soft-Voting Ensemble were assessed using a stratified 80/20 train–test split and stratified 10-fold cross-validation. Test performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, confusion matrices, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Under stratified 10-fold cross-validation, Logistic Regression achieved the highest mean accuracy (83.83%), followed by the Multilayer Perceptron (83.16%), while Logistic Regression also achieved the highest mean ROC AUC (0.9093). On the complementary 60-record held-out test partition, the Support Vector Machine and Multilayer Perceptron achieved the highest observed accuracy (86.67%), whereas the Support Vector Machine achieved the highest ROC AUC (0.9565). Tree-based feature-importance analyses and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis of the Gradient-Boosting model showed relatively large model-attribution values for the number of major vessels visualized by fluoroscopy, the asymptomatic chest-pain category, age, ST-segment depression, cholesterol, and specific thallium stress-test categories. More complex models showed no consistent performance advantage. Excluding the fluoroscopy-derived predictor ca reduced mean cross-validation accuracy and ROC AUC for all eight classifiers. In the more restrictive seven-predictor analysis, which additionally excluded thallium and exercise-test variables, the highest mean cross-validation accuracy was 78.15% (Logistic Regression), while the highest ROC AUC was 0.8315 (Random Forest). Given the small, historical, single-center sample, the inclusion of target-proximal diagnostic predictors, the absence of calibration assessment, and the lack of external validation, the findings should be interpreted as an internal comparative benchmark rather than evidence of clinical applicability or readiness for clinical deployment.</jats:p>

title: Smoking-Status Determination from Human Nails Based on Attenuated Total Reflection Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy and Machine Learning
abstract: <jats:p>Human nails are a durable, non-invasively collected keratin matrix that records exposure over months. We assessed whether attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared (ATR FT-IR) spectroscopy of intact fingernail clippings, combined with machine learning, can discriminate self-reported smokers from non-smokers. Spectra (n = 3681) from 87 donors (42 smokers, 45 non-smokers) were second-derivative transformed, truncated to the informative regions and L2-normalized. PLS-DA and a radial-basis-function support-vector-machine discriminant analysis (SVM-DA) were developed with fully nested, donor-grouped tuning and evaluated over ten repeated 20-donor hold-outs at the spectrum and donor levels. Aggregating spectra per donor improved discrimination (+0.07–0.09 AUROC). SVM-DA on all nails reached a donor-level AUROC of 0.86 (95% CI 0.75–0.98; balanced accuracy 0.77, specificity 0.91, sensitivity 0.62); PLS-DA, logistic regression and random forest reached 0.79–0.84, with no statistically significant differences. Smokers were older and predominantly male: sex and age alone gave an AUROC of 0.79; adding the spectral score raised it to 0.89, an uncertain gain (95% CI −0.04 to 0.23), and SVM-DA retained an AUROC of 0.79 in male donors only. ATR FT-IR of nails carries a smoking-associated signal, but confirmation in a demographically matched, biochemically verified, independent cohort is required before forensic use.</jats:p>

title: Ethical Considerations and Challenges of Implementing Machine Learning in Smart Healthcare Informatics
abstract: <jats:p>The incorporation of machine learning (ML) into advanced healthcare informatics systems offers significant potential for revolutionising healthcare delivery, diagnosis and patient care. However, alongside the transformative potential, this synergy raises significant ethical considerations and challenges that demand thorough exploration. This research article delves into the multifaceted ethical landscape surrounding the implementation of ML in smart healthcare informatics. This study examines how ML technologies can either reinforce or disrupt these principles, with particular attention to issues of privacy, informed consent and data security. The potential for bias amplification in predictive models, especially in underrepresented patient populations, is a critical concern, and the ‘black-box’ nature of ML algorithms can hinder transparency and accountability, making it challenging for healthcare providers to justify treatment decisions to patients. Incorporating ML into smart healthcare informatics also raises questions about the equitable distribution of benefits and burdens. This article concludes by emphasising the need for a comprehensive ethical framework to guide the development and deployment of ML in healthcare. This study advocates for multidisciplinary collaboration among technologists, healthcare professionals, policymakers and ethicists to navigate these challenges effectively, fostering a healthcare ecosystem where ML serves as a valuable tool while upholding the highest ethical standards. Ultimately, the responsible and ethical implementation of ML in smart healthcare informatics has the potential to transform healthcare delivery, improving outcomes and enhancing patient trust and well-being.</jats:p>

Assessing Machine Learning Model Stability and the Value of Hyperparameter Transfer: Effects of Sample Size and Dataset Heterogeneity
abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This study investigates two critical factors affecting the performance of traditional machine learning (ML) models: training dataset size and the impact of integrating external, potentially noisy data (dataset heterogeneity). Additionally, we evaluate the effectiveness of hyperparameter transfer. Experiments utilized three distinct COVID-19 blood test datasets: the Wuhan dataset (356 cases), used as the source for hyperparameter extraction; the San Raffaele Hospital (OSR) dataset (1,624 cases), serving as the primary target for training, testing, and creating balanced subsets of varying sizes; and the Istituto Ortopedico Galeazzi (IOG) dataset (58 cases), which was integrated to simulate heterogeneity due to its collection via different devices and clinical settings. The discussion extends to a simple TL approach in which optimal hyperparameters were transferred from the Wuhan source to OSR target models. Both Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) and Generalized Linear Model (GLM) algorithms were tested in traditional and TL settings. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity. Results show that data quantity and quality substantially influence model performance, with saturation typically observed around 450–500 observations. The addition of external, noisy data (IOG) significantly impacted specificity, particularly in GBM models trained on smaller OSR samples. Specifically, the GBM-based hyperparameter transfer learning (HTL) model demonstrated a “crossover” effect; while it initially lagged behind traditional ML in accuracy at low data volumes (0.74 vs. 0.78 at n = 50), it surpassed ML in larger datasets, reaching a peak accuracy of 0.87 (vs. 0.84 for ML) at n = 1,100. However, due to heterogeneity, this approach also exhibited sensitivity fluctuations in high-data regimes. GLM models demonstrated greater robustness with consistent accuracy levels (~0.84) and minimal variance, possibly due to their simpler structure and better alignment with underlying data characteristics. This study highlights the importance of considering both training data volume and integrity in ML and TL applications. While increasing the quantity of data can enhance performance, the unfiltered inclusion of noisy external data may degrade it. Hyperparameter transfer is a promising strategy for maintaining model reliability across varying data conditions.</jats:p>

title: Predicting Asphalt-Mixture Fatigue Life Under Multi-Peak Axle Loading: A Comparison of Machine Learning and Multilinear Regression Models
abstract: <jats:p>Fatigue cracking is a major concern in asphalt-pavement design and maintenance and is influenced by structural configuration, material properties, environmental conditions, and traffic loading. Full-scale fatigue evaluation is costly and time-consuming, while laboratory testing remains demanding, particularly for low-amplitude signals associated with long fatigue lives. This study compares five machine learning approaches—artificial neural networks, support vector regression, Gaussian process regression, random forests, and gradient boosting—with a recalibrated multilinear model for predicting asphalt-mixture fatigue life under axle-induced multi-peak loading. The models use four physically defined signal descriptors: maximum strain, number of positive peaks, normalized positive area, and average duration per positive peak. Development and evaluation employed 78 unique experimental observations and repeated nested cross-validation. The recalibrated multilinear model achieved the most favorable mean held-out performance, with a mean absolute error of 0.181, root mean square error of 0.224, coefficient of determination of 0.853 in logarithmic fatigue-life space, and a20-index of 32.1% on the original cycle scale. Gaussian process regression was the strongest nonlinear method and produced closely comparable results. However, fold-wise variability overlapped substantially, and a corrected paired comparison did not detect a statistically significant MAE difference between the multilinear model and GPR (p = 0.525). For this small, structured database, the results did not demonstrate a consistent predictive advantage from added model complexity. Physically meaningful descriptors combined with an interpretable model can therefore support preliminary assessment and help prioritize laboratory testing within the investigated domain.</jats:p>

title: Assessing Agricultural Land and Determining Crop Suitability for Optimum Yield using Machine Learning Approach
journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
abstract:
<jats:p>Machine Learning has developed rapidly and increasingly becoming significant in agricultural
domain as there is need of efficient logical practice for detecting new and valuable information
in agricultural domain. Agriculture serves as the primary economic driver and major
employment provider for the majority of the population in Nigeria. However, the sector is
vulnerable to challenges stemming from inadequate agronomic practices. This study built an
Agricultural land assessment model that predict optimum yield using logistic regression model
and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers using Python and VScode. Comparing Logistic
Regression and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classifying crops based on their nutrient
content and yield, both algorithms exhibit high overall accuracy of around 87%. However,
SVM stands out due to its consistently high precision, recall, and F1-scores across various
crops. This indicates that SVM provides a more balanced and robust performance, vital for
accurate agricultural predictions. The study also introduces a novel application of machine
learning techniques to the field of agriculture and bridges the gap between traditional
agricultural practices and modern data analytics, fostering innovation and improving
agricultural efficiency and sustainability. The study can further enhance its impact on
agricultural productivity and sustainability by Incorporate Internet of Things (IoT) devices to
collect real-time data on soil moisture, temperature, and other environmental factors, promote
improving the accuracy of crop suitability predictions. Also to extend the model to include a
wider variety of crops and explore its applicability to different climatic and geographical
regions, ensuring broader relevance and utility</jats:p>

Direct Electrochemical α-Deuteration of Secondary Benzylic Alcohols in Flow
abstract: <jats:p>A direct electrochemical method for the α-deuteration of secondary benzylic alcohols is described. Sequential paired electrolysis in a flow system couples anodic alcohol oxidation with cathodic reductive deuteration on graphite electrodes. Deuterium oxide serves as the sole deuterium source, with lithium tetrafluoroborate as the supporting electrolyte. No further molecular catalyst or soluble redox mediator is needed. The deuterated model alcohol is isolated in 72% yield with 90% deuterium incorporation, and selected substituted benzhydrols undergo similarly high labeling.Cyclic voltammetry and reaction-progress studies support an alcoholketone redox sequence. Competitive oxidation experiments reveal preferential depletion of the protiated isotopologue, consistent with isotope-dependent discrimination that contribute to deuterium enrichment.</jats:p>

A 1951–1998 Lutao coral Pb isotope record reveals site-specific, marine-integrated anthropogenic Pb pollution signals in the Northwest Pacific
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Coral lead (Pb) isotope records provide multi-decadal perspectives on marine Pb histories, but how individual records represent regional isotope histories remains an important interpretive question. We present a 1951–1998 Pb isotope record from a
                    <jats:italic>Porites</jats:italic>
                    coral at Lutao, southeast of Taiwan, and compare it with published records from Dongsha and Ogasawara in the Northwest Pacific. The three coral records exhibited substantial inter-site isotopic differences during 1953–1963, smaller differences in interval-mean
                    <jats:sup>208</jats:sup>
                    Pb/
                    <jats:sup>207</jats:sup>
                    Pb during 1964–1984, and persistent site-specific characteristics. In 1985–1998, Lutao had a statistically distinguishable lower
                    <jats:sup>208</jats:sup>
                    Pb/
                    <jats:sup>207</jats:sup>
                    Pb composition than Dongsha, whereas the middle-to-late change within Lutao itself was not statistically resolved. This contrast shows that inter-site isotopic differences need not imply an equivalent temporal shift at an individual site. Published Pb isotope reference fields are compatible with multiple possible source combinations but do not uniquely identify historical sources or marine transport mechanisms. Together, these results reveal spatial heterogeneity in coral Pb isotope histories, with smaller inter-site differences during 1964–1984, and highlight the need to evaluate the spatial representativeness of individual coral Pb isotope records before extrapolating site-specific signatures to regional historical interpretations.
                  </jats:p>

title: A weak-form discrete physical-residual PINN method for solving multigroup neutron diffusion equations
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    To address the substantial computational burden of high-order spatial derivatives, the difficulty of residual optimization near material interfaces, and the optimization stiffness associated with direct space-time training when conventional strong-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are applied to heterogeneous multigroup neutron diffusion problems, a PINN method based on weak-form discrete physical residuals is developed. Finite-element shape functions are used to construct the flux interpolation field and assemble the discrete physical operators, while the neural network predicts nodal fluxes and neural source iteration drives the coupled convergence of the fluxes and effective multiplication factor. P1 triangular elements are adopted for the two-dimensional problem and Q1 hexahedral elements for the three-dimensional problem, eliminating the need to evaluate high-order spatial derivatives of the flux by automatic differentiation during training. The method is progressively verified using the TWIGL and IAEA-3D PWR benchmarks. For the steady-state TWIGL problem, the PINN yields an effective multiplication factor of 0.9132141, differing from the finite element method (FEM) result by 0.04 pcm, while the root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of both fast- and thermal-group fluxes are below 2.4 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    . When this steady-state flux is used to initialize the FEM/Crank–Nicolson (C-N) transient calculation, the RMSEs of relative power for the step and ramp perturbations are 5.27 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    and 4.57 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    , respectively, relative to the pure FEM/C-N results; the maximum absolute relative deviations from the published POLCA-T reference values are both below 0.1%. For the IAEA-3D PWR problem, the PINN produces an effective multiplication factor of 1.0289669, differing from the same-mesh FEM result by 3.67 pcm. The RMSEs of the fast- and thermal-group fluxes are 3.008 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    and 1.487 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    , respectively. For the assembly relative power, the mean and maximum absolute relative errors with respect to published reference values are 0.1779% and 0.4647%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method avoids the dependence of strong-form PINNs on high-order spatial automatic differentiation and achieves accurate solutions of heterogeneous two-dimensional P1 and three-dimensional Q1 multigroup core-diffusion problems within a unified framework, providing a common methodological basis for differentiable solution of complex reactor-physics problems.
                  </jats:p>

title: Long-term stone recurrence following ureteroscopic holmium laser lithotripsy: Association with perioperative nursing interventions in a retrospective cohort study
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>
                      This study aimed to examine the association between an enhanced systematic nursing program and postoperative stone recurrence following ureteroscopic holmium laser lithotripsy and to identify factors associated with recurrence in a retrospective cohort. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, medical records and follow-up documentation were reviewed for 185 adults treated between January 2024 and January 2025. The routine-care group comprised 123 patients treated from January to June 2024, and the enhanced-nursing group comprised 62 patients treated from July 2024 to January 2025. Outcomes included recorded stone recurrence at 6 and 12 months, time to first recurrence, recurrence-free status, adherence, and postoperative complications. The original analyses included Cox proportional hazards regression and exploratory subgroup interaction tests. Groups were defined by calendar period rather than randomized allocation. The 12-month recurrence rate was 9.7% (6/62) with enhanced nursing versus 22.8% (28/123) with routine care (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = .031); the corresponding reported 12-month recurrence-free proportions were 90.3% and 77.2% (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = .031). Reported time to first recurrence was 10.12 ± 2.51 versus 8.46 ± 2.83 months (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = .018). Water intake, dietary, and follow-up adherence were higher in the enhanced-nursing group (all
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       < .01). Overall complication rates did not significantly differ (21.0% vs 30.9%,
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = .155). The reported multivariable model identified associations with stone diameter ≥ 1.5 cm (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.68, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01–2.81), metabolic abnormalities (HR = 2.08, 95% CI 1.23–3.52), and enhanced nursing (HR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.20–0.96). In this retrospective, calendar-period cohort, enhanced nursing was associated with lower documented 12-month recurrence and improved adherence. Given the nonrandomized design, potential secular confounding, and differences in clinical surveillance and co-interventions, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than proof of causal benefit. Larger prospective studies are needed.
                    </jats:p>

title:
High‐Performance 2D MXene‐Derived TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Integrated Optical Polarizers
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, 2D materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond the laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). The 2D TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal/chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers that achieve high polarizer FOMs of up to ∼19.3 (a record among 2D‐material‐coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield (∼98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios of up to ∼12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong potential for large‐scale manufacturing, these devices represent a solid step toward industrial implementation of 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers.
                  </jats:p>

title: Integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning with isotope hydrology to support sustainable water management
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) with isotope-based approaches has demonstrated a strong potential for enhancing the analysis of hydrological processes, tracer dynamics, system responses, and strengthening water resource management under increasing environmental pressures. However, this integration has not been fully explored and formulated yet.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To fill this knowledge gap, this paper conceptualizes perspectives on the application of AI/ML tools in isotope hydrology to promote sustainable water management. Results were developed based on the expert consultations and group work following the modified Delphi and Nominal Group Technique method. Fourteen international experts with diverse background worked together during the technical meeting coordinated by International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) (Vienna, Austria, 2025).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results and discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Diverse applications of AI/ML methods to enhance interpretation of isotope data, improve isotope-enabled modeling accuracy, and support decision-making were conceptualized in this paper. The results showed the need for developing interoperable data platforms, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration and hybrid physical-AI modeling, ensuring ethical AI/ML practices and the advancement of IAEA Global Water Analysis Laboratory (GloWAL) Network. The approach presented here has broader applicability and could be implemented across other networks and related programmes to support resilient and sustainable water resource management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: High-Current Accelerator-Driven Neutron Sources (HiCANSs): Current Projects and Perspectives in Europe
abstract: <jats:p>To provide neutrons for science and industry, various processes are applied, such as nuclear fission, spallation, fusion or low-energy nuclear reactions. With the availability of high-current proton accelerators, the latter process has gained growing interest in recent years. The prospect of access to versatile neutron sources with affordable cost and efficient and strong neutron flux has inspired many projects worldwide to establish high-current accelerator-driven neutron sources (HiCANSs). While compact accelerator-driven neutron sources (CANSs) using low-energy nuclear reactions have been used for decades, this novel class of sources, HiCANSs, would open new opportunities to access and exploit neutrons in science and industry. The most ambitious projects in this field have been developed in Europe, including the ARGITU project in Spain, the ICONE project in France and the HBS project in Germany. In the present paper, the basic physical and technological properties of HiCANSs will be outlined briefly, and the European HiCANS projects will be described. A short outlook on the future opportunities for HiCANSs in the landscape of the neutron facilities in Europe will be given.</jats:p>

title: Stable Isotope Insights Into the Trophic Role of the Invasive Atherina boyeri (Atherinidae) in Central Anatolia, Türkiye
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study aimed to determine the trophic role of the big‐scale sand smelt (BSSS) (
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">
                      <jats:italic>Atherina boyeri</jats:italic>
                    </jats:styled-content>
                    ) in Lake Eğirdir, a large freshwater lake in Central Anatolia, Türkiye, using carbon (δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C) and nitrogen (δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N) stable isotope analyses. Although this euryhaline species rarely occurs in freshwater habitats, it has recently expanded into many freshwater systems worldwide, including Türkiye. The species was introduced into Lake Eğirdir approximately 18 years ago and has been associated with the decline of several native fish stocks, primarily due to predation on fish eggs. Stable isotope samples of BSSS (boneless and skinless dorsal muscle) were collected during spring and autumn of 2010 from four stations across the lake. Mean isotope signatures of BSSS (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 21) were δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C = −18.73 ± 1.24‰ and δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N = 11.65 ± 0.71, showing little spatial or seasonal variation. The species occupied the second‐highest trophic level in the food web, with a mean trophic position of 3.51 ± 0.19. Diet composition was estimated using three mixing models (IsoSource, SIAR, and Bugalho et al. 2008) to compare methodological outcomes. All models consistently indicated that invertebrates were the dominant dietary source (IsoSource: mean 46%, range 44%–48%; Bugalho et al. 2008: 44%–49%; SIAR: mean 26%, range 12%–39%). When invertebrate prey was partitioned by taxon, crabs and crayfish were found to contribute 40%–60% to the diet of BSSS. Contrary to the stomach contents analysis, stable isotope data indicated very low contribution of zooplankton to the tissues of BSSS. Niche size analysis revealed strong seasonal variation, with SEAc values of 4.16 and 0.29 in spring and autumn, respectively, suggesting that BSSS exploited a broader range of prey when its feeding intensity is higher and a narrower range when feeding intensity is lower. This is the first study in Türkiye to investigate the role of
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">
                      <jats:italic>Atherina boyeri</jats:italic>
                    </jats:styled-content>
                    in Lake Eğirdir through the understanding of its feeding ecology using stable isotope methods. The long‐standing belief that BSSS severely depletes fish egg populations in Lake Eğirdir is only partially supported by these results, as stable isotope models indicated a relatively minor contribution of fish eggs to its assimilated diet.
                  </jats:p>

title: Feeding ecology of mesopelagic fish in the southwestern Atlantic: integrating stomach contents and bulk and amino acid stable isotope analyses
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Mesopelagic fish play key roles in the biological carbon pump and energy transfer within pelagic marine food webs. Despite their high abundance, their feeding ecology remains poorly resolved in the southwestern Atlantic Ocean. In this study, we characterized diet composition and feeding strategies via stomach content analysis (n = 151), assessed spatial, habitat, and ontogenetic patterns in trophic structure with carbon (δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C) and nitrogen (δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N) isotope analysis of bulk muscle tissue (n = 244), and evaluated baseline nitrogen isotope composition with amino acid δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N analysis (n = 30). Myctophids exhibited similar diets and broader trophic niches, with euphausiids as their main prey, whereas the sternoptychid
                    <jats:italic>Maurolicus stehmanni</jats:italic>
                    was highly specialized on copepods. Spatial patterns in δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C and δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N reflected contrasting oceanographic conditions between regions: fishes from the northern area (23-28°S), influenced by oligotrophic waters and seasonal upwelling, had higher δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C values, whereas δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N
                    <jats:sub>bulk</jats:sub>
                    and δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N
                    <jats:sub>AA</jats:sub>
                    values were higher in the southern area (28-34°S) influenced by the Subtropical Convergence. Despite the large range in δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N
                    <jats:sub>bulk</jats:sub>
                    values (3.7-13.5‰), δ
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N
                    <jats:sub>AA</jats:sub>
                    enabled us to distinguish baseline from trophic drivers of isotopic variation. Trophic position (TP) estimates indicated zooplanktivorous feeding at the third trophic level, although
                    <jats:italic>Gymnoscopelus bolini</jats:italic>
                    occupied a comparatively higher TP, and TP increased with size in
                    <jats:italic>M. stehmanni</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Lepidophanes guentheri</jats:italic>
                    . Our multi-proxy approach clarifies energy pathways leading to higher-order consumers in the southwestern Atlantic Ocean and enhances our understanding of key drivers of trophic structure in deep-pelagic food webs.
                  </jats:p>

title: Impairment-aware WDM–CPDM laser VLC with adaptive coherent DSP
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Laser-based visible-light communication (VLC) can exploit wavelength and polarization multiplexing, but amplifier, channel, and coherent-receiver impairments interact. This paper develops an impairment-aware simulation of an eight-wavelength, dual-circular-polarization link carrying a 380.16-MHz occupied orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) resource grid within a nominal 400-MHz fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR)-aligned channel. The model includes laser-diode/semiconductor-optical-amplifier (LD–SOA) saturation and amplified spontaneous emission, wavelength-dependent gain ripple, Lambertian line-of-sight loss, residual wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) crosstalk, polarization mixing, coherent-receiver noise, phase/frequency offsets, and quadrature imbalance. The receiver combines covariance whitening, pilot-estimated 2 × 2 regularized multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) separation, pilot-assisted phase correction, and damped decision-directed refinement. With quadrature phase-shift keying, the nominal net payload rate after applying a 7 % FEC-overhead factor for rate reporting is 8.527 Gb/s. In the controlled reference realization, the proposed receiver remains below the 3.8 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    pre-FEC bit-error-rate screening level through 50 m. A receiver ablation shows that both Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization and symmetric covariance whitening remove most of the reference I/Q-imbalance penalty, while the decision-directed update provides a smaller incremental improvement near the reach boundary. A separate sweep gives 17.054 Gb/s with 16-level quadrature-amplitude modulation through 16 m. The results provide a traceable baseline for joint optical-front-end and coherent-receiver design.
                  </jats:p>

Seeing the Invisible: A Hydrogen‐Centred View of Heterogeneous Catalysis Enabled by Neutron Spectroscopy
abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydrogen governs virtually every stage of heterogeneous catalytic reactions, yet its chemical identity, location, mobility, and mechanistic role are often difficult to establish by experiments. Recent advances in neutron spectroscopy have enabled direct observation of hydrogen species across increasingly complex catalytic systems, generating a rapidly growing body of mechanism insights. However, general principles of hydrogen behaviour have not been fully extracted. In this mini‐review, we present a hydrogen‐centred framework that reorganises recent neutron‐spectroscopic studies around four fundamental questions: what hydrogen species exist, where hydrogen resides, how it moves, and how it participates in catalytic reactions. This mini‐review integrates hydrogen species, spatial distribution, dynamics, and reactivity into understanding across diverse systems, and emphasises how neutron spectroscopy provides direct mechanism insights into the chemistry of hydrogen and enables discrimination between competing catalytic pathways. Finally, we discuss current limitations and future opportunities for combining neutron spectroscopy with complementary experimental and theoretical approaches to establish a more comprehensive understanding of hydrogen‐controlled catalysis.</jats:p>

Testing subsistence in the medieval lower Syr-Darya through an archaeobotanical and stable isotope approach: a pilot study
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    This study provides a preliminary assessment of the subsistence base and possible dietary patterns of communities along the lower Syr-Darya River (modern-day Kazakhstan) in Central Asia from the fourth century BCE to the eighteenth century CE, with a deep focus on the medieval period, particularly attention to the Antiquity and Mongol periods. Stable carbon and nitrogen isotope analyses of animal bone collagen (fourth-second centuries BCE and twelfth-fifteenth centuries CE) and human bone collagen (twelfth-fifteenth centuries CE) were combined with archaeobotanical evidence (fourth century BCE to eighteenth century CE) and published palaeoenvironmental data to examine subsistence strategies in these desert-oasis settings. This research challenges several hypotheses previously proposed by scholars, including Aral regressions in Antiquity due to intensive agriculture and irrigation (the second half of the first millennium BCE) and the shift to pastoralism after the Mongol Conquest (the thirteenth to fifteenth century CE). The isotope data further suggest that livestock diets were predominantly based on C
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    resources, while elevated herbivore
                    <jats:italic>δ</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N values may reflect aridity, soil salinization, or grazing and foddering in nitrogen-enriched environments. Human
                    <jats:italic>δ</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                    N values from Kyshkala are consistent with substantial animal-protein consumption, although the specific dietary sources of this enrichment remain uncertain. By providing some of the first isotope data for fish remains from the Syr Darya region, this study establishes a preliminary ecological baseline for future reconstructions of human diet in Mongol and post-Mongol Central Asia. Overall, this pilot study demonstrates the potential of integrating archaeobotanical and stable isotope evidence to critically evaluate existing models of subsistence change. Future research should apply this approach to larger, systematically sampled datasets to test these preliminary interpretations at a regional scale.
                  </jats:p>

title: Discrete-EDFA-Free Amplification: EDF-Assisted Random DFB Raman Laser
abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a simulation-based study of an erbium-doped-fibre-assisted random distributed-feedback (rDFB) Raman amplifier for long-haul wavelength-division multiplexed transmission. The proposed architecture combines distributed Raman amplification over a 50 km standard single-mode-fibre span with a 25 cm terminal erbium-doped fibre (EDF) section pumped only by the residual 1460 nm rDFB field. The terminal EDF is intended to compensate span-end connection losses without a dedicated 980 nm or 1480 nm pump source. The model is calibrated against an experimentally measured optical-time-domain-reflectometer (OTDR) power profile, and an additional 2 dB EDF-gain margin is introduced to represent inter-span losses. The study considers a single 2 dB net-gain operating point, selected by minimizing signal-power variation along the span. The optimized configuration is applied to a 50-channel C-band WDM system over an equivalent 150-span, 7500 km link with idealized per-span power reset. The simulated central-channel OSNR reaches approximately 18.9 dB after 7500 km, while the channel OSNRs remain between about 17.5 and 19 dB. However, central-channel optimization produces a strongly nonuniform gain profile, increasing from approximately 2 dB near the band centre to 6.5 dB at the long-wavelength edge. The Kerr nonlinear-product power also increases by about 30 dB between one span and 7500 km. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed architecture for span-end loss compensation, while showing that gain flattening, multi-channel optimization, system-level nonlinear analysis, and experimental validation are required before practical deployment.</jats:p>

Comparative study of therapeutic ultrasound vs low level laser therapy combined with manual drainage technique on subjects with chronic maxillary rhinosinusitis
abstract:
<jats:p>ABSTRACT 
Introduction: Chronic maxillary rhinosinusitis is a persistent inflammatory disorder characterized by impaired sinus ventilation, pain, and reduced quality of life. Conventional medical management may be limited due to poor sinus drainage and biofilm formation. Non-invasive physical therapy modalities such as therapeutic ultrasound and low-level laser therapy have demonstrated potential benefits, particularly when combined with manual drainage techniques. However, comparative evidence regarding their clinical effectiveness remains limited. 
Materials and Methods: An informal experimental study was conducted at the Department of ENT OPD, SVIMS-COP. Thirty individuals diagnosed with chronic maxillary rhinosinusitis were randomly allocated into two groups. Group 1 received therapeutic ultrasound, while Group 2 received low-level laser therapy. Both groups underwent ten treatment sessions on alternate days and received manual drainage as a common intervention. Outcome measures included pain intensity assessed using the Numerical Pain Rating Scale, chest expansion during nasal breathing, and quality of life evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-22. Assessments were performed before and after the intervention period. 
Results :
Both treatments led to reductions in pain, improvements in sinus symptoms, and increased chest expansion. Overall, ultrasound therapy produced more consistent and greater benefits, while both interventions were equally effective at the xiphoid level during inhalation 
Conclusion:
Both interventions are effective for symptom relief and improving chest expansion; however, Ultrasound Therapy appears to be superior overall compared to LLLT, making it a more effective treatment option in most measured outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Enhanced shock pressure via Teflon tape confinement: a soft conformable tamper for laser-driven shock applications
abstract: <jats:p>Soft, pliable tampers, particularly commercially available fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP), commonly known as Teflon tape, have been shown to substantially increase laser-driven shock pressure and impulse relative to unconfined ablation. These materials provide an inexpensive, readily deployable alternative to rigid or liquid confinement systems. However, previous characterizations of tape tampers have focused on idealized, single-strip configurations, leaving unresolved how practical deployment considerations, including increased thickness for durability and the joining of adjacent strips, affect shock performance. Here, we present a systematic experimental study of Teflon tape in three practically motivated configurations: multilayer stacking, partial coverage, and stitched strips separated by a controlled gap. Consistent with previous reports, a single continuous layer confines the ablation plasma effectively, increasing the peak pressure and impulse by factors of 12.0 ± 2.3 and 16.8 ± 0.8, respectively, relative to the untamped condition. Adding multiple layers does not measurably change this enhancement since the optical transmission remained nearly the same. Under partial tamper coverage, the compression response transitions over a band of roughly ±2 mm about the tamper edge, from nearly full confinement on the tamped side to essentially unconfined ablation on the untamped side. Stitched strips exhibit a strong, nonlinear dependence on gap size, with an approximately 1 mm gap reducing both peak pressure and impulse by roughly 70%. A model is developed to relate the pressure to the gap width. Our study can provide guidance for extending tape-based confinement to large scale targets.</jats:p>

title: Coaxial Monitoring of Meltpool for Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Control
journal: Strojniški vestnik - Journal of Mechanical Engineering
abstract: <jats:p>Reliable process monitoring is critical for advancing laser powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M), as it provides the process information required for corrective control actions to prevent defects such as lack-of-fusion and keyhole porosity. A promising approach for PBF-LB/M process monitoring is coaxial measurement of light emitted from the meltpool area. More than two hundred research studies on coaxial monitoring of the meltpool have been performed, but there is still no validated and reliable method for measuring a suitable variable that could be directly used as an input for high-resolution control of the PBF-LB/M process, enabling process parameters such as laser power and scan speed to be dynamically adjusted not only at the part level, but locally for individual micrometer-scale segments along the scan track. This work reviews existing research studies on coaxial meltpool monitoring and identifies potential future research and development directions toward a standard and reliable meltpool monitoring method. Meltpool depth is identified as a particularly promising control-relevant variable. With the ability to monitor and control meltpool depth, it is possible to avoid undesirable process conditions due to too high or too low energy input, which would result in defects like keyhole porosity or lack-of-fusion. However, only five studies have attempted to estimate the melt pool depth coaxially during the PBF-LB/M process. Despite these attempts, there is no sufficiently validated method for high-resolution coaxial monitoring of meltpool depth in PBF-LB/M. The potential solution seems to be in combining concepts and recent discoveries from two-color coaxial camera- and photodiode-based meltpool area monitoring approaches. Based on the existing literature and hands-on experiences with establishing and working with coaxial monitoring systems, this work also provides guidelines and lists the most common challenges for implementing coaxial monitoring of the meltpool in the PBF-LB/M process.</jats:p>

title: Laser hemorrhoidoplasty vs. stapled hemorrhoidopexy: a meta-analysis of clinical outcomes with considerations in surgical anatomy
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Hemorrhoidal disease is a common colorectal condition affecting millions. Recently, minimally invasive approaches have gained popularity for their faster recovery. However, current literature lacks a comprehensive comparison between these two methods. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares the efficacy and outcomes of stapled hemorrhoidopexy (SH) and laser hemorrhoidoplasty (LH).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus identified studies comparing SH and LH. Patient cohorts were analyzed for recovery, perioperative outcomes, and complications. Meta-analysis was performed using R to calculate pooled Odds Ratios (OR) and Weighted Mean Differences (WMD).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LH demonstrated a significantly shorter mean operative time compared to SH (25.9 vs. 33.0 min; MD = 7.14). The stapled approach was associated with significantly higher rates of postoperative urinary retention (7.7% vs. 3.0%; OR = 1.92), stenosis (4.5% vs. 0%; OR = 9.74), and longer hospital stays (MD = 16.32). No significant differences were observed regarding estimated blood loss (MD = 2.49), return to normal activity, readmission, postoperative bleeding, or overall VAS pain scores at any time point (12 h, 24 h, 1 week, 2 weeks, and 3 months). Subgroup analyses indicated LH yielded significantly lower pain at 3 months in severe cases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LH and SH showed no statistically significant differences across several reported short-term outcomes, including postoperative pain, bleeding, and time to return to normal activities. While LH was associated with shorter operative times, reduced hospital stays, and lower rates of urinary retention and stenosis in the available studies, these findings must be interpreted with caution. Crucially, the true comparative therapeutic efficacy of these techniques remains uncertain. Because relevant variables like symptom resolution, patient-reported outcomes, disease-specific functional outcomes were insufficiently assessed, while recurrence data are limited by heterogeneous and inadequately reported follow-up, this analysis permits conclusions regarding short-term perioperative recovery, but not robust conclusions regarding comparative long-term success and efficacy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Exploring theatrical subtext translation
journal: Target. International Journal of Translation Studies Target / International Journal of Translation Studies Target
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Subtext remains a vital yet underexplored frontier in research on theatre translation. This study revisits debates
					on its universality — often constrained by Eurocentric evidence — through two canonical Chinese operas,
                    <jats:named-content content-type="foreign-phrase">西廂記</jats:named-content>
                    <jats:italic>Xixiang ji</jats:italic>
                    ‘The story of the western
					wing’ and
                    <jats:named-content content-type="foreign-phrase">牡丹亭</jats:named-content>
                    <jats:italic>Mudanting</jats:italic>
                    ‘The
					peony pavilion’, and two contemporary productions (
                    <jats:italic>The West Wing</jats:italic>
                    2008;
                    <jats:italic>The Peony Pavilion — The Youth
						Version</jats:italic>
                    2004). Integrating analysis of performance, libretti, and surtitles, it examines director-translators’
					motives and creative strategies through a practice-oriented transcreation framework, showing how subtext operates beyond
					Anglo-European realist norms. Focusing on pivotal moments, the research demonstrates how ‘the unspoken’ is re-encoded through
					intermodal dynamics, where vocal, gestural, and textual cues converge with music and symbolic staging. The findings underscore
					multimodal synergy as central to conveying subtext across cultural and linguistic divides. The study clarifies how implicit
					meanings function in classical Chinese theatre, advancing theatre translation scholarship.
                  </jats:p>

In-situ Gamma Spectrometric Assessment of Terrestrial Gamma Radiation Dose Rates and their Geological Controls in the Pindiga Formation, Gombe State, Nigeria
journal: Unimaid Journal of Physics and Radiation Studies
abstract: <jats:p>This study presents a radiological assessment of the Pindiga Formation, North-Eastern Nigeria, based on in-situ measurements of terrestrial gamma radiation dose (TGRD) rates as well as activity concentrations of 238U, 232Th and 40K across 37 locations. The objectives were to establish lithological controls on dose distribution, and estimate associated health risks to residents. Results revealed considerable spatial variability, reflecting geological heterogeneity. Locations underlain by organic-rich shales and limestone of the Fika Member exhibited elevated dose rates, attributable to enhanced uranium and thorium-series radionuclides associated with clay mineralogy and phosphate nodules. Conversely, sandy beds of the Deba-Fulani Member alongside cross-bedded sandstones and shales of Dumbulwa Member showed markedly lower values, consistent with geochemical depletion in quartz-dominated lithologies. Limestones and shales areas of the Kanawa Member and sandstones and mudstones of the Gulani Member displayed intermediate dose rates, with localized hotspots linked to secondary phosphate mineralization. The mean TGRD (~44 nGy/h) was about 25% below the UNSCEAR global average of 59 nGy/h. Activity concentrations of ²³⁸U, ²³²Th, and ⁴⁰K averaged 23.7, 30.5, and 241.1 Bq/kg, all below UNSCEAR world averages, with contributions following ⁴⁰K > ²³²Th > ²³⁸U. The annual effective dose remained below recommended limits for the public and radiation workers, indicating radiological safety. The mean excess lifetime cancer risk (0.188 × 10⁻³) was about 35% below the UNSCEAR world average. However, chronic internal exposure pathways, particularly dust inhalation and food-chain transfer, remain a study limitation. These findings provide a robust baseline and underscore the need for sustained radiological monitoring in farming areas and surrounding communities.</jats:p>

Neural architecture of the jhānas: a gamma-infraslow duet with quantum overtones
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Building on previous electrophysiological investigations that posited meditative absorption (jhāna) as a radical disruption of sensory default consciousness (DCs), this study explores the underlying non-linear neural architectures and state transitions. Re-analysis of long-duration (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 18) DC-stabilized records reveals that alpha spindles index three distinct developmental stages of the first jhāna, reflecting attentional mastery through
                    <jats:italic>vitakka</jats:italic>
                    (directed attention) and
                    <jats:italic>vicāra</jats:italic>
                    (sustained attention). A broadband (0.005–150 Hz) 3D eLoreta source analysis of a major 4,000 µV relaxation-oscillation (R-O) transition into the second jhāna, confirms the active silencing of fronto-temporal linguistic networks, leading to the profound mental stillness characteristic of higher absorption states. This macro state transition is driven by a near-absolute variance concentration of infraslow rhythms localized to the midline vertex (
                    <jats:italic>z</jats:italic>
                     = 70) supplementary motor area (SMA), supported by a lateralized left-hemisphere temporal and visual-gating gamma network. As the jhāna hierarchy deepens, the brain recruits an unprecedented electrophysiological dynamic range. Spanning four orders of magnitude in time (10
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    –10
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    s) bridging the absolute physical boundaries of human neurobiology, this architecture couples high-amplitude infraslow carriers (2,000–4,000 µV) to ultra-fast gamma microbursts (100–200 µV). This coordinated gamma–infraslow duet constructs an impenetrable, low-entropy Markov blanket, actively insulating the internal cognitive field from sensory perturbation while maintaining waking alertness. Concurrently, the 600-fold deceleration of cortical rhythms at the vertex facilitates heightened synchrony with visceral neurovascular systems. At critical R-O inflection thresholds, brief (1–2 s) global high-gamma microbursts function as inhibitory sweeps across left-lateralized hubs (BA 47, BA 21/22/38), dismantling emerging inner speech to protect absorptive stability. The study further demonstrates that the jhāna hierarchy follows a scale-free trajectory distinct from the θ, α, β frequency bands of default sensory consciousness (DCs), bypassing the 1 Hz deep-sleep transition, replacing nested sensory Markov blankets with a singular global boundary at the fourth-jhāna limit—a system with intriguing similarities to noise-shielded quantum “superposition.” We conclude that jhāna consciousness (JCs) constitutes an autonomous and previously unrecognized, highly structured second-tier of human consciousness, rather than an altered state of (sensory) consciousness (ASC).
                  </jats:p>

Model Predictive Control for a Multiport 4L NPC DAB Converter Under Unbalanced and No-Load Conditions
abstract: <jats:p>Multilevel (ML) neutral-point-clamped (NPC) dual-active-bridge (DAB) topologies have emerged as a promising solution for multiport dc-dc power conversion systems. In particular, the 4L NPC DAB is a promising solution for the auxiliary power module (APM) in electric vehicles (EVs) featuring a multiple-voltage architecture in their auxiliary system (AS). By connecting three low-voltage (LV) battery modules between the 4L dc-link nodes, multiple dc ports with different operating voltages are obtained. Then, EV auxiliary loads can be grouped according to their optimum voltage ratings and supplied from three distinct-voltage dc ports. In this configuration, the main challenge is to regulate the state of charge (SoC) of the LV-battery modules. For this purpose, this paper proposes a moving-discretized-control-set model predictive control (MDCS-MPC) for a 2L–4L NPC DAB in the EV APM application. The proposed control strategy combines the adjustment of modulation angles with the use of redundant switching patterns to regulate the LV-battery modules SoC in a wide operating range, including no-load conditions in the partial-voltage dc ports. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments verify the real-time performance of the proposed control.</jats:p>

Thermal Analysis and PCB Layout Optimization of a DC-DC Buck Converter
journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
abstract: <jats:p>A small DC-DC buck converter printed circuit board PCB is. Carefully improved to make it better at handling heat using a computer simulation called Finite Element Method FEM. As electronic systems need to be more reliable and have power in a small space keeping heat under control in power converters is a big problem. Old ways of designing usually find heat problems after making the real PCB, which causes hot areas, expensive changes and slow progress. Also regular FR-4 materials do not let heat move well which makes it hard to spread heat without help. In this study the main parts that make heat in the power part the switching MOSFET, the freewheeling diode and the power inductor are treated as heat sources on a FR-4 board. Initial heat simulations show differences in temperature not much heat moving across the board and serious heat problems under the parts that make the most heat. To fix these problems the PCB design is improved in three ways: making bigger areas of copper to help spread heat across the board putting special holes under the hot parts to help heat move up and down and moving parts apart so they do not make each other hotter. Simulation results show that the improved design lowers the temperature on the board makes the heat more even and makes it easier for heat to move away, from the parts. By doing this in the design the converter works better and needs fewer changes after it is built.</jats:p>

title: A Reproducible Multi-Target Computational Framework for Prioritizing Plant-Derived Natural Products in Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: <jats:p>Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is biologically heterogeneous, and plant-derived natural products provide chemically diverse starting points for multi-target discovery. Reproducible prioritization is needed to distinguish literature-supported evidence from candidate-specific predictions not yet generated. Our objective was to develop a reproducible, evidence-informed framework for prioritizing plant-derived natural products in AD and define a transparent candidate library and prespecified screening set for subsequent computational and experimental evaluation. Completed work included selection of an AD target panel (AChE/BChE, BACE1, GSK-3β and MAO-B), synthesis of a published target-specific machine-learning (ML) benchmark, curation of a 20-compound candidate library with traceable chemical identities and literature support, and selection of a 13-compound prespecified screening set. Published performance metrics were treated solely as external benchmark evidence. Study-specific model training, prospective ML screening, molecular docking, BBB/drug-likeness and ADMET evaluation, multi-objective ranking, and experimental validation were prespecified as future work and were not performed. The framework links mechanistically justified targets, published ML benchmarks, a chemically diverse 20-compound library, and a 13-compound set for future screening. The library includes evidence-rich reference compounds and comparatively underexplored scaffolds; no candidate-specific computational ranking or selection outcome is reported. This study presents an evidence-informed, multi-target computational framework for prioritizing plant-derived natural products in Alzheimer’s disease. Its methodological contribution lies in integrating a mechanistically defined target panel, published machine-learning benchmarks, a traceable 20-compound candidate library, and a prespecified 13-compound screening set within a transparent prospective evaluation strategy. By distinguishing completed framework-development activities from future computational and experimental analyses, the study establishes a structured foundation for subsequent model validation, multi-objective prioritization, and experimental investigation.</jats:p>

title: A case of massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate overdose mimicking brain death
abstract: <jats:p>A 36-year-old female was brought into hospital following a massive overdose of 100 ml of gamma-hydroxybutyrate. Unlike prior case reports where ethanol was a co-ingestant with gamma-hydroxybutyrate or its precursor, gamma-hydroxybutyrate was believed to have been the only substance ingested in this case. The patient developed a severe and persistent high anion gap metabolic acidosis and required continuous renal replacement therapy. The patient developed fixed and dilated pupils early on in her clinical course and was found to have a transient loss of most brainstem reflexes on clinical examination, thus mimicking brain death. She also developed generalised tonic-clonic seizures and received midazolam and levetiracetam for seizure control. She was successfully extubated after 5 days on mechanical ventilation and was discharged home on day 11 with no neurological deficits.</jats:p>

title: Oxidized LDL pathophysiology and potential as a therapeutic target in atherosclerosis
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Uptake of oxidized and other forms of modified low-density lipoprotein (LDL) drives formation of foam cells, a hallmark of atherosclerotic plaques. Experimental studies demonstrating the proinflammatory and cytotoxic properties of oxidized LDL have led to the concept of LDL oxidation as one key factor in both development and destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques. Such data positioned oxidized LDL as a promising target for prevention or mitigation of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Yet the failure of multiple antioxidants to reduce cardiovascular risk in large randomized clinical trials has hampered this prospect. Such null studies have stimulated interest in an alternative approach: the therapeutic potential of antibodies against oxidized LDL. High levels of IgM against oxidized LDL phospholipids are associated with lower cardiovascular risk and these antibodies function primarily through neutralization and stimulation of clearance of modified LDL. IgG antibodies against aldehyde-modified peptide sequences in apolipoprotein B-100, the signature protein component of LDL, are also associated with lower risk of cardiovascular disease but experimental studies have shown that these antibodies function by locally forming immune complexes with oxidized LDL that limit the inflammatory activity of certain plaque macrophages. A phase 2 pilot study showed that one such antibody, orticumab, reduces an imaging index of local coronary arterial inflammation in patients with psoriasis. Thus, emerging evidence supports the possibility of using oxidized LDL antibodies to limit atherothrombotic disease.</jats:p>

title: Exploring Variability in Infliximab Target Attainment and Implications for Concentration-Guided Dosing (CGD) in Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD)
abstract: <jats:p>Background: Substantial interindividual variability in infliximab pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics (PKPD) complicates dose optimization in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Infliximab concentration-guided dosing (CGD) mostly relies on the Therapeutic Window Approach (TWA). Although this approach is widely used in clinical practice, its implications in the setting of substantial variability remain insufficiently characterized. Methods: Model-based simulations evaluated the probability of target (non)-attainment across standard and intensified dosing strategies for intravenous and subcutaneous infliximab. Target attainment was predefined using a therapeutic window (3–7 mg/L) for intravenous infliximab and a threshold (≥12 mg/L) for subcutaneous infliximab. Results: Across dosing strategies, substantial exposure variability resulted in a proportion of patients remaining below the predefined targets. For intravenous infliximab, interval shortening achieved a greater probability of target attainment than dose escalation alone; for example, among patients receiving 5 mg/kg, 50.5% achieved concentrations ≥3 mg/L with Q6W versus 24.5% with Q8W. For subcutaneous infliximab, simulated 180 and 240 mg doses increased the probability of target attainment (≥12 mg/L) versus the approved 120 mg dose, in higher body weight cohorts (72.0% and 86.5%, respectively, vs. 35.5%), potentially highlighting limitations of the current “one-size-fits-all” dosing paradigm. Conclusions: In the presence of substantial infliximab PKPD variability and IBD dynamics, the predefined therapeutic window and fixed threshold may not adequately account for individual variability, potentially contributing to clinical discordance between drug exposure, predefined target attainment, and clinical outcomes. These considerations support evaluating the Target Concentration Approach (TCA) in clinical trials and routine IBD management, given its potential to dynamically adapt dosing to achieve patient-specific target concentration.</jats:p>

title: Thermo-hydrodynamic behavior of hybrid nanofluids in a wavy-cooled Gamma-shaped porous cavity under magnetic field
journal: International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat & Fluid Flow
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to investigate the coupled effects of magnetic-field orientation, magnetic-field strength, thermal radiation, porous-medium permeability and wavy-wall characteristics on natural convection heat transfer in a porous enclosure saturated with a Cu–Al₂O₃/water hybrid nanofluid (HNF). The objective is to clarify the dominant mechanisms governing thermal transport and identify favourable operating conditions for enhanced heat-transfer performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A two-dimensional wavy porous enclosure is considered, with sinusoidal cold vertical and horizontal top boundaries and G-shaped internal partitions maintained at a uniform hot temperature, while the remaining walls are adiabatic. Fluid flow through the porous medium is modeled using the Darcy–Brinkman formulation. The effects of the magnetic field are incorporated through the Lorentz-force term, whereas thermal radiation is modeled using the Rosseland diffusion approximation. The resulting dimensionless governing equations are formulated in vorticity–stream function form and solved using a second-order finite difference scheme on a Cartesian cut-cell finite difference method. Parametric simulations are performed for Rayleigh number 103 &lt; Ra &lt; 106, Darcy number 10−3 &lt; Da &lt; 10−1, magnetic field inclination angle 0° &lt; γ &lt; 90°, Hartmann number 0 &lt; Ha &lt; 50 and radiation parameter 0 &lt; Rd &lt; 5.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Increasing the Rayleigh number from 103 to 106 enhances the mean Nusselt number by approximately 324%, confirming the dominant contribution of buoyancy-driven convection to heat transfer. By contrast, increasing the Hartmann number from 0 to 50 decreases the average Nusselt number from 14.4904 to 6.9145, corresponding to a reduction of 52.2822%. This reduction is attributed to the Lorentz force, which suppresses buoyancy-driven fluid motion and consequently weakens convective heat transfer. Reducing the Darcy number from 0.1 to 0.0001 decreases the average Nusselt number from 13.8058 to 6.5834, corresponding to a reduction of 52.3142%. The reduction is associated with the increased hydraulic resistance of the porous medium, which restricts fluid motion and weakens convective heat transfer. The combined effects of wall undulation and amplitude enhance thermal performance by up to 6%, while favorable magnetic-field inclination angles increase the average Nusselt number by approximately 3.8%. Overall, buoyancy and porous-medium permeability are identified as the primary mechanisms promoting heat transfer, whereas magnetic damping represents the dominant suppressing mechanism.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides a comprehensive assessment of the combined effects of magnetic-field orientation, Lorentz-force damping, thermal radiation, porous-medium permeability and wavy-wall geometry on HNF natural convection. The findings provide useful guidelines for controlling and optimising heat transfer in magnetically influenced porous thermal systems with complex enclosure geometries.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
