title: Development and field application of 10 m ultra-large mining-height technologies for ultra-thick coal seam extraction
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ultra-thick coal seams are an important resource for high-production underground mining in China, yet single-pass extraction of seams exceeding 10 m in thickness presents unprecedented challenges in strata control, equipment capacity, and intelligent coordination. Targeting the geological conditions of the Caojiatan Coal Mine, this study investigates the key technologies and equipment required for the world’s first 10 m ultra-large mining-height fully mechanized working face. A coordinated strata control strategy integrating strong proactive support and protection with regional hydraulic fracturing (HF) destressing was established. Ultra-high-capacity hydraulic supports with a working resistance of 29,000 kN were developed, featuring a "double telescopic canopy beam + three-level coal-wall protection" structure for stabilizing the ultra-high coal wall. A 5 m³/min high-flow underground HF system was designed to weaken and destress thick hard roof strata, reducing cantilever development and mitigating strong mine pressure. A complete set of mining equipment—including a high-power shearer, heavy-duty armored face conveyor, and intelligent cluster-control system—was developed and integrated for the 10 m mining-height application. Field implementation demonstrated significant improvements in mine pressure behavior: initial weighting intervals decreased from > 150 m to 49.3 m, periodic weighting intervals remained below 25 m, and dynamic loading coefficients were substantially reduced. The working face achieved a maximum daily production of 71,800 tonnes, a monthly production of 1.55 million tonnes, and a recovery rate exceeding 95%, leading to considerable economic benefits and enhanced resource recovery. The successful deployment of these technologies establishes a technical pathway for safe, efficient, and intelligent extraction of ultra-thick coal seams and advances the development of next-generation high-end mining equipment for ultra-large mining-height conditions.</jats:p>

Pre-Wetted Ceramsite as a Dual-Functional Lightweight Aggregate and Internal Curing Reservoir for Lightweight Ultra-High-Performance Concrete
abstract: <jats:p>Lightweight ultra-high-performance concrete (LUHPC) can reduce structural self-weight, but porous aggregates may compromise strength and transport resistance. This study evaluates shale ceramsite as both a lightweight aggregate and an internal-curing reservoir. Four mixtures were compared: quartz-sand UHPC (UH), dry-ceramsite LUHPC (LUC), dry ceramsite with additional free water (LUC-ad), and pre-wetted ceramsite (LUC-pr). At 7 days, LUC-pr maintained an internal relative humidity (IRH) of 87%, versus 74% for LUC. At 28 days, LUC-pr achieved compressive and flexural strengths of 128.1 and 22.0 MPa, 4.1% and 7.8% above UH. Its autogenous and dry shrinkage were reduced by 51.2% and 32.0%, respectively. Its cumulative mercury intrusion volume and electrical charge passed were 0.048 cm3/g and 917.3 C. Compared with LUC, LUC-pr increased compressive and flexural strengths by 23.1% and 31.0%, reduced cumulative intrusion volume by 34.2%, and reduced charge passed by 30.3%. Conversely, additional free water increased dry shrinkage and charge passed. Overall, storing water in pre-wetted ceramsite provided a better balance among moisture regulation, strength, dimensional stability, and transport resistance than simply increasing free-water content.</jats:p>

title: PHONON: Silicon-Photonic Network-on-Interposer for Energy-Efficient and High Performance LLM Inferencing
journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit extreme compute and memory demands, necessitating large-scale multi-chiplet systems to achieve high-performance and scalability. In such systems, frequent off-chip memory accesses for model parameters and intermediate activation exchanges induce substantial data movement between compute and storage chiplets, making inter-chiplet communication a critical performance and energy bottleneck. Silicon photonic (SiPh) Networks-on-Interposers (NoIs) offer high bandwidth and low latency communication, making them an attractive choice for the inter-chiplet communication backbone. However, conventional SiPh NoI designs require long-range multi-hop data exchanges, resulting in degraded performance and energy efficiency, and poor scalability. In this work, we present PHONON, a novel Silicon-

                    tonic
                    <jats:underline>N</jats:underline>
                    etwork-
                    <jats:underline>o</jats:underline>
                    n-I
                    <jats:underline>n</jats:underline>
                    terposer architecture, that jointly optimizes compute–compute and compute–storage inter-chiplet communication. PHONON employs structured waveguide placement, cluster-level connectivity to storage chiplets, and optimized mapping of compute kernels to chiplets. PHONON optimizes waveguide crossings and reduces waveguide propagation losses, insertion losses, and memory-access contention. Simulation results show that PHONON reduces NoI latency and energy consumption by up to 9.4× and 28.4×, respectively, compared to state-of-the-art SiPh NoI architectures, enabling scalable, high-performance, and energy-efficient LLM acceleration. PHONON reduces the LLM-serving metrics of time-to-first-token (TTFT) by up to 1.48×, and improves tokens/sec and tokens/Joule by up to 4.9× and 28×, respectively, compared to SiPh NoI counterparts.

title: Improvement of Interfacial Adhesion and Tribological Performance of Ultra-High-Molecular-Weight Polyethylene Using Chromic Acid Treatment and Plasma-Functionalized Graphene Nanoplatelets Coatings
journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
abstract: <jats:p>Ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene is a common choice for wear-resistant applications due to its low friction, high toughness, and chemical stability. However, its chemical inertness and low surface energy limit the adhesion of functional coatings such as graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs). In this study, chromic acid etching and plasma-functionalized GNP coating were used to improve the interfacial adhesion and tribological performance of UHMWPE. Substrates of UHMWPE were etched in chromic acid for 0, 5, 10, and 15 min and then dip-coated with argon plasma-treated GNPs. Etching time significantly impacted surface morphology, coating stability, wettability, and friction behavior. Moderate surface roughness, mechanical interlocking, and homogeneity of the GNP coating were obtained for the 5 min etching condition. This condition achieved the best tribological performance, with the coefficient of friction decreasing to 0.23 and the water contact angle decreasing to 88.17°. Mechanical testing showed that the 5 min etched sample kept most of its bulk properties, with a tensile modulus of 512.8 MPa, tensile strength of 27.71 MPa, and hardness of 67 Shore D. Longer etch times led to over-roughening and generation of micro-defects, causing lower coating uniformity and higher friction. This study shows the potential of controlled chromic acid etching with plasma-functionalized GNP coating to enhance the surface adhesion and tribological characteristics of UHMWPE, and mechanical properties were largely retained.</jats:p>

title: GLP-1 dose escalation and disputed ignition interlock alcohol results: Case report
abstract: <jats:p>Ignition interlock breath alcohol devices use electrochemical fuel-cell technology to detect alcohol in breath. Although these devices are intended to detect ethanol, fuel-cell sensors also detect other alcohols, including isopropanol. Prior reports have described false-positive breath alcohol results in individuals with increased ketone body production, including a case involving a very-low-calorie ketogenic diet and another involving diabetic ketoacidosis. This report involves a 45-year-old woman prescribed Wegovy, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, who had two positive ignition interlock results within days of a dose increase from 1.0 mg to 1.7 mg. The individual denied alcohol consumption, testified regarding several years of sobriety, and otherwise maintained employment and compliance with ignition interlock requirements. One plausible explanation for the positive results is that reduced caloric intake following the GLP-1 dose escalation increased reliance on fat metabolism. This may have triggered an increased endogenous acetone production and subsequent reduction of acetone to isopropanol. Isopropanol undergoes electrochemical oxidation on fuel-cell-based breath alcohol sensors and can produce an apparent alcohol-positive result despite not drinking alcohol. This mechanism should be considered when evaluating disputed ignition interlock violations in individuals using GLP-1 receptor agonists.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Molecular control of the proton environment in phosphoric acid (PA) based electrochemical interfaces is critical for efficient proton transport and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet effective strategies for actively regulating this environment remain limited. Here, we show that Brønsted acid sites (BASs) in HY zeolite function as solid-state proton regulating centers that directly participate in and reorganize the interfacial PA hydrogen bond network. By combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, free energy calculations, variable-temperature diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (VT-DRIFTS), and electrochemical measurements, we reveal a BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution mechanism. The framework BAS proton transfers to an adjacent PA molecule, generating an excess proton defect that dynamically redistributes among neighboring PA molecules through hydrogen-bond-assisted proton hopping. The potential of mean force (PMF) along δ01 reveals a favorable free energy change for BAS to PA1 proton transfer (–0.122 eV), while density functional theory (DFT) calculations show lower electronic energies for representative PA-associated configurations, with PA2 exhibiting the lowest energy. AIMD simulations further demonstrate preferential excess-proton accommodation and dynamic redistribution within the PA network. VT-DRIFTS measurements reveal PA-induced changes in the temperature-dependent hydroxyl response of HY, while calculated harmonic infrared spectra of representative proton configurations provide molecular-level insight into interfacial proton interactions and hydrogen bond reorganization. Electrochemical measurements further show that HY incorporation reduces proton transport and ORR charge transfer resistances while increasing Pt electrochemical accessibility. These findings identify BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution as a promising molecular strategy for regulating PA-based electrochemical interfaces.</jats:p>

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in High‐Risk Patients Undergoing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion With Watchman FLX
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
<jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion remains uncertain.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">We studied 2817 patients undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion at 8 hospitals from 2016 to 2023 using registry data linked to Medicare claims. Among 2448 Watchman FLX recipients, the primary exposure was time‐varying dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) versus pooled direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)‐based therapy. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major bleeding, and device complications. The primary instrumental‐variable analysis used operator FLX preference; overlap weighting was secondary and pairwise regimen comparisons exploratory.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">
                      DAPT was associated with lower MACE (absolute risk difference [ARD], −1.5% [95% CI, −1.9% to −1.0%]; number needed to treat, 67) and major bleeding (ARD −1.6% [95% CI, −2.0% to −0.9%]; number needed to treat, 63) than pooled DOAC‐based therapy, without increased device complications. Overlap‐weighted associations with MACE and major bleeding were nonsignificant. In exploratory pairwise analyses, DAPT did not differ significantly from DOAC monotherapy for MACE or major bleeding; lower major bleeding was limited to DAPT versus DOAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (ARD, −0.6% [95% CI, −1.1% to −0.2%];
                      <jats:italic toggle="no">P</jats:italic>
                      =0.008). Most estimated benefit accrued within 6 months.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec xml:lang="en">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p xml:lang="en">DAPT was associated with lower MACE and major bleeding than pooled DOAC‐based therapy after Watchman FLX implantation. The safety benefit was concentrated in the comparison with DOAC + single antiplatelet therapy, whereas DAPT and DOAC monotherapy did not clearly differ in either outcome. These findings support randomized trials comparing DAPT with DOAC monotherapy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Digital information overload and ageing: physiological evidence, an abiotic-stressor analogy, and competing dose–response hypotheses
abstract: <jats:p>Digital information overload (DIO) is increasingly considered an environmentally mediated stress exposure, yet its physiological consequences and relevance to biological ageing remain uncertain. This critical narrative review evaluates evidence for sustained allostatic strain, adaptation and alternative exposure–response patterns, distinguishing content-defined overload from occupational technostress, general screen use, screen-emitted light and broader stress biology. The literature was collected between 4 March and 20 August 2026 and appraised according to exposure specificity, study design and measured endpoints. Occupational studies reported an inverse prospective association between technostress and hair cortisol, without significant associations with C-reactive protein, challenging assumptions of uniform hypercortisolism or inflammation. Acute autonomic responses varied with task conditions, while experimental screen-light research demonstrated circadian effects without isolating informational content. A short randomised screen-reduction study reported favourable changes in selected physiological measures, although its broad exposure definition and co-interventions prevent attribution to DIO. In a cross-sectional study, an association between social-media duration and DunedinPACE was attenuated after adjustment for body mass index, while GrimAge2 was not associated with exposure duration. Current research does not establish that objectively quantified DIO causes cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction or accelerated biological ageing. We propose the unvalidated Digital Information Stress Dose (DISD) framework, encompassing exposure duration and frequency, arousal, cognitive load, attentional capture, circadian displacement and perceived controllability. Null or weak, monotonic adverse, threshold and biphasic hormesis-like relationships remain plausible but untested alternatives. Future investigations should combine passive exposure logs and ecological momentary assessment with repeated physiological measurements, neutral and supportive digital comparators, longitudinal follow-up and controlled exposure modifications. DISD is intended as a falsifiable research framework, not an established biomarker, clinical threshold or demonstration of harm.</jats:p>

title: Acute diarrhea following the first subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab: a case report of a probable adverse drug reaction
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tafolecimab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9). Diarrhea is a recognized adverse reaction, but detailed post-marketing case descriptions with clear timing, differential assessment, and outcome remain limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Case Summary</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 51-year-old man hospitalized for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction received his first one-time 600-mg subcutaneous dose of tafolecimab (SINTBILO) at 15:14 on 13 July 2026. Approximately 7 h 46 min later, he developed abdominal pain and diarrhea occurring 5–8 times daily, with nausea and mild periumbilical pain but no fever, tenesmus, visible hematochezia or melena, dehydration, hypotension, rebound tenderness, or guarding. Stool testing showed loose yellow stool, positive occult blood and red blood cells, 0–1 white blood cells/high-power field, and a negative rotavirus test; electrolytes and liver and kidney function were normal. Stool culture and testing for Clostridioides difficile, norovirus, and adenovirus were not performed. Tafolecimab was not re-administered. After fluid replacement, montmorillonite, and loperamide hydrochloride, diarrhea decreased within 1 day and resolved after approximately 2 days, with no recurrence after discharge. Long-term stable acarbose therapy was continued without recurrence. The Naranjo score was 5, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case supports probable tafolecimab-associated acute diarrhea. New-onset diarrhea after PCSK9 inhibitor initiation should prompt precise temporal documentation, medication reconciliation, targeted microbiological evaluation, and pharmacovigilance reporting.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

baryonic expansion framework developed by the author since 1990, we examine how G is related to the proton’s mass,
radius and internal pressure. The principal findings are three. (i) Applying the author’s 1993 expansion equation to the
proton and comparing the result with the acceleration its internal pressure (≈1035 Pa) would produce in the absence of
confi nement defines a confinement leakage factor k ≈ 3 × 10-40.
(ii) G is then bound to proton quantities by the exact relation G = 4π k Pp rp

4

leakage factor equals the proton’s gravitational coupling αG ≈ 6 × 10-39 divided by a geometric factor of about 20. As
defi ned here, k contains G, so these relations are consistency relations and not yet a derivation of G. We state the condition

title: Empirical and semi-empirical methods to determine the kV exponent ( n value) for diagnostic X-ray machines
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The air kerma, and beam quality measurements were performed on 43 diagnostic X-ray machines (25 fixed and 18 mobile) that met acceptance criteria for tube potential accuracy, half-value layer, and tube output. Measurements were conducted at tube potentials from 40 kV to 120 kV using a calibrated solid-state dosimetry system at a fixed focus-detector distance of 1 m, normalized output (mGy/mAs) and half-value layer were determined at each setting of the tube potential. Two methods (method 1 – empirical and method 2 – semi-empirical) were used to derive the exponent value. In method 1, a power-law fit of tube output versus tube potential yielded an average exponent of $n$ ≈ 2.334 ± 0.118 based on the group of X-ray machines with high-power frequency generators, consistent with values reported for diagnostic systems with standard filtration [1, 2]. In method 2, the $n$ was derived as a function of tube potential by incorporating the measured variation of half-value layer with tube potential, explicitly accounting for effective filtration. This approach showed that $n$ decreases from ~2.69 at 40 kV to 2.09 at 120 kV, demonstrating greater output sensitivity to tube potential changes at lower tube potentials. Therefore, the study introduces a semi-empirical method for estimating the exponent ($n$ value) that incorporates measured half-value layer variation to account for effective beam hardening, which is neglected in conventional empirical models. This provides a practical tool for characterizing the dependence of X-ray tube output on tube protocol optimization and equipment performance assessment, applicable for quality control in diagnostic X-ray machines.</jats:p>

Artificial Intelligence in Temporomandibular Joint Imaging: Diagnostic Performance Across Input Modality–Target Pairings—A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To estimate standalone artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic performance in temporomandibular joint (TMJ) imaging across input modality–target pairings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Four databases were searched through 18 June 2026. Eligible studies assessed standalone imaging AI and supplied an exact test-set 2 × 2 table in the report or after author contact. Four pairings were analysed by bivariate meta-regression. Two reviewers applied QUADAS-3 at estimate level.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sixteen studies contributed 17 estimates. For disc displacement, magnetic resonance imaging input yielded pooled sensitivity 0.924 (95% CI, 0.859–0.960) and specificity 0.812 (0.709–0.885), compared with 0.765 (0.618–0.867) and 0.741 (0.592–0.850) for panoramic or cone-beam computed tomography input. The sensitivity difference was 0.159 and remained 0.152–0.198 in leave-one-out and replicate analyses; the omnibus pairing test was not significant (χ²(6) = 10.38, P = .110). Reference-standard relation and pairing partitioned the disc-displacement evidence identically. No estimate had low overall risk of bias, and several otherwise eligible estimates lacked exact published 2 × 2 data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sensitivity was higher when disc displacement was depicted directly on magnetic resonance imaging than when inferred from imaging that does not depict the disc. However, the cross-domain group contained only three estimates, the omnibus pairing test was not significant, and design factors were entangled. Performance should therefore be interpreted by pairing, while direct depiction versus proxy inference requires prospective testing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Advances in knowledge</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>TMJ imaging AI performance should be interpreted in the context of the input modality–target pairing rather than as a property of the algorithm alone; exact test-set confusion matrices are essential for verification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Governing Cross-Border Nuclear Partnerships: A Q-NPT Framework Analysis of the Egypt–Russia El Dabaa Nuclear Power Project
abstract: <jats:p>Large-scale nuclear energy projects depend on credible governance arrangements to support international cooperation and address institutional and societal concerns surrounding nuclear energy development. This study applies the Qudrat-Ullah Nuclear Peace and Trust (Q-NPT) framework to examine the governance of the Egypt–Russia El Dabaa Nuclear Power Plant (ERENPP). The framework comprises four pillars—Trust, Equity, Transparency, and Inclusion—with institutional alignment treated as a cross-cutting dimension. Using a qualitative single-case study design and deductive content analysis, the study examines documentary evidence from intergovernmental agreements, financing arrangements, regulatory and international review documents, official project statements, media reports, civil-society publications, and relevant academic literature. The analysis distinguishes formal commitments and reported activities from implementation, stakeholder perceptions, and demonstrated outcomes. The findings identify formal bilateral and institutional arrangements relevant to trust and coordination, alongside governance questions concerning the disclosure of project information, the distribution of costs and benefits, and the scope and influence of stakeholder participation. Although documented consultation activities and regulatory milestones provide evidence of governance processes, they do not independently establish public confidence, equitable outcomes, or the effectiveness of stakeholder engagement. The study demonstrates how Q-NPT can structure documentary evidence across the four pillars, identify cross-pillar relationships, and make evidence gaps explicit without assigning an unsupported overall governance rating or inferring causal effects. It contributes a context-sensitive application of Q-NPT to cross-border nuclear energy governance and identifies priorities for further assessment, including accessible information disclosure, meaningful stakeholder engagement, institutional coordination, and transparent evaluation of project costs and benefits. The framework offers a complementary analytical approach for examining governance in nuclear energy partnerships and informing comparative research on energy-system development.</jats:p>

title: Diagnostic Performance of Data-Driven MRI Habitat Analysis for Preoperative Prediction of IDH Status in Adult Gliomas: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-Analysis
abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) status is important for the classification and prognosis of adult gliomas. Whole-tumor MRI summary measures may obscure intratumoral spatial heterogeneity, whereas data-driven habitat analysis identifies imaging-defined tumor subregions and may better capture this heterogeneity. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of MRI habitat analysis for preoperative prediction of IDH status. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Data from database inception through 22 August 2026. Eligible studies used data-driven MRI habitat analysis to predict IDH status in adult gliomas. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model. We also performed sensitivity analyses, univariable meta-regression, subgroup analyses, and Radiomics Quality Score 2.0 (RQS 2.0) assessment. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261489645). Results: Eighteen reports were included in the systematic review, and 13 independent studies involving 1236 patients contributed to the meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.78 (95% CI, 0.70–0.84) and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.79–0.89), respectively, with an SROC AUC of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.86–0.91). I2 was 82.1% for sensitivity and 71.3% for specificity. Excluding two studies with approximately reconstructed 2 × 2 tables did not materially change the pooled estimates. Radiomics studies and studies using ≥4 habitats showed higher specificity and lower sensitivity, but their overlap limited separate interpretation of feature type and habitat number. Conclusions: MRI habitat analysis showed promising diagnostic performance for preoperative prediction of IDH status in adult gliomas. However, limited external validation and incomplete assessment of reproducibility and clinical utility remain barriers to clinical translation. Future prospective multicenter studies should further evaluate habitat stability, model calibration, and clinical net benefit.</jats:p>

abstract:

                    The objective of this study is to evaluate the influence of technological process parameters on the shielding effectiveness of conductive composite coatings, as well as to assess the adhesive strength of these coatings when applied to cement-sand plaster under conditions closely approximating those found in rural environments.

The achieved homogeneity of the polydisperse system resulted in greater resistance to external factors, with the coating retaining its original properties even after testing. Modifications to the paint composition allowed for the inclusion of additional components that bolster shielding properties and improve operational characteristics, such as adhesion to the substrate surface.

In-situ Gamma Spectrometric Assessment of Terrestrial Gamma Radiation Dose Rates and their Geological Controls in the Pindiga Formation, Gombe State, Nigeria
journal: Unimaid Journal of Physics and Radiation Studies
abstract: <jats:p>This study presents a radiological assessment of the Pindiga Formation, North-Eastern Nigeria, based on in-situ measurements of terrestrial gamma radiation dose (TGRD) rates as well as activity concentrations of 238U, 232Th and 40K across 37 locations. The objectives were to establish lithological controls on dose distribution, and estimate associated health risks to residents. Results revealed considerable spatial variability, reflecting geological heterogeneity. Locations underlain by organic-rich shales and limestone of the Fika Member exhibited elevated dose rates, attributable to enhanced uranium and thorium-series radionuclides associated with clay mineralogy and phosphate nodules. Conversely, sandy beds of the Deba-Fulani Member alongside cross-bedded sandstones and shales of Dumbulwa Member showed markedly lower values, consistent with geochemical depletion in quartz-dominated lithologies. Limestones and shales areas of the Kanawa Member and sandstones and mudstones of the Gulani Member displayed intermediate dose rates, with localized hotspots linked to secondary phosphate mineralization. The mean TGRD (~44 nGy/h) was about 25% below the UNSCEAR global average of 59 nGy/h. Activity concentrations of ²³⁸U, ²³²Th, and ⁴⁰K averaged 23.7, 30.5, and 241.1 Bq/kg, all below UNSCEAR world averages, with contributions following ⁴⁰K > ²³²Th > ²³⁸U. The annual effective dose remained below recommended limits for the public and radiation workers, indicating radiological safety. The mean excess lifetime cancer risk (0.188 × 10⁻³) was about 35% below the UNSCEAR world average. However, chronic internal exposure pathways, particularly dust inhalation and food-chain transfer, remain a study limitation. These findings provide a robust baseline and underscore the need for sustained radiological monitoring in farming areas and surrounding communities.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We report an infant referred for apnoeic episodes and a facial port-wine stain, prompting brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess for Sturge-Weber syndrome. MRI showed no leptomeningeal angiomatosis but revealed abnormal temporal lobe morphology with altered sulcation and bilateral hippocampal non-inversion, a pattern previously associated with fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3)-related skeletal dysplasia. This unexpected finding led to targeted genetic testing, which confirmed a de novo FGFR3 variant diagnostic of hypochondroplasia. Skeletal features were subtle in early infancy and became more obviously apparent later. This case highlights temporal lobe morphology as a diagnostic clue for FGFR3-related dysplasia on brain MRI performed for unrelated indications, potentially enabling earlier genetic diagnosis before clinical skeletal features emerge.</jats:p>

title: Difficult-to-Treat Rheumatoid Arthritis: Diagnostic Reassessment, Clinical Scenarios and Treatment Selection—A Narrative Review
abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA), defined by the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) in 2020/2021, requires treatment according to the recommendations, failure of at least two biological or targeted synthetic DMARDs (b/tsDMARDs), at least one feature of active, progressive or symptomatic disease, and the perception that management is problematic. Similar treatment histories may conceal different mechanisms: persistent inflammation, non-inflammatory pain, poor adherence, and comorbidity. This review examines diagnostic reassessment and treatment selection in D2T RA. Methods: A narrative review based on targeted searches of PubMed (2015–2026), Embase, and the Cochrane Library, prioritizing randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and EULAR recommendations. Results: The pooled prevalence of D2T RA is 11.7% (95% CI 9.5–14.3). Adherence to DMARDs is approximately 66%; non-adherence, comorbidity, and mimickers require exclusion before escalation. Persistent objective inflammation was reported in 47.1% of patients (95% CI 33.3–61.4). In Rituximab versus tocilizumab in anti-TNF inadequate responder patients with rheumatoid arthritis (R4RA), molecular stratification identified differential response to tocilizumab versus rituximab Clinical Disease Activity Index (CDAI) CDAI50: 63% vs. 36%; p = 0.035), whereas histological classification did not (56% vs. 45%; p = 0.31). Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors retain efficacy after bDMARD failure (SELECT-BEYOND: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) ACR20 65% vs. 28%; FINCH 2: 66% vs. 31%). Most trials enrolled broader populations, and their results do not establish a universal hierarchy of drug classes. Conclusions: Management should follow a structured reassessment sequence: verification of EULAR criteria, adherence review, exclusion of mimickers, parallel assessment of inflammatory and non-inflammatory mechanisms, individualized drug selection, glucocorticoid reassessment, and shared decision-making. Synovial pathotypes and molecular models remain investigational pending prospective evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Stock Market Reaction to the Announcement of the Change of Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia (An Event Study Analysis)
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCE HUMANITY & MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
abstract: <jats:p>The objective of this study is to measure the response of the capital market to the announcement of the change in the Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia by means of event study. Market response is calculated through abnormal return (AR), cumulative abnormal return (CAR), trading volume activity (TVA), and standard deviation (SD) of stocks of companies in the banking sector that are listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The event date for this study is set as September 8, 2025, where the change in the Minister of Finance was announced. The data observation period will employ an event window of 30 days before and 30 days after the event. The research sample will include banking stocks that were actively traded throughout the research period and that had all the required data. The secondary data used for the analysis will be the stock prices and trading volumes that are available from Indonesia Stock Exchange. The analytical procedures involve calculation of actual return, market return, abnormal return, average abnormal return, cumulative abnormal return, and trading volume activity. Testing of hypothesis is done by using One-Sample t-Test for AR and CAR and Paired-Sample t-Test for examining the difference in trading volume activity and standard deviation of stock prices before and after the event. It is shown from the results that there is a significant abnormal return and cumulative abnormal return at the announcement date, which implies that there is a capital market reaction to the event. Furthermore, the existence of significant difference in trading volume activity and stock standard deviation before and after the announcement indicates the change in trading activity and stock volatility of banks in the capital market. This research supports efficient market hypothesis and signaling theory, as information about the change of the Minister of Finance is useful information for investors.</jats:p>

Diagnostic Challenges and Management of Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria: A Case Report from Nepal
journal: World Journal of Medical Case Reports
abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This case report focuses on a 26-year-old man from Nepal who was diagnosed with paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria (PNH), an uncommon and potentially life-threatening haematological disorder. PNH is characterised by chronic intravascular haemolysis, bone marrow failure, and an increased risk of thrombosis, which can contribute to considerable clinical complications. The patient presented with several symptoms, including generalised weakness, jaundice, recurrent episodes of nosebleeds, dark-coloured urine, and pain in the large joints during the winter season. These symptoms had developed over time and reflected the varied clinical manifestations that can occur in patients with PNH. On clinical examination, the patient had scleral icterus and hepatomegaly, supporting the presence of an underlying haemolytic condition. Laboratory investigations demonstrated severe anaemia, leukopenia, an elevated lactate dehydrogenase level, and a significant PNH clone identified through flow cytometric analysis. Bone marrow examination also revealed findings that were consistent with the diagnosis of PNH. The combination of the patient’s clinical presentation, laboratory abnormalities, flow cytometry findings, and bone marrow results helped establish the final diagnosis. This report highlights the diagnostic difficulties associated with PNH because of its rarity and diverse clinical presentation, which may delay accurate recognition of the condition. It also reviews the available treatment approaches, including eculizumab and corticosteroids. Overall, the case emphasises the importance of maintaining clinical awareness and achieving a timely and accurate diagnosis to support the effective management of this rare and potentially fatal haematological disorder.</jats:p>

Prognostic and diagnostic value of gelsolin in sepsis: a meta-analysis and systematic review
abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, leading to substantial morbidity and mortality. Reliable biomarkers that support early diagnosis and risk stratification are still in great need. Gelsolin (GSN), an actin-binding protein involved in cytoskeletal remodeling, actin scavenging, and inflammatory regulation, has been proposed as a potential biomarker in sepsis, but the available clinical evidence has not been systematically summarized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library and clinical trial registries were searched from database inception to July 26, 2026. Original studies that measured circulating GSN levels in adult patients with sepsis and reported either survival outcomes or comparisons with a control group were eligible. The ratio of means (ROM) was used to compare GSN levels between non-survivors and survivors. For diagnostic analyses, sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, diagnostic odds ratios (ORs), and post-test probabilities were summarized when sufficient data were available.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. In seven studies reporting survival outcomes, GSN levels were significantly lower in non-survivors than in survivors (ROM = 0.62, 95% CI:0.53-0.73,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.00001), with high statistical heterogeneity (
                      <jats:italic>I</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                       = 74%). One study reported an admission plasma GSN threshold of 113.6 mg/L that showed prognostic discrimination for 28-day mortality; however, this single study derived threshold should be considered exploratory because it requires external validation and may not be generalizable given variations in assay methods and reported cut-off values across studies. Three studies were included in the exploratory diagnostic analysis. The pooled sensitivity was 0.81 (95% CI:0.71-0.89), whereas specificity was modest at 0.61 (95% CI:0.49-0.72) with substantial heterogeneity across studies (
                      <jats:italic>I</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                       = 90.6%), indicating considerable variability in false-positive classification. The positive likelihood ratio was 2.19 and the diagnostic OR was 6.38; however, these estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies, heterogeneous comparator groups, and variability in diagnostic settings.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Lower circulating GSN levels are associated with mortality in patients with sepsis and may have value for early prognostic risk stratification. However, because GSN is reduced in several inflammatory and tissue-injury conditions and because diagnostic specificity was modest with substantial heterogeneity, GSN should not be considered a stand-alone diagnostic biomarker for sepsis. Further larger multicenter prospective studies using standardized assays and clinically relevant comparator groups are needed to validate its prognostic and diagnostic utility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:title>Systematic review registration</jats:title>

                      , identifier CRD420261463914.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Exploring theatrical subtext translation
journal: Target. International Journal of Translation Studies Target / International Journal of Translation Studies Target
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Subtext remains a vital yet underexplored frontier in research on theatre translation. This study revisits debates
					on its universality — often constrained by Eurocentric evidence — through two canonical Chinese operas,
                    <jats:named-content content-type="foreign-phrase">西廂記</jats:named-content>
                    <jats:italic>Xixiang ji</jats:italic>
                    ‘The story of the western
					wing’ and
                    <jats:named-content content-type="foreign-phrase">牡丹亭</jats:named-content>
                    <jats:italic>Mudanting</jats:italic>
                    ‘The
					peony pavilion’, and two contemporary productions (
                    <jats:italic>The West Wing</jats:italic>
                    2008;
                    <jats:italic>The Peony Pavilion — The Youth
						Version</jats:italic>
                    2004). Integrating analysis of performance, libretti, and surtitles, it examines director-translators’
					motives and creative strategies through a practice-oriented transcreation framework, showing how subtext operates beyond
					Anglo-European realist norms. Focusing on pivotal moments, the research demonstrates how ‘the unspoken’ is re-encoded through
					intermodal dynamics, where vocal, gestural, and textual cues converge with music and symbolic staging. The findings underscore
					multimodal synergy as central to conveying subtext across cultural and linguistic divides. The study clarifies how implicit
					meanings function in classical Chinese theatre, advancing theatre translation scholarship.
                  </jats:p>

title: Lessons from the pore: how computational structural biology turned ion channel drug failures into design principles
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Although ion channels represent ∼19% of human protein drug targets, and are the molecular targets for ∼18% of approved small-molecule drugs, rational design remains highly challenging. These membrane proteins cycle through multiple conformations and share highly conserved binding pockets. We review a decade of computational advances in ion channel drug design, presenting four case studies spanning from post-failure examination to prospective designs. We begin with TRPV1, where dose-limiting hyperthermia halted clinical trials. New structural data are starting to explain the difference between hyperthermia-causing vs. non-causing ligands. Next, we discuss hERG, an off-target case where cryo-EM and simulations revealed the structural basis of its promiscuity. This enabled drug discovery campaigns to proactively design out of this cardiac liability. We then examine Na
                    <jats:sub>V</jats:sub>
                    1.8, where the recently approved suzetrigine proves that subtype selectivity is achievable despite high sequence conservation across sodium channels. Finally, for TRPM3, integrated cryo-EM, virtual screening, and medicinal chemistry yielded a picomolar antagonist, showcasing prospective drug design capability with computational structural biology. Together, these cases demonstrate how integration of cryo-EM, machine learning, and affinity calculations have transformed ion channel drug discovery. The field has evolved from using computational structural biology as a retrospective explanatory tool to a prospective design engine, accelerating design cycles.
                  </jats:p>

                    <sub>2</sub>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Platinum diselenide (PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ), a noble-metal transition metal dichalcogenide, has attracted increasing attention for next-generation electronics owing to its air stability, thickness-dependent electronic structure, and compatibility with low-temperature processing. However, achieving simultaneous control over crystallinity, thickness, and spatial patterning at back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible temperatures remains a major challenge. Here, we report a mask-free and site-selective strategy for the direct formation of patterned few-layer PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    films by combining focused-ion-beam (FIB) deposition of a Pt precursor with subsequent low-temperature selenization. The FIB process enables deterministic control of lateral geometry and thickness of the precursor, which is translated into thickness-controlled PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    after conversion. Compared with e-beam-deposited precursors, the FIB-derived Pt-rich films form more continuous networks prior to selenization, leading to PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    channels with more linear
                    <jats:italic>I</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>D</jats:sub>
                    –
                    <jats:italic>V</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>D</jats:sub>
                    behavior and improved electrical continuity. Structural characterization confirms the formation of layered PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    with polycrystalline stacking and thickness-dependent morphology. Raman spectroscopy reveals systematic evolution of the
                    <jats:italic>E</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>g</jats:sub>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>A</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>1g</jats:sub>
                    modes, consistent with enhanced interlayer coupling in thicker films. Importantly, we observe a strong substrate-dependent behavior in the low-temperature regime. At reduced temperature (200 °C), PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    formation is more pronounced on SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /Si substrates, consistent with more efficient nucleation and selenium incorporation on the amorphous oxide surface. At elevated temperature (350 °C), PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    grown on sapphire substrates exhibits sharper Raman features and improved structural ordering together with enhanced electrical characteristics. This behavior is consistent with a transition from nucleation‐limited growth at low temperature to crystallinity‐limited growth at higher temperature, governed by substrate‐dependent growth kinetics rather than a universally superior substrate. Field-effect transistors fabricated from the patterned films exhibit
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    -type transport behavior, demonstrating electrical continuity of the directly formed PtSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    channels. This work provides a BEOL-compatible pathway for spatially selective integration of two-dimensional (2D) materials and highlights the importance of substrate-dependent growth kinetics in low-temperature 2D material synthesis.
                  </jats:p>

title: Upgrading Low-Density Black Poplar Wood with Oak and Ash Facings: Bending Strength and a Laminated-Beam Design Framework
abstract: <jats:p>Black poplar (Populus nigra L.) is a fast-growing hardwood whose use in furniture and joinery is limited by its low density and strength. This study combined bending tests with a laminated-beam analysis to quantify and generalize the effect of symmetric oak (Quercus robur L.) and ash (Fraxinus excelsior L.) veneer facings on poplar cores. 45 specimens (15 per group) were tested in three-point bending. Facing increased the density from 432 kg/m3 to 504 kg/m3 (oak) and 494 kg/m3 (ash) and the bending strength (MOR, 12% moisture content) from 63.5 MPa to 86.8 MPa (+37%) and 77.1 MPa (+21%) (Welch’s ANOVA, p < 0.001). A dimensionless transformed-section framework was developed in which strength gain equals the product of stiffness amplification, determined by the face fraction and the face-to-core modulus ratio, and the face-to-core ratio of failure strains. Inverse analysis yielded in situ face strengths of 97 MPa (oak) and 91 MPa (ash) and failure-strain ratios of 1.06 and 0.81, which explains why the stiffer ash facings produced the smaller strength gain. The framework predicts face-governed failure, in agreement with the observations, and shear stresses below the shear strength of poplar. For components of fixed depth, the mass-specific strength is maximized at face fractions of 0.15–0.25, where faced poplar outperforms both unfaced poplar and solid oak or ash; the tested oak-faced elements were close to this optimum. Closed-form conditions and design charts generalize these results to other face–core combinations.</jats:p>

title: Mirror-assisted nearly 180° beam steering using three microstructured edge-emitting laser sub-arrays
journal: Journal of the Optical Society of America B
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Edge-emitting semiconductor lasers offer high efficiency and spectral purity but typically suffer from limited emission angles due to waveguide confinement and facet geometry, restricting their application in wide-angle solid-state optical systems. In this work, we demonstrate a microstructured edge-emitting laser architecture consisting of three sub-arrays, where periodic slot gratings provide intrinsic angular emission control and tilted reflective mirrors extend the accessible angular range through passive optical redirection. The first sub-array establishes the intrinsic emission range through slotted facet gratings that couple guided modes into free space via the grating-assisted phase-matching condition. The second and third sub-arrays employ tilted reflective mirrors to passively redirect the emitted beams and extend the accessible angular range through geometric optical reflection. Experimental and numerical analyses demonstrate a combined angular coverage envelope approaching 180° with well-defined far-field emission and preserved beam characteristics. Quantitative system-level analyses further verify the architecture, showing angular sector overlaps of 2.7° and 3.6°, discrete angular addressing with an approximately 4° increment, negligible thermal pointing drift (<0.2
                    <jats:sup>∘</jats:sup>
                    over 50 K), minimal optical path-length mismatch among the three branches, and an estimated mirror insertion loss of 0.5 dB. This compact monolithic–reflective approach provides a scalable platform for wide-angle semiconductor laser emission and integrated optical beam-control applications.
                  </jats:p>

title: Structural Insights into Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers after Long-Term Operation Using Advanced 3D Focused Ion Beam–Scanning Electron Microscopy Tomography
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are key to sustainable hydrogen production, but their long-term performance is limited by degradation, particularly in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which remains a barrier to commercial viability. Moreover, the need for corrosion-resistant materials and the intricate fabrication of bipolar plates and porous transport layers (PTLs) further impede large-scale deployment and account for a major share of the stack cost. Because lifetime and replacement costs are strongly influenced by the local microstructure and contact conditions, especially at the anode/PTL interface, a multiscale characterization approach combining 3D focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy (FIB–SEM) with time-of-flight mass spectrometry is used to investigate degradation in an MEA after several thousand hours of operation under industrially relevant conditions. The 3D reconstruction and ppm-level chemical mapping show that local contact heterogeneities at welds in an expanded-metal mesh PTL act as degradation hotspots. At these sites, intensified catalyst utilization accelerates iridium dissolution, driving iridium migration and deposition as extended filaments into the membrane. Concurrently, membrane voids are formed beneath these sites, accompanied by iron contamination detected at both contact types. In contrast, general contact regions mainly show a thin redeposition layer without voids or filaments. These findings provide a mechanistic framework that links local contact conditions and microstructural heterogeneities to coupled catalyst and membrane degradation, supporting design rules for improved PEMWE durability.</jats:p>

title: Numerical study of divergence half angle reduction with preserved ion-beam transmission in a converging-grid electrospray thruster

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Ionic-liquid electrospray thrusters are promising micropropulsion devices for small spacecraft; however, excessive ion-beam divergence reduces useful axial momentum and increases particle interception by downstream electrodes. This study investigates a compact converging-grid configuration designed to reduce the maximum beam-divergence half-angle while preserving high ion-transmission efficiency. Unlike architectures employing a dedicated focusing electrode or a separate focus grid, the proposed configuration uses the downstream biased accelerator extractor itself as an ion-optical field-shaping element. A three-dimensional bidirectionally coupled electrostatic–particle model was used to account for particle-induced space-charge effects. title: Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation of AISI 316L Stainless Steel Parts Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite (
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF.
                  </jats:p>

title:
Artificial Intelligence-Assisted
Ion-Association Design
Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
journal:
Journal of
the American
Chemical Society
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions. Here, we introduce an AI-assisted ion-association design strategy utilizing a binary electrolyte architecture to break through the linearity–dynamic range trade-off. GPR-assisted regression analysis maps complex electrolyte formulations to synaptic nonlinearity, identifying an optimized NaCl·Na-TFSI binary configuration. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest distinct intrinsic ion-association tendencies between Na+–Cl– and Na+–TFSI– pairs, consistent with the observed doping and relaxation behaviors: strongly associated Na+–Cl– pairs suppress abrupt doping to optimize linearity, reducing nonlinearity by up to ∼6-fold compared with single-anion controls, while weakly associated Na+–TFSI– pairs facilitate ion retention to expand the dynamic range (Gmax/Gmin ∼ 103). This balanced dual-anion transport enables linear, extensible, and high-dynamic-range multistate conductance modulation. Consequently, the optimized OESTs exhibit improved LTP/D linearity, reproducible cycling, and a 94.88% MNIST recognition accuracy. These results establish predictive binary ion-association design as a general framework for controlling synaptic weight modulation in organic neuromorphic devices.</jats:p>

title: Trust Adaptive Provenance Watermarking for Synthetic News Broadcasting
journal: Bridging of Emerging AI and Media Broadcasting (BEAM)
abstract: <jats:p>The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence in digital news broadcasting has increased the production of synthetic news content, raising critical concerns regarding authenticity, source verification, content manipulation, and audience trust. This study proposes a trust-adaptive provenance watermarking framework designed to dynamically protect and verify AI-generated news content by integrating provenance information with trust-aware watermarking mechanisms throughout the broadcasting workflow. The proposed framework combines adaptive digital watermarking, provenance metadata, and a trust-scoring mechanism that adjusts watermark strength according to content sensitivity, source credibility, and manipulation risk. Experimental evaluation is conducted using synthetic news samples under common content transformations, including compression, resizing, cropping, re-encoding, and partial manipulation, while performance is assessed through watermark detection accuracy, robustness, content quality, and provenance verification reliability. The experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high watermark detectability while maintaining acceptable perceptual quality across different broadcasting transformations. The adaptive trust mechanism further improves provenance verification for high-risk synthetic content and enables more reliable identification of manipulated or unauthorized news assets compared with conventional fixed-strength watermarking approaches. The proposed trust-adaptive provenance watermarking framework provides a practical approach for strengthening authenticity, traceability, and accountability in synthetic news broadcasting, offering a foundation for trustworthy AI-enabled media ecosystems while supporting broadcasters, audiences, and digital platforms in mitigating misinformation and unauthorized content manipulation.</jats:p>

title: In-situ hydrothermal synthesis of a bifunctional composite material multiwalled carbon nanotubes/cobalt phosphate for heavy-metal ion removal and supercapacitor electrode
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part L: Journal of Materials: Design and Applications
abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the drawbacks of existing bifunctional materials for adsorption-supercapacitor applications, including limited adsorption capacity and weak synergistic effect, a hydroxylated multi-walled carbon nanotubes/cobalt-phosphate (MWCNTs/CoTEDA-DAP) bifunctional composite was facilely fabricated via an in-situ hydrothermal strategy for aqueous Hg(II) (divalent mercury ion)/Pb(II) (divalent lead ion) removal and for use as supercapacitor electrodes. The adsorption behaviours towards Hg(II) and Pb(II), including kinetics, isotherms, thermodynamics and selectivity were systematically investigated. Box-Behnken response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimise adsorption parameters. Meanwhile, the electrochemical performance of MWCNTs/CoTEDA-DAP (hydroxylated multi-walled carbon nanotubes/cobalt-triethylenediamine-diammonium phosphate coordination phosphate) as supercapacitor electrode material was evaluated. The adsorption processes of Hg(II) and Pb(II) followed the Elovich and pseudo-second-order kinetic models, which demonstrates that chemisorption dominated the adsorption mechanism. The Langmuir isotherm model well described the monolayer adsorption behaviour. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG < 0, Gibbs free-energy change, ΔH > 0, enthalpy change, ΔS > 0, entropy change) verified that the adsorption was spontaneous, endothermic and entropy-increasing. Under the optimised RSM conditions, the maximum adsorption capacities attained 1345.24 mg/g for Hg(II) and 1521.83 mg/g for Pb(II). When deployed as a supercapacitor electrode, the composite achieved a specific capacitance of 181 F/g at 1 A/g. The synergistic effect originating from chelation of -OH, -NH- and phosphate groups as well as the conductive network of MWCNTs (hydroxylated multi-walled carbon nanotubes) contributes to the desirable bifunctional performance. This study provides a feasible strategy for designing integrated materials toward environmental remediation and energy-storage applications.</jats:p>

title: High-Current Accelerator-Driven Neutron Sources (HiCANSs): Current Projects and Perspectives in Europe
abstract: <jats:p>To provide neutrons for science and industry, various processes are applied, such as nuclear fission, spallation, fusion or low-energy nuclear reactions. With the availability of high-current proton accelerators, the latter process has gained growing interest in recent years. The prospect of access to versatile neutron sources with affordable cost and efficient and strong neutron flux has inspired many projects worldwide to establish high-current accelerator-driven neutron sources (HiCANSs). While compact accelerator-driven neutron sources (CANSs) using low-energy nuclear reactions have been used for decades, this novel class of sources, HiCANSs, would open new opportunities to access and exploit neutrons in science and industry. The most ambitious projects in this field have been developed in Europe, including the ARGITU project in Spain, the ICONE project in France and the HBS project in Germany. In the present paper, the basic physical and technological properties of HiCANSs will be outlined briefly, and the European HiCANS projects will be described. A short outlook on the future opportunities for HiCANSs in the landscape of the neutron facilities in Europe will be given.</jats:p>

title: A study on the 3D printing preparation method of reinforced casings for lithium-ion batteries in energy storage power stations using high specific energy absorption metamaterials
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part L: Journal of Materials: Design and Applications
abstract: <jats:p>Additive manufacturing has enabled the development of advanced lattice and metamaterial structures with tailored mechanical performance for energy absorption and lightweight structural applications. In this study, a novel round gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) metamaterial is designed, fabricated 3D printing, and systematically investigated under quasi-static compression loading. A combined experimental and finite element method (FEM) approach is employed to evaluate the mechanical response and validate the numerical model. The FEM results show excellent agreement with experiments, with only 1.3% deviation in stiffness and 5.8% difference in ultimate compressive load, confirming the high accuracy of the developed simulation framework in capturing the complex deformation behavior of the proposed architecture. The deformation analysis reveals a progressive and stable collapse mechanism governed by distributed plasticity and strain localization within the gyroid network. A comprehensive parametric study is then conducted to investigate the influence of structure thickness (T) and unit-cell height (H) on mechanical performance. The results demonstrate that T is the dominant parameter controlling load-bearing capacity and energy absorption, while H mainly influences deformation evolution with limited impact on global response. Importantly, the structure exhibits exceptionally high specific energy absorption (SEA), reaching up to 2586.5 mJ/g, significantly increasing with thickness and showing only minor variation (1–3%) with changes in H. This highlights the robustness and tunability of the proposed design for energy dissipation applications. Overall, the findings confirm that the proposed round gyroid TPMS metamaterial introduces a new geometry-driven strategy for achieving high-performance, lightweight, and highly efficient energy-absorbing structures.</jats:p>

title: Cation Chemistry and Ion Density Effects on Mono- and Divalent Ion Transport in Unentangled PEO Electrolytes
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding how cation valency, cation size, and ion density govern ionic transport in polymer electrolytes is essential for the development of next-generation multivalent batteries. While the transport mechanisms of monovalent ions in poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) are now well established, considerably less is known about divalent ion transport in the diffusion-controlled regime of unentangled polymer hosts. Here, we systematically investigate LiTFSI-, NaTFSI-, Mg(TFSI)2-, and Ca(TFSI)2-based electrolytes in low-molecular-weight, unentangled PEO (Mw = 0.35 kg mol–1), where ion transport is governed by polymer translational diffusion. Thermal characterization reveals that divalent cations suppress crystallinity more efficiently and induce substantially larger increases in the glass-transition temperature than their monovalent counterparts, consistent with stronger perturbation of the PEO dynamics by the divalent salts. Within each valency class, NaTFSI electrolytes exhibit higher total ionic conductivities than their LiTFSI counterparts, while Ca(TFSI)2-containing electrolytes exhibit higher ionic conductivities than the corresponding Mg(TFSI)2 systems at comparable cation-to-ethylene oxide ratios. These differences are consistent with the corresponding trends in glass-transition temperatures, suggesting that cation-dependent changes in polymer dynamics contribute to ion transport. Despite these stronger interactions, ionic conductivities exceeding 10–4 S/cm are achieved near room temperature at low ion densities, representing comparatively high total ionic conductivities among reported dry polymer electrolytes containing Mg(TFSI)2 and Ca(TFSI)2. For all electrolytes, the conductivity exhibits a characteristic nonmonotonic dependence on ion density arising from the competition between increasing ionic concentration and decreasing ionic mobility, with the conductivity maximum occurring at significantly lower ion densities for divalent salts. Finally, correlating ionic conductivity with zero-shear viscosity and introducing a charge-normalized conductivity based on the Nernst–Einstein framework collapses the transport behavior of all four electrolytes onto a common master trend. These results reveal a common macroscopic relationship between polymer friction and total ionic conductivity across mono- and divalent electrolytes and establish a unified framework for describing diffusion-controlled transport in oligomeric PEO.</jats:p>

A Reproducible Multi-Target Computational Framework for Prioritizing Plant-Derived Natural Products in Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: <jats:p>Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is biologically heterogeneous, and plant-derived natural products provide chemically diverse starting points for multi-target discovery. Reproducible prioritization is needed to distinguish literature-supported evidence from candidate-specific predictions not yet generated. Our objective was to develop a reproducible, evidence-informed framework for prioritizing plant-derived natural products in AD and define a transparent candidate library and prespecified screening set for subsequent computational and experimental evaluation. Completed work included selection of an AD target panel (AChE/BChE, BACE1, GSK-3β and MAO-B), synthesis of a published target-specific machine-learning (ML) benchmark, curation of a 20-compound candidate library with traceable chemical identities and literature support, and selection of a 13-compound prespecified screening set. Published performance metrics were treated solely as external benchmark evidence. Study-specific model training, prospective ML screening, molecular docking, BBB/drug-likeness and ADMET evaluation, multi-objective ranking, and experimental validation were prespecified as future work and were not performed. The framework links mechanistically justified targets, published ML benchmarks, a chemically diverse 20-compound library, and a 13-compound set for future screening. The library includes evidence-rich reference compounds and comparatively underexplored scaffolds; no candidate-specific computational ranking or selection outcome is reported. This study presents an evidence-informed, multi-target computational framework for prioritizing plant-derived natural products in Alzheimer’s disease. Its methodological contribution lies in integrating a mechanistically defined target panel, published machine-learning benchmarks, a traceable 20-compound candidate library, and a prespecified 13-compound screening set within a transparent prospective evaluation strategy. By distinguishing completed framework-development activities from future computational and experimental analyses, the study establishes a structured foundation for subsequent model validation, multi-objective prioritization, and experimental investigation.</jats:p>

title: Exploring combinations of spatial laser beam shaping for advancing nanoparticle synthesis by ablation in liquids
abstract: <jats:p>Pulsed laser ablation in liquids (PLAL) is a versatile and sustainable technique for the synthesis of ligand-free colloidal nanoparticles, but its wider application is limited by relatively low productivity and insufficient control over particle size distributions. Here, to advance the technique, we investigate the possibility of combining in one synthesis process the advantages of two recently developed cost-effective approaches, multibeam PLAL for productivity increase and donut-shaped laser beams for particle size modification. Nanoparticles of gold, an iron–nickel alloy, and a high-entropy alloy were produced in water using single-beam and multibeam configurations with four and eleven picosecond sub-beams. The effects of beam profile, beam-splitting factor, and laser fluence on particle yield and size distributions were systematically evaluated. Splitting donut-shaped beams is shown to offer a similar productivity increase as Gaussian pulses, and, at moderate fluences, multiple donut beams can be even more efficient. A single donut-shaped beam generally reduces the particle size, but, in a multibeam configuration, the reduction effect is hindered by secondary processes such as the interaction of cavitation bubbles, nanoparticle fragmentation, and redeposition. The results demonstrate the feasibility of combining donut-shaped beams with multibeam ablation in PLAL synthesis and identify key process parameters that have to be optimized to achieve both high productivity and improved particle size control.</jats:p>

title: Oxidized LDL pathophysiology and potential as a therapeutic target in atherosclerosis
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Uptake of oxidized and other forms of modified low-density lipoprotein (LDL) drives formation of foam cells, a hallmark of atherosclerotic plaques. Experimental studies demonstrating the proinflammatory and cytotoxic properties of oxidized LDL have led to the concept of LDL oxidation as one key factor in both development and destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques. Such data positioned oxidized LDL as a promising target for prevention or mitigation of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Yet the failure of multiple antioxidants to reduce cardiovascular risk in large randomized clinical trials has hampered this prospect. Such null studies have stimulated interest in an alternative approach: the therapeutic potential of antibodies against oxidized LDL. High levels of IgM against oxidized LDL phospholipids are associated with lower cardiovascular risk and these antibodies function primarily through neutralization and stimulation of clearance of modified LDL. IgG antibodies against aldehyde-modified peptide sequences in apolipoprotein B-100, the signature protein component of LDL, are also associated with lower risk of cardiovascular disease but experimental studies have shown that these antibodies function by locally forming immune complexes with oxidized LDL that limit the inflammatory activity of certain plaque macrophages. A phase 2 pilot study showed that one such antibody, orticumab, reduces an imaging index of local coronary arterial inflammation in patients with psoriasis. Thus, emerging evidence supports the possibility of using oxidized LDL antibodies to limit atherothrombotic disease.</jats:p>
