abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy (SMART) syndrome is a rare, delayed complication of cranial irradiation for central nervous system malignancies. It manifests with subacute, prolonged stroke-like episodes characterized by seizures, visual disturbances, focal neurologic deficits, and migraine-like headaches. Diagnosis remains challenging due to significant clinical and radiographic overlap with tumor recurrence, cerebral infarction, and post-ictal phenomena. Transient unilateral gyriform cortical enhancement confined to the prior radiation field is a hallmark MRI finding that, when promptly recognized, can prevent unnecessary interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To describe the clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and management of SMART syndrome through an illustrative case and to highlight key features that facilitate timely and accurate diagnosis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Case Report</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A patient in their early 70s with a history of right temporo-occipital oligodendroglioma status post chemoradiation decades prior, presented with new headaches and episodes of colorful flashing lights in their left visual field. Brain MRI demonstrated gyriform diffusion restriction and leptomeningeal enhancement in the right occipital cortex, confined to the prior radiation field. EEG revealed right hemispheric rhythmic delta activity without seizures. CTA Head showed multifocal narrowing along right distal M2 and M4 branches. SMART syndrome was favored instead of tumor recurrence. The patient was discharged on anti-seizure medication with close neuro-oncology follow-up. Repeat brain MRI 2 months later showed almost complete resolution of enhancement and diffusion restriction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Diagnosis of SMART syndrome is based on the revised Black et al. criteria; characteristic MRI findings include unilateral, reversible gyriform cortical enhancement and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity within the radiation port, with relative white matter sparing. Although historically considered reversible and self-limited, recent series report incomplete neurologic recovery in up to 45% of patients. Proposed mechanisms include radiation-induced neuronal hyperexcitability, cortical spreading depression, and impaired cerebrovascular autoregulation. Management is primarily supportive, with pulse corticosteroids and verapamil commonly used. SMART syndrome remains a diagnosis of exclusion and should be considered based on history to avoid unnecessary interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article examines two virtual reality musical instruments through a phenomenological lens drawn from German idealism and Heidegger: SIIIGNAL, a gesture-centered, physics-based performance system, and the 3-D Granulator, a field-centered, electroencephalogram-adaptive installation. In SIIIGNAL, sound arises through directed action, extending human intention into a manipulable sonic medium. In the 3-D Granulator, sound originates from the reciprocal relations among locomotion, neural variability, and spatial orientation, reframing musical interaction as a process of disclosure that displaces control. The analysis argues that these interaction modes function as complementary approaches that reconfigure the subject–object relation underpinning modern aesthetics, using technology as a medium through which presence becomes structurally audible. The resulting framework situates virtual reality sound design within a poietic paradigm in which gesture and field, action and attunement, converge to reveal new modes of musical meaning.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>With the development of space exploration technologies, space-grade CMOS image sensors require high-performance on-chip clock circuits with low jitter, low power consumption, small area, and excellent radiation robustness. This paper presents a radiation-hardened self-biased phase-locked loop (PLL) implemented in a 55 nm CMOS process and optimized for space-grade image sensors. By replacing the conventional dual charge pump with a current adder to separate the proportional and integral paths, and incorporating a voltage-to-current converter to eliminate the loop filter resistor, the proposed design reduces the number of nodes susceptible to single-event transient (SET) effects, lowers power consumption and area, and inherently enhances radiation tolerance. Additionally, localized radiation-hardening techniques are applied to sensitive nodes to further improve SET resilience. The proposed PLL operates over a frequency range of 0.5–2.8 GHz. At an output frequency of 1 GHz, it achieves a lock time of 2.11 μs, power consumption of 3.04 mW, phase noise of −93.84 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset, and RMS jitter of 7.12 ps, with a core area of 0.049 mm2. Under simulated heavy-ion irradiation with a linear energy transfer (LET) of 75 MeV·cm2/mg, the hardened PLL reduces output frequency deviation by 82.86% and recovery time by 37.63% compared to an unhardened design. These results demonstrate that the proposed PLL achieves significant radiation hardness without compromising performance, power consumption, or area.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) is a leading core technology in the fields of robotics and autonomous driving. Traditional VSLAM uses fixed frame rate image acquisition mode, which has a lot of redundant information, serious computational power consumption, motion blur, high power consumption and other problems. However, the integration between event camera and traditional camera can combine the advantages of both, providing a new idea to solve the bottleneck problem of traditional VSLAM. This paper not only explains the principle, advantages and disadvantages of traditional camera and event camera, but also discusses the typical VSLAM algorithm for fusing the two sensors in recent two years. In addition, this paper deeply analyzes the characteristics, performance and applicable scenarios of these VSLAM algorithms. The challenges and problems in this emerging field, such as sensor calibration, data fusion and algorithm development, are also discussed. Finally, the paper summarizes the potential applications and future directions of integrating event camera and traditional camera in the field of VSLAM.</jats:p>

Investigation on flow stability of flow field around an unmanned aerial vehicle
abstract: <jats:p>Rotor flow field stability is essential to the flight performance and aerodynamic characteristics of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). In this work, three-dimensional numerical simulations are carried out to investigate the flow stability characteristics of a small-scale UAV rotor. The Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes method coupled with the k–epsilon model is used to simulate the rotor flow field of UAV models, and the stability of the rotor flow field is analyzed by using the energy gradient theory. A calculation method for the energy gradient function K is derived for three-dimensional flows in this study. The spatial distribution of the dimensionless energy gradient function K can precisely identify the locations and concentrated zones of flow instability. For the UAV flow field, the energy gradient theory detected that there are two most unstable flow regions in the flow field, namely, the tip region and the wake region of the rotor. At the design flow rate or large flow rate, the high risk unstable region of the flow field only occurs at the tip of the rotor. As the flow rate decreases, high K unstable region appears in the wake. As such, both the rotor tip instability and the wake instability contribute to flow instability of rotor flow field at low flow rates. Therefore, targeted optimization of these two unstable regions in the design is vital for enhancing the operational reliability and aerodynamic efficiency of UAV rotors. This study provides a reliable technical reference for the aerodynamic design and performance optimization of miniature UAV rotors.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>We start with a brief introduction to the many faces of the Sun, the dynamic star that is the main source of space weather. We explain the need for spacecraft observations, the structure of the solar atmosphere, and the Sun’s magnetic cycle. Next, we focus on the Sun’s influence on Earth, define ‘space weather,’ and briefly discuss its effects on our technology and related socio-economic impacts. Then, we present data-driven, physics-based simulation models with predictive capabilities that enable forecasting and mitigation. We focus on models developed by my team at KU Leuven and the results and predictions they produce: the heliospheric wind and CME evolution models EUHFORIA and ICARUS, the global solar corona model COCONUT, and the solar energetic particle acceleration and transport model Particle Radiation Asset Directed at IP Space Exploration. abstract: <jats:p>Cross-efficiency-based Malmquist productivity measurement involves both the selection of DEA-optimal weights across Malmquist states and the aggregation of heterogeneous peer assessments. This study develops the Inertial Cross-Efficiency Malmquist Productivity Index (I-CEMPI). The method retains the state-specific primary-optimal weighting sets and coordinates the four Malmquist states through minimum intertemporal adjustment, yielding a unique and reproducible weight representation while preserving primary DEA optimality. Peer Cross-Malmquist assessments are subsequently combined through strategic-perspective-balanced geometric aggregation, which preserves the multiplicative decomposition into efficiency change and technical change. Applying I-CEMPI to 440 listed Chinese SRDI “Little Giant” enterprises over 2019–2024 shows substantial scope for intertemporal selection within the empirical optimal sets. Perspective balancing produces larger changes in aggregate productivity assessments than intertemporal coordination, while comparisons with the standard MPI and a published Cross-GMPI show high overall agreement together with differences in a subset of firm-level classifications. Innovation productivity contracts over most horizons, with technical change accounting for the larger share of cumulative contraction. Strategic perspectives differ more clearly in their efficiency-change and technical-change compositions than in persistent aggregate productivity rankings.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Automated classification of canine dermatological images is challenging because visually overlapping lesions, uncertain repository labels, and repeated or transformed source photographs can influence performance estimates. This study evaluated fixed ImageNet-pretrained DenseNet201, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0 features, alone and in fusion, with support vector machine (SVM), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and logistic regression classifiers for six repository-provided categories. Transformation-robust source auditing yielded 3088 images: 2862 development images from 864 source groups and a source-group-separated held-out internal test set of 226 images from 226 groups. Model selection used five-fold source-group-aware outer cross-validation with source-group-aware inner grid search. DenseNet201–EfficientNetB0 + SVM achieved the highest mean outer-fold balanced accuracy (0.9462 ± 0.0174), while triple fusion was comparable (0.9449 ± 0.0142) with a larger feature representation. On the held-out internal test set, accuracy was 0.8319 (95% CI 0.7832–0.8805), balanced accuracy was 0.7806 (0.7219–0.8384), and macro F1 was 0.7871 (0.7234–0.8432). Independent, clinically annotated external validation remains necessary to assess generalizability. These findings highlight the value of source-aware evaluation and parsimonious feature fusion when assessing multiclass canine dermatological image classification using repository-based datasets.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high latent heat and near‐isothermal heat storage and release, making them attractive for thermal energy storage and regulation. However, melt leakage, low thermal conductivity, and solid‐state rigidity hinder the simultaneous achievement of dimensional stability, flexibility, interfacial adaptability, and multifunctional responsiveness at high energy‐storage densities. Here, we develop ultraflexible paraffin‐based composite phase change materials (CPCMs) using a hybrid static–dynamic covalent three‐dimensional network and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) as rapid heat‐transfer pathways. Static covalent bonds maintain network integrity, while exchangeable boronic ester moieties enable thermally triggered rearrangement. Experiment and simulation results demonstrate the cross‐linked network suppresses large‐scale cooperative migration of paraffin while preserving the local degrees of freedom required for reversible phase transitions. The resulting CPCM delivers a phase‐change enthalpy of 172.2 J/g and an ultra‐high fracture elongation of 1219.5%. GNP incorporation increases thermal conductivity to 2.07 W/m·K while retaining an enthalpy efficiency over 98.8%, together with excellent adhesion, self‐healing, recyclability, and shape memory. The material further enables efficient thermal regulation in electronics, wide‐temperature‐range batteries, solar thermal storage, and flexible wearable thermal management. This strategy provides a novel design route toward integrating high energy storage, ultraflexibility, structural stability, and dynamic interfacial adaptability in one phase‐change material system.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Blast-wave propagation within interconnected compartments is strongly influenced by the characteristics of openings connecting adjacent spaces. While previous studies have investigated the effects of compartment geometry and opening configuration in the two-room problem, limited attention has been given to the influence of breakable media on blast-wave transmission and their representation in numerical simulations. This study presents a combined experimental and numerical investigation of blast-wave propagation in a two-compartment structure, focusing on the effects of receiving-compartment confinement, partition configuration, and a breakable medium located within the opening connecting the compartments. A series of small-scale blast experiments was conducted using a two-compartment model instrumented with pressure sensors. Several candidate materials were evaluated as representative breakable media, leading to the selection of a 75 g/m
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    paper sheet. High-speed Digital Image Correlation was employed to determine a failure criterion for numerical implementation. A computational fluid dynamics model, incorporating the breakable medium modelled as glazing based on a pressure-impulse curve, was subsequently developed in ProSAir and validated against the experimental measurements. The results demonstrate that confinement significantly increases blast loading within the receiving compartment. The introduction of a breakable medium resulted in delays in blast-wave arrival and reductions in the first pressure peak and the positive-phase impulse. The numerical model successfully validated the experimentally observed trends. The study improves the understanding of blast-wave transmission in interconnected compartments and presents a validated methodology for modelling blast-wave interaction with breakable media in numerical simulations.

abstract: <jats:p>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) strengthens the factuality of large language model outputs by grounding the generation process in retrieved external knowledge. Given that the efficacy of one-stage retrieval strictly defines the evidence available for generation, it is imperative to analyze the applicable boundaries of various retrieval methods under heterogeneous queries. This study compares BM25, a DPR-style dense retrieval baseline, and several fusion retrieval strategies. Queries are systematically categorized into terminology, semantic, and mixed types, utilizing the ‘enhanced mid’ dataset as the primary experimental corpus. Performance is evaluated using Top-1 Accuracy, Recall@3, and MRR@3. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Dynamic v2b method achieves the highest Top-1 Accuracy and MRR@3, at 82.50% and 0.8708, respectively. However, grid search analysis reveals that a fixed weight of 0.2 (BM25) + 0.8 (Dense) slightly outperforms it in Recall@3 and MRR@3, indicating that while the Dense-biased design of Dynamic v2b is effective, its dynamic weighting strategy requires further refinement. Finally, generation-side auxiliary scoring indicates that although retrieval improvements significantly enhance local sample quality, the overall impact on generation performance remains relatively limited.</jats:p>

title: When Does Spatial Modeling Help? A Controlled Study of Sparse Graph Fusion for Traffic Forecasting

affiliation.name: School of Computer Science and Technology, Shandong University

abstract: <jats:p>Spatial gains can arise from detector identity, additional capacity, or denser learned graphs. This exploratory development study tests when cross-node modeling improves multi-horizon traffic forecasting under degree-and capacity-controlled comparisons. Horizon-Conditioned Sparse Graph Fusion (HCSGF) combines a causal node-aware temporal encoder with degree-matched physical and sparse learned supports. Across the California Department of Transportation Performance Measurement System, District 03 (PEMS03), PEMS04, and PEMS08, five-seed aggregate Mean Absolute Error (MAE) reductions versus the lower-capacity temporal-only control are 1.60%, 0.81%, and 1.09%. Against the equal-capacity node-wise control, gains are 0.56%, 0.11%, and 0.46% and survive Holm correction only on PEMS08. Removing all spatial contributions increases 60-minute MAE by 12.61%, 16.33%, and 22.11%, indicating greater late-horizon reliance within the fitted models. Learned-only beats physical-only on PEMS03 and PEMS08 but not PEMS04. HCSGF does not beat the designated Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Embedding Transformer (STAEformer) comparator, while global routing beats horizon-conditioned routing on two datasets. Peak underestimation remains substantial, indicating that the present inputs do not capture rare traffic extremes or omitted external conditions reliably. The evidence therefore supports dataset-dependent rather than universal cross-node utility and requires confirmation on an untouched dataset or later time period.</jats:p>

title: Learner Confusion Detection from Facial Video: A Comparison of Deep Visual Models and Static– Dynamic Feature Fusion

affiliation.name: College of Computing and Data Science, Nanyang Technological University

abstract: <jats:p>Online learning systems have difficulty knowing whether learners truly understand the content. This research explores learner confusion detection based on facial expressions using video clips from the Dataset for Affective States in E-Environments (DAiSEE). A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a Residual Network (ResNet-18), and a Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) are compared as single-frame baseline models, and a static–dynamic feature fusion method is further proposed to combine single-frame appearance features with temporal facial blendshape statistics. Considering the severe imbalance between sample classes, model performance is evaluated using balanced accuracy, confused-class recall, confused-class F1-score, and Precision–Recall Area Under the Curve (PR-AUC) rather than accuracy alone. The static–dynamic fusion method achieves the highest balanced accuracy (0.606), confused recall (0.516), and confused F1-score (0.221) among all models, though with lower confused-class precision, indicating a trade-off between detecting more confused samples and producing more false positives. Overall detection performance remains limited, indicating that facial information alone may not be sufficient to fully capture learner confusion.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>High classification scores are meaningful only if the prediction target is physically consistent. We audited image-only, tabular-only and fusion experiments on 9000 ZooScan objects drawn from the 1,153,507-object PELGAS collection. The archived three-class labels were tertiles of the stored equivalent spherical diameter (ESD), not biomass classes. All 893,542 records exported with version v7.26 followed the documented ESD formula, whereas all 259,965 v7.24 records equalled twice the integer part of projected area divided by π. All 2017 v7.24 objects in the subset fell in the highest archived class. Recomputing ESD consistently from area and pixel calibration changed 3430 of the 9000 labels. The subset spans 13 cruises and 697 cruise–station groups and includes 2639 objects annotated as non-living. On the corrected target, tree-based controls using all descriptors reached a macro-F1 of about 0.998 under both object-stratified and station-grouped evaluation. In preliminary single-seed neural runs without area- or length-based descriptors, tabular networks reached a macro-F1 of 0.89, a Swin-T image model 0.946 and gated fusion 0.944; the image-based runs covered three folds and retained scale cues, so they do not isolate the contribution of each modality. Target provenance should be verified before multimodal performance rankings are used in ecological monitoring.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common malignant brain tumor of the central nervous system and is associated with a poor median survival of approximately 15 months. Current preclinical GBM models are limited by the lack of a physiologically relevant human microenvironment and the inability to reproducibly model tumor heterogeneity and cell–cell interactions. To address these limitations, we developed a scalable platform for generating uniform BO–VO–GBM fusion organoids using a 3D mold-based system. This approach enables controlled assembly of brain organoids (BOs), vascular organoids (VOs), and patient-derived GBM tissues with high reproducibility and structural consistency. Compared to conventional spontaneous fusion methods, our platform allows faster and more reliable formation of fusion organoids. The resulting assembloids exhibit stable integration between tumor, neural, and vascular components, supporting complex multicellular interactions within a defined microenvironment. Importantly, this system enables functional drug evaluation in a reproducible and physiologically relevant setting. Drug treatment groups, including bevacizumab, temozolomide (TMZ), and combination treatment (TMZ + bevacizumab), showed measurable reductions in tumor area compared with untreated controls, with the combination group exhibiting the greatest inhibitory effect on tumor growth. In addition, immunostaining analysis demonstrated decreased Ki-67 expression and increased cleaved caspase-3 (Cas-3) expression following drug treatment, indicating reduced proliferative activity and enhanced apoptotic responses in GBM regions. Overall, our 3D mold-based fusion organoid platform provides a robust and reproducible method for modeling GBM in a human-relevant context and offers a promising tool for therapeutic evaluation and precision medicine.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>We develop a kinetic model of electron–ion inverse bremsstrahlung absorption in magnetized fusion plasmas that extends the conventional constant-Coulomb-logarithm treatment. The model incorporates the velocity dependence of the Coulomb logarithm and plasma screening directly into the electron–ion collision frequency, while a super-Gaussian electron distribution is used to account for non-Maxwellian distortions. The formulation explicitly retains magnetization and circular-polarization effects and yields asymptotic scaling laws for magneto-inertial fusion (MIF) plasmas and microwave-heated magnetically confined plasmas. The results show that the velocity-dependent Coulomb logarithm can either reduce or enhance absorption depending on the electron distribution, whereas plasma screening systematically suppresses it. Under the conditions studied, the complete collisional model changes the MIF absorption rate by about 19% relative to the thermal-logarithm approximation. In the microwave-heated regime, the corresponding reduction is about 6% over the whole density range considered. These results highlight the need to treat non-Maxwellianity, velocity-dependent collisions, and plasma screening self-consistently when modeling inverse bremsstrahlung absorption in magnetized fusion plasmas.</jats:p>

title: A Hybrid Fuzzy MCDM and Dempster Shafer Evidence Fusion Framework for Assessing MOOC Learning Impact in Engineering Education
abstract:
<jats:p>The educational evaluation of Massive Open Online
Courses (MOOCs) is a multi-dimensional learning
process with interrelated, different criterion and
uncertainty in learners’ responses. This study proposes
a hybrid fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making and
evidence-fusion framework for assessment of MOOC
learning impact in engineering education. The
framework was applied to 1725 third- and fourth-year
students of computer science and engineering from 15
Universities in Uttarakhand, India. We created a
hierarchical assessment framework with 13 learning
dimensions and 63 indicators to capture conceptual,
technical, problem-solving, academic, independentlearning and career-related outcomes. Criterion
weights were estimated independently from the Best
Worst Method, Analytic Hierarchy Process and Fuzzy
Analytic Hierarchy Process and then combined to
obtain robust parameters and indicator weights.
Dempster-Shafer theory was applied to combine the
weighted student-response evidence under three
impact states: Low, Medium and High. The results
indicate that Problem Solving Ability is the most
influential dimension, with an integrated weight of
0.155, followed by Coding Competency (0.130),
Algorithmic Thinking (0.105), Programming
Knowledge (0.095) and Debugging and Testing Skills
(0.085). These five technical dimensions accounted for
57% of the total parameter weight. The evidence-fusion
results classified eight universities as high MOOC
learning impact, four as medium and three as low. Our
proposed framework offers an uncertainty-aware and
hierarchical technique for integrating fuzzy expert
judgments and multidimensional learner evidence.
It can support the comparative evaluation of
technology-enabled learning and can be adapted to
other engineering and higher education decision
environments.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>This study tests whether Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KAN) outperform the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) as a cross-modal fusion head. Sixteen configurations (BERT/DistilBERT text encoders, ViT/DeiT image encoders, concatenation or gated fusion, and MLP or KAN heads) were compared on MASAD (38,066 binary-labeled text-image pairs) and MVSA-Multiple (17,027 three-class pairs) under identical splits and protocols (ten seeds for the confirmatory BERT+ViT pair, five for the others). The primary metrics were domain-averaged F1 (MASAD) and weighted F1 (MVSA-Multiple). On MASAD, all configurations fell within a 95.3–96.0% weighted F1 band. Among the sixteen configurations, the best mean, 96.01 ± 0.19%, came from BERT+DeiT (concat)+MLP, and the best KAN configuration reached 95.74 ± 0.12%. For the confirmatory BERT+ViT pair, the head effect (KAN − MLP) in domain-averaged F1 was +0.19 points under concatenation (90% CI [−0.11; +0.49]) and −0.08 under gated fusion ([−0.36; +0.21]), within the pre-specified ±0.5-point equivalence margin; no other encoder pair showed a consistent head advantage. On MVSA-Multiple, no head was consistently superior, and wide intervals precluded an equivalence conclusion; a class-macro-F1 gain for gated KAN in the BERT+ViT pair (+1.77 points, 90% CI [0.00; +3.53]) was not reproduced for the other encoder pairs and remains exploratory. The findings do not support the assumption that KAN automatically improves multimodal fusion.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PLAG1 is a recognized proto-oncogene that has been implicated in multiple tumor types. PLAG family-altered CNS tumors – including PLAG1-fusion neuroepithelial tumors and embryonal tumors with PLAGL1/PLAGL2 amplifications – have recently emerged as novel but distinct entities, primarily in pediatric patients. We report a supratentorial neuroepithelial tumor with CHD7::PLAG1 fusion and concurrent TERT promoter mutation in an adult patient. Histologically, this tumor exhibited ependymal features – highlighting the utility of widespread methylation profiling for diagnostic confirmation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Retrospective chart and literature review of CNS tumors with PLAG family alterations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 52-year-old woman presented with acute dizziness and ataxia. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed acute cerebellar infarct and an incidental 1.4 cm heterogeneously enhancing intraventricular mass in the left lateral ventricle. Follow-up imaging revealed 2-3 mm growth over 6 months, prompting gross total surgical resection. Histopathology demonstrated monomorphic cells with minimal pleomorphism, round-oval nuclei, perivascular pseudorosettes, and inconspicuous mitoses, favoring supratentorial ependymoma, not otherwise specified (NOS). Immunohistochemistry showed GFAP positivity, scattered dot-like positivity for EMA, IDH-1 wildtype, and focal Ki-67 up to 8%. DNA methylation profiling revealed likely pathogenic CHD7:: PLAG1 fusion, leading to an integrated diagnosis of neuroepithelial tumor with CHD7::PLAG1 fusion, not elsewhere classified (NEC). Next generation sequencing (NGS) also detected a pathogenic TERT promoter mutation (c-124C&gt;T). CSF cell-free DNA testing was negative. Spine MRI revealed a 3mm intradural extramedullary enhancing T4 nodule of unclear significance. She remains clinically well on surveillance imaging.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PLAG1-rearranged CNS tumors are rare but distinct entities emerging in the era of molecular profiling and are not recognized in the 2021 WHO CNS Classification. To our knowledge, this is the first reported neuroepithelial tumor with CHD7::PLAG1 fusion and TERT promoter mutation – alterations in likely independent oncogenic pathways. Larger studies reconciling molecular findings, morphology, and clinical outcomes are necessary to inform prognosis and management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Intraparenchymal central nervous system (CNS) schwannomas with VGLL-family gene fusions are a recently characterized rare tumor entity. These benign neoplasms are distinct from classic peripheral nerve sheath tumors and may radiologically mimic gliomas or metastases. To date, no progression or recurrence has been documented in the molecularly defined VGLL-fused subgroup. We present a case highlighting the critical role of molecular analysis in diagnosis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 47-year-old female presented with one week of worsening headache and bilateral blurred vision. Neurological examination revealed a left partial hemianopia. Brain CT and MRI were obtained, followed by surgical resection. Histopathological evaluation and molecular profiling, including RNA sequencing, DNA methylation analysis, and copy number studies, were performed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>MRI demonstrated a 5 cm right parietal cystic lesion with a 1.9 cm irregularly enhancing nodule causing mass effect and 4 mm midline shift. Papilledema was present at diagnosis and improved postoperatively. Imaging showed a substantial non-enhancing cystic component without a well-defined capsule; therefore, gross total resection of the enhancing nodule was performed. Histopathology revealed a spindle cell neoplasm. Molecular analysis identified a canonical CHD7::VGLL3 fusion, confirming a VGLL-altered intraparenchymal schwannoma. Additional low-level somatic DOT1L mutations and a heterozygous CHEK2 mutation were detected. Postoperatively, the patient experienced marked improvement in headache and visual symptoms, without recurrence on follow-up imaging.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case underscores the importance of advanced molecular diagnostics in atypical intraparenchymal CNS tumors. The nonspecific clinical and radiological presentation could easily have resulted in misdiagnosis. Although not formally recognized in the WHO CNS tumor classification, accumulating evidence supports VGLL-fused schwannoma as a distinct benign tumor entity for which surgical resection appears curative. Reporting additional cases is essential to improve diagnostic accuracy and support future classification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract: <jats:p>Surface electromyography (sEMG) supports personalized movement recognition, but feature utility must be interpreted together with preprocessing conditions. We evaluated a task-specific integration of a smooth fast Fourier transform (FFT) subband bank, nearest-neighbor entropy (NNE), time-domain (TD) descriptors, and participant-specific extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Nine-channel recordings from 40 Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology Lower Limb Motion Dataset (SIAT-LLMD) participants were evaluated for 16-class recognition using repetition-grouped five-fold cross-validation. Under complete-record amplitude normalization, the 216-dimensional fusion achieved 95.63% accuracy and 94.54% macro-F1, exceeding TD-XGB by 1.043 percentage points; random and repeated-feature expansion did not reproduce this gain. With the classifier configurations held fixed, macro-F1 was 94.85% with record-specific references fitted to all eligible samples, 95.58% with record-specific training-only references, and 75.31% with shared participant-level training references. The record-specific controls require movement-associated recording identity and do not establish prospective unknown-action performance. This gain was accompanied by median single-thread CPU computation of 34.210 ms per conditioned window for Fusion-XGB, compared with 5.392 ms for TD-XGB (approximately sixfold). Across the evaluated amplitude-reference conditions, Fusion-XGB retained a macro-F1 improvement over TD-XGB, while absolute recognition performance varied with the reference definition.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Non-cooperative signal recognition is essential for spectrum awareness and interference management in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications, where unknown emitters, jamming threats, and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) make modulation classification and parameter estimation particularly challenging. Existing approaches often treat modulation classification, parameter estimation, and semantic reasoning as isolated tasks, making it difficult to exploit the complementarity of cross-domain information. This paper proposes PeirceTriadicNet (PTN), a Peircean triadic-relation network for this problem. The Representamen branch processes observable signal representations (IQ waveforms, time–frequency maps, and power spectral densities), the Object branch embeds physical source parameters (modulation type, symbol rate, carrier-frequency offset, roll-off, bandwidth, and SNR), and the Interpretant branch incorporates modulation-family and SNR priors for semantic reasoning. The final model, PTN-ResIcon, fuses the three branch embeddings with fixed equal weights (αR=αO=αI=1/3). On RML-S-Full-Std, a UAV-oriented synthetic dataset that re-generates the RML2016.10a modulation set under representative UAV link conditions (Rician fading, Doppler shift, and barrage, partial-band, follower, and deceptive jamming), with 220,000 IQ frames of 11 modulation formats over −20 to +18 dB, per-frame physical-parameter and semantic annotations, and a released open-data generation script—the covered PSK/QAM OFDM video downlinks and FSK/CPM frequency-hopping control links mirror the signal families observed in real commercial drone RF links—PTN-ResIcon achieves an overall modulation-recognition accuracy of 80.67%, which is 17.6 percentage points higher than the Representamen branch alone and 24.0, 20.1, and 20.2 percentage points higher than CNN2, CNN-LSTM, and ResNet1D, respectively; the +18 dB accuracy is 91.50%. On the real DroneRFa corpus (USRP-acquired recordings of four DJI devices at three flight distances), the complete triadic configuration reaches 72.50% device-identification accuracy, demonstrating that the framework transfers from synthetic to genuine UAV signals. An SNR-biased learnable-attention variant, PTN-ResIcon-Learned, dynamically adjusts the triadic weights from the oracle SNR and branch confidences; it reaches 76.86%, showing that fixed equal-weight triadic fusion itself provides the main gain and that overly aggressive SNR gating slightly degrades generalization. In the UAV-swarm scenario of RML-S-Full-Std, PTN-ResIcon maintains an accuracy of 81.44%, demonstrating its applicability to UAV communication environments and to spectrum-awareness tasks in emergency-response missions.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Recent advances in rapid molecular diagnosis for central nervous system (CNS) tumors, including detection of IDH mutations, have enabled the development of intraoperative genotyping. In addition to single nucleotide variants, gene fusion abnormalities are also recognized as important molecular markers in CNS tumors. Fusion genes are valuable not only for diagnosis but also as potential therapeutic targets, highlighting the importance of rapid identification. In this study, we developed a rapid detection method for the KIAA1549::BRAF fusion, which is observed in approximately 66% of pilocytic astrocytomas (PAs).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Using RNA extracted from tumor specimens, we established a rapid analysis system with the GeneSoC high-speed real-time PCR platform, which enables reverse transcription and 50 cycles of real-time PCR to be completed on a single microfluidic plate within approximately 20 minutes. RNA was extracted from frozen tumor samples obtained from 26 patients with PA who underwent surgical resection at our institution between 2019 and 2025. With conventional PCR using complementary DNA (cDNA) synthesized by reverse transcription with fusion-specific primers targeting K16–B9, K15–B9, and K16–B11, we identified fusion abnormalities in 13 cases (50%). Using the same tissue specimens, reverse transcription followed by real-time PCR with GeneSoC successfully detected fusion genes in all positive cases within an average of 32 minutes, including the time needed for RNA extraction.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study demonstrated that the GeneSoC high-speed real-time PCR system can rapidly identify the KIAA1549::BRAF fusion from small tumor specimens. This system may serve as a useful platform for integrated intraoperative molecular diagnosis of PA.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>In spinal correction surgery, metallic rods are commonly bent intraoperatively by surgeons to conform to the patient-specific spinal curvature and are then fixed with pedicle screws. However, intraoperative rod contouring can introduce surface scratches and notches, which may reduce fatigue strength and act as initiation sites for fracture. In this study, spinal correction rods with a prescribed spinal contour were fabricated from a Co–28Cr–6Mo–0.11N alloy (hereafter referred to as the CCMN alloy) by electron beam powder bed fusion (PBF-EB) to reduce dependence on intraoperative bending. Their compressive response, cyclic compression behavior, and fracture characteristics were experimentally evaluated, and their deformation behavior was further examined by finite element analysis (FEA). The CCMN rods were subjected to one, two, or three cycles of combined aging and reverse transformation heat treatment, denoted RT, 2RT, and 3RT, respectively. Under a compressive load of 1000 N, the displacement decreased with an increasing number of reverse transformation cycles, and the 3RT specimen showed the highest apparent resistance to deformation. The loads required to produce a displacement of 5 mm were 812, 843, 865, and 896 N for the as-built, RT, 2RT, and 3RT rods, respectively; thus, the 3RT rod exhibited an increase of 84 N relative to the as-built rod. Although all specimens were fabricated using the same CAD geometry and adjusted to the same nominal dimensional profile, small specimen-specific geometric deviations could not be independently quantified. Therefore, the observed differences in load–displacement response cannot be attributed exclusively to heat-treatment-induced microstructural changes. Furthermore, increasing the maximum diameter of the middle region of the variable-diameter rod from 7 to 8 mm reduced the displacement under 1000 N from 3.3 to 2.7 mm. In a single-specimen cyclic compression screening test at 0–300 N, 1 Hz, and 1 × 106 cycles, no apparent macroscopic residual deformation or fracture was observed. This result represents runout under the specified loading condition and does not establish a fatigue limit. These results support the feasibility of using PBF-EB to fabricate CCMN rods with prescribed curved and variable-diameter geometries and demonstrate a stable mechanical response under the specific static and cyclic loading conditions examined in this study.</jats:p>

title: Coaxial Monitoring of Meltpool for Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Control
journal: Strojniški vestnik - Journal of Mechanical Engineering
abstract: <jats:p>Reliable process monitoring is critical for advancing laser powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M), as it provides the process information required for corrective control actions to prevent defects such as lack-of-fusion and keyhole porosity. A promising approach for PBF-LB/M process monitoring is coaxial measurement of light emitted from the meltpool area. More than two hundred research studies on coaxial monitoring of the meltpool have been performed, but there is still no validated and reliable method for measuring a suitable variable that could be directly used as an input for high-resolution control of the PBF-LB/M process, enabling process parameters such as laser power and scan speed to be dynamically adjusted not only at the part level, but locally for individual micrometer-scale segments along the scan track. This work reviews existing research studies on coaxial meltpool monitoring and identifies potential future research and development directions toward a standard and reliable meltpool monitoring method. Meltpool depth is identified as a particularly promising control-relevant variable. With the ability to monitor and control meltpool depth, it is possible to avoid undesirable process conditions due to too high or too low energy input, which would result in defects like keyhole porosity or lack-of-fusion. However, only five studies have attempted to estimate the melt pool depth coaxially during the PBF-LB/M process. Despite these attempts, there is no sufficiently validated method for high-resolution coaxial monitoring of meltpool depth in PBF-LB/M. The potential solution seems to be in combining concepts and recent discoveries from two-color coaxial camera- and photodiode-based meltpool area monitoring approaches. Based on the existing literature and hands-on experiences with establishing and working with coaxial monitoring systems, this work also provides guidelines and lists the most common challenges for implementing coaxial monitoring of the meltpool in the PBF-LB/M process.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is associated with poor clinical outcomes. Interictal scalp EEG-based DRE identification faces a methodological limitation: segment-level models often capture individual-specific EEG patterns rather than group-level pathological differences. In this retrospective study of 42 patients (21 DRE, 21 non-DRE), we constructed an EEG-based DRE recognition framework. Multi-domain features (temporal, spectral, nonlinear) were extracted, and a mutual validation strategy integrating patient-level statistical tests and machine learning was applied to verify the pathological discriminative validity of features. A multi-domain support vector machine was built with ReliefF feature selection, evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation and hold-out validation, and further analyzed for interpretability and clinical correlations. Significant between-group differences were found in clinical and electrophysiological features, with prominent alterations in prefrontal temporal statistics, θ/β band power and entropy features. The multi-domain model consistently outperformed single-domain models; prefrontal β/γ power and entropy features were identified as core candidate biomarkers, significantly correlated with disease duration and seizure frequency. This study identifies prefrontal EEG features as candidate DRE biomarkers, and the combined validation framework supports the pathological basis of classification performance. Nevertheless, the single-dataset retrospective design and limited benchmark comparisons restrict conclusion generalizability. Further multicenter external validation is warranted to assess the framework's generalization capacity and clinical translational potential.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nonreciprocal interactions, in which action–reaction symmetry is broken, provide a powerful route to collective dynamics that cannot be captured by equilibrium free-energy minimisation. Here, we introduce and analyse a two-species nonreciprocal McKean–Vlasov equation (MVE) derived from an underlying system of interacting stochastic particles. Combining linear stability analysis, weakly nonlinear arguments, pseudo-spectral simulations, and Langevin particle dynamics, we show that the structure of nonreciprocity controls the onset and nature of collective order. For spatially uniform weak nonreciprocity, asymmetry shifts the critical diffusion threshold but produces only stationary instabilities, indicating that uniform imbalance alone is insufficient to generate sustained time-dependent motion. In contrast, spatially modulated nonreciprocity fundamentally enriches the dynamics: depending on its symmetry and coupling to the interaction potential, the homogeneous state can lose stability through Hopf bifurcations, giving rise to standing and travelling wave states. We identify two distinct mechanisms for this: breaking of pairwise action–reaction symmetry by the even part of the modulation, and, for an odd modulation entering at the level of the force, a pair force that remains reciprocal but is no longer conservative on the torus, driving the two species into counter-propagating drift. We identify both subcritical and supercritical Hopf transitions, relate the selected patterns to Landau saturation coefficients, and show that travelling waves can emerge even in the weak-nonreciprocity regime without explicit microscopic run-and-chase rules. Direct Langevin simulations confirm that these oscillatory and travelling states persist at the particle level and are not artefacts of the continuum mean-field description. Our results establish nonreciprocal MVEs as a minimal framework for understanding how spatially structured asymmetric interactions generate self-organised motion, dynamical phase transitions, and nonequilibrium collective order.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Brain metastases (BM) are the most common intracranial malignancy in adults and remain associated with poor morbididty and mortality despite advances in multimodal therapy. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a minimally invasive approach to assess disease biology, but its relationship to clinical, radiographic, and survival outcomes in BM remains poorly characterized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We retrospectively analyzed perioperative plasma cfDNA concentration in 108 consecutive patients who underwent surgical resection of BM from breast cancer, lung cancer, or melanoma between 2010 and 2019. cfDNA was extracted from peripheral plasma and quantified by fluorometric assay. Patients were dichotomized at cfDNA &gt;21 ng/mL, corresponding to the upper tertile.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma cfDNA was elevated in patients with uncontrolled systemic disease (p = 0.013) and leptomeningeal disease (p = 0.002), but was not associated with intracranial tumor volume, lesion number, edema volume, or proximity to CSF or venous structures. High cfDNA was associated with worse OS across the full cohort (p = 0.044), but not PFS or cumulative incidence of intracranial progression. This OS association was most pronounced in melanoma BM (p &lt; 0.001), with no significant association in breast or lung BM. On univariate Cox regression, cfDNA concentration was associated with worse OS (HR 1.01/ng/mL, 95% CI 1.00–1.01, p = 0.048), along with uncontrolled systemic disease, high BM volume, lower KPS, partial resection, and prior hormonal/immunotherapy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Perioperative plasma cfDNA concentration tracks systemic disease burden rather than intracranial tumor load and carries prognostic significance for overall survival in patients with BM. The histology-dependent nature of this association, particularly in melanoma, warrants validation in larger, molecularly annotated cohorts. These findings highlight the need for more sensitive, CNS-directed liquid biopsy strategies to capture intracranial disease burden.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cold atmospheric plasma is applied to dental implants for surface activation, osseointegration, infection control and host modulation. This review reads those four uses as one reactive‐species mechanism with a separate exposure axis per target (an organizing interpretation, not a measured law) and audits what an illustrative sample of thirty‐three protocols reports about dose. Plasma medicine has a source‐characterization specification (DIN SPEC 91315) and candidate dose descriptors, delivered energy and equivalent total oxidation potential, whose inputs no audited protocol reports in full. Of twenty‐five atmospheric‐pressure protocols, working gas is stated in twenty‐four, flow in nineteen, power or voltage setting in eleven; across all thirty‐three, treated area and delivered dose in none, a measured output in two. Human endpoints are mostly surrogates.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We start with a brief introduction to the many faces of the Sun, the dynamic star that is the main source of space weather. We explain the need for spacecraft observations, the structure of the solar atmosphere, and the Sun’s magnetic cycle. Next, we focus on the Sun’s influence on Earth, define ‘space weather,’ and briefly discuss its effects on our technology and related socio-economic impacts. Then, we present data-driven, physics-based simulation models with predictive capabilities that enable forecasting and mitigation. We focus on models developed by my team at KU Leuven and the results and predictions they produce: the heliospheric wind and CME evolution models EUHFORIA and ICARUS, the global solar corona model COCONUT, and the solar energetic particle acceleration and transport model Particle Radiation Asset Directed at IP Space Exploration. We end with a few take-home messages.</jats:p>

title: Maternal plasma cell-free RNAs and sonographic parameters for predicting spontaneous preterm birth in twin pregnancies: A prospective cohort study
abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: To evaluate whether cervical length (CL), uterocervical angle (UCA), and five maternal plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNAs) markers can predict spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) before 37 and 34 weeks in twin pregnancies.
Methods: This prospective study included 80 twin pregnancies examined at 14 - 24 weeks’ gestation at Hai Phong Medical University Hospital, from February 2023 to February 2025. CL and UCA were measured by transvaginal ultrasonography, and plasma cfRNA concentrations of PSME2, NAMPT, APOA1, APOA4, and Hsa-let-7g were quantified using droplet digital PCR. Participants were followed until delivery. Associations with sPTB were assessed using multivariable binary logistic regression, and predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
Results: Women who delivered preterm had a significantly larger UCA and shorter CL than those delivering at term. Among the five RNA markers, only Hsa-let-7g differed significantly between women with sPTB before 34 weeks and those delivering at or after 34 weeks (1.89 ± 0.51 vs. 1.03 ± 0.54, p = 0.024). After adjusting, UCA was independently associated with sPTB before 37 weeks (OR 1.042, 95% CI 1.005 - 1.081) and before 34 weeks (OR 1.056, 95% CI 1.004 - 1.111). Hsa-let-7g was associated with sPTB before 34 weeks (OR 3.391, 95% CI 1.089 - 10.556). Area under the curve for predicting sPTB before 34 weeks was 0.799 for UCA, 0.712 for Hsa-let-7g, and 0.829 for their combination.
Conclusion: Second-trimester UCA and plasma Hsa-let-7g showed potential as non-invasive markers for predicting sPTB in twin pregnancies. Their combined use may improve the prediction of sPTB before 34 weeks.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma liquid biopsy offers a minimally invasive strategy for glioblastoma (GBM) monitoring, but assay sensitivity remains limited. We evaluated a matched tumor-plasma whole exome sequencing (WES) approach to longitudinally detect somatic variants in plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) during chemoradiotherapy (CRT).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma cfDNA was collected from 8 patients with GBM at baseline, intra-CRT, and after CRT (NCT05480644). Tumor tissue and plasma WES were performed by Caris Life Sciences. Variants were called and filtered using the Genome Analysis Toolkit. Timepoint-matched genomic DNA (gDNA; from buffy coat) served as matched normal for serial cfDNA analyses; baseline gDNA served as the matched normal for tumor analyses. Coding variants were defined as protein-altering/splice-site variants, including missense, truncating, frameshift, in-frame indel, start/stop codon, and splice-site alterations. dbSNP-annotated variants were removed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Median patient age was 58 years (interquartile range [IQR] 36-66); 62% were male. All patients received conventionally fractionated radiotherapy (59.4Gy/33fx) with concurrent temozolomide. Tumor and plasma WES generated 9,213 and 16,032 variant calls, respectively. Variants absent from matched normal gDNA (cfDNA-only) were detectable with median VAF of 6.4% (range 0.104-95.9%) and 9.1% (range 0.316-68.4%) in tumor and plasma samples, respectively. Across patients, 128 unique cfDNA-only variants were present in matched tumor and plasma, including 21 coding variants. Tumor-concordant cfDNA-only variant counts were highest at baseline and decreased during/after RT. This decrease was significant by paired Wilcoxon testing (p &lt; 0.02) and was not associated with differences in median variant read depth. A subset of tumor-concordant variants (n = 21) persisted across serial plasma timepoints.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This exploratory pilot study demonstrates longitudinal tumor-informed plasma WES is feasible during CRT for GBM and may identify dynamic tumor-concordant cfDNA variants. Plasma variants were not dominated by canonical GBM driver alterations, suggesting that longitudinal, tumor-informed plasma cfDNA WES may capture broader low-frequency molecular patterns beyond isolated detection of established tumor-defining events.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Background: Aging is a complex and irreversible process influenced by a combination of factors, including genetic background, environment, and various diseases. Aging-related processes are reflected at the transcriptomic level. Expression profiling of peripheral blood, the only tissue connected to all organs and thus capable of reflecting processes occurring throughout the body, is of particular interest. Methods: In this study, we conducted a whole-transcriptome analysis of peripheral blood from male rhesus macaques in two age groups: 5.83 ± 1.06 and 28.4 ± 1.7 years. Enrichment analysis was performed using Cytoscape v.3.10.4. Results: RNA-seq analysis identified 741 differentially expressed genes (DEGs): 377 upregulated and 364 downregulated in old macaques compared to young individuals. The enrichment analysis identified 22 metabolic processes distributed across 10 groups. Conclusions: Bioinformatic analysis of DEGs revealed a complex picture of processes associated with genome stability (chromatin remodeling and organization, histone modification), gene expression (RNA splicing, translation), transport, oxidative stress, and platelet aggregation during aging. The identified key genes represent promising potential markers of aging. This list includes both upregulated DEGs (NDUFS7, PPIA, FERMT3, and RPS14) and downregulated DEGs (CHD6, CHD7, NDE1, CHAF1A, CHD2, EIF2S2, UPF3B, SMARCA4, and LOC706480 (NAP1L1)). The known functions of these genes, as well as their disease associations, strongly support the hypothesis that peripheral blood reflects processes occurring throughout the body, including the brain.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Brain metastases (BMs) remain a critical challenge in oncology with limited tools for real-time molecular monitoring. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has transformed treatment monitoring in extracranial cancers, but whether cfDNA can reliably detect and track intracranial disease remains unclear. We performed serial cfDNA sequencing in a cohort of patients with BMs of diverse histologies treated with pembrolizumab on a phase 2 trial (Brastianos et al., Nat Med 2023). Ultra-low-pass whole genome sequencing (ULP-WGS) was performed on serial plasma samples and CSF (where available) with tumor fraction (TF) estimated by ichorCNA (limit of detection ∼3%). Targeted sequencing was performed on matched tissue (BM, primaries, extracranial metastases) and plasma to assess tissue-plasma mutation concordance. Advanced quantitative MRI including DCE permeability (ktrans) and DSC perfusion was obtained at serial timepoints. 238 serial plasma ULP-WGS samples were collected from 57 patients (median 4 per patient). Among 36 patients with pre-treatment samples, 20 had baseline plasma TF below the limit of detection. Detectable baseline TF trended toward shorter overall survival (5.2 vs 8.3 months, p = 0.06). In 17 patients with matched tissue and plasma targeted sequencing, overall tissue-to-plasma mutation concordance was 65% but varied dramatically by patient (11-100%). Concordance strongly correlated with baseline plasma TF (rho=0.87, p = 0.005) and was similar across tissue compartments (BM 62%, extracranial metastasis 66%, primary 55%). MRI-derived BBB permeability (ktrans) did not correlate with plasma TF (rho=-0.02, p = 0.96; n = 18), indicating shedding constraints extend beyond vascular permeability. All CSF samples analyzed (n = 4) had readily detectable TF (range 4.4-45.7%). Plasma cfDNA has limited sensitivity for detecting and monitoring BM, with most patients below reliable detection thresholds. This limitation is not explained by BBB vascular permeability alone, suggesting alternative biological mechanisms restrict tumor DNA shedding from intracranial disease. CSF-based and ultra-sensitive sequencing approaches warrant investigation for molecular monitoring in this population.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Plasma membrane integrity is essential for cellular survival, yet how cells repair micron-scale plasma membrane ruptures remains poorly understood. Here, using the genetically tractable Caenorhabditis elegans epidermis, we combine live imaging, genetics, super-resolution microscopy, and biophysical approaches to define a size-dependent role for endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT)-III in large-scale membrane repair. Small wounds induce transient, focal VPS-32 accumulation, whereas large wounds trigger the formation of a persistent but dynamic, circumferential ESCRT-III assembly that remains associated with the wound during repair. Formation of this assembly requires conserved ESCRT regulators, including ALX-1, TSG-101, and VPS-4, together with VPS-32 polymerization. The wound-associated ESCRT-III assembly is required for membrane tension restoration and efficient membrane repair, while disrupting VPS-32 polymerization impairs tension recovery, reduces vesicle recruitment and wound closure, and consequently compromises axon regeneration and organismal survival following injury. Together, our findings suggest that large plasma membrane wounds induce a persistent, dynamic ESCRT-III assembly that restores membrane tension and facilitates vesicle-mediated membrane addition to promote wound repair.</jats:p>

Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Power Distribution Network Reconfiguration using Hybrid Particle Swarm and Genetic Algorithm
journal: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
abstract: <jats:p>Power distribution networks are a critical component of the electric power distribution system. Hence, numerous research has focus on distribution network reconfiguration systems, intending to minimize power losses and interruptions, namely, Customer Average Interruption Index (CAIDI), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), Energy Not Supplied (ENS), and Voltage Profile (VP) improvement, either by Genetic Algorithm (GA) or Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Nonetheless, existing research has not simultaneously employed a hybrid of GA and PSO optimization methods to ascertain which optimization method is better in terms of improving the reliability indices, such as CAIDI, SAIFI, and ENS, while minimizing power losses and improving the VP, thus leaving a gap in the literature. Hence, the proposed research work seeks to utilize the synergy of GA and PSO optimization techniques on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems with the aforementioned reliability targets to unearth which of the optimization techniques is better than the other. Meanwhile, the obtained results indicate that the GA exhibits a higher voltage level enhancement of 2.75% with a corresponding SAIFI reduction of 33%. Nonetheless, the PSO unveils superior or enhanced power loss reduction of 61.75%, ENS reduction of 48%, and CAIDI reduction of 30% with a corresponding computational speed of 0.24 seconds. Hence, based on the aforementioned analysis of the results, it can be concluded that the selection of the optimization algorithm depends on the network's specific operational requirements, as no single algorithm performs optimally across all parameter measurements. Besides, while the PSO performs excellently in terms of loss, ENS, and CAIDI reduction, the GA performs well in terms of voltage enhancement and SAIDI reduction.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Presentation of antigen from necrotic cancer cells within tumour microenvironments to T cells requires efficient uptake by DCs. However, intact necrotic tumour cells present physical barriers to direct endocytosis. Here, we investigate the non-canonical role of the serine protease plasmin and its regulatory network in tumour cell endocytosis by human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (mDCs) and downstream T cell stimulation. Pre-treating heat-killed melanoma cells with plasmin significantly enhanced their endocytosis by mDCs, an effect reversed by the physiological inhibitor α2-antiplasmin. Live-cell imaging and flow cytometry demonstrated that mDCs predominantly internalise micron-scale cellular debris rather than whole cells, and that plasmin activity “digests” dead-cell particles, thereby enabling uptake of particles of optimal diameter (∼1-3 μm). Enhanced endocytosis directly translated to increased CD4+ T cell activation. Furthermore, both heat-killed melanoma cells and mDCs functioned as lysine-dependent plasminogen-binding surfaces capable of generating localised proteolytic activity. Plasmin treatment modestly reduced DC cell-surface PD-L1 expression and altered specific inflammatory cytokines. These findings reframe plasmin as a modulator of immune-tumour interactions and highlight important methodological considerations regarding serum-derived proteases in experimental immunology.</jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Urethral stricture is a common and debilitating urological condition in which fibrosis narrows the urethral lumen. Recurrence after surgical repair is frequent, and no antifibrotic pharmacotherapy has been established. Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) show antifibrotic activity in several organ systems, but whether they act in urethral fibrosis, and by what mechanism, had not been examined.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We isolated and characterized hUC-MSC-EVs and tested them in primary human urethral fibroblasts (UFBs) stimulated with TGF-β1 and in a rat model of trauma-induced urethral stricture. Small RNA sequencing was used to profile the EV miRNA cargo, and the role of let-7i-5p was examined by gain- and loss-of-function experiments, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and let-7i-5p-depleted EVs (KD EVs), both
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      .
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      hUC-MSC-EVs dose-dependently suppressed TGF-β1-induced UFB proliferation, migration and myofibroblast differentiation and lowered α-SMA and Collagen I expression, with reduced Smad2/3 phosphorylation. Periurethral injection in rats significantly reduced urethral wall hyperechogenicity, luminal narrowing, submucosal collagen deposition and profibrotic protein expression at the 4-week postoperative endpoint. Small RNA sequencing placed let-7i-5p among the most abundant miRNAs packaged in hUC-MSC-EVs, and this miRNA was efficiently transferred to recipient UFBs. let-7i-5p bound the 3′-UTR of TGFBR1 and suppressed TGFBR1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels. Depleting let-7i-5p from EVs with an inhibitor largely abolished their antifibrotic activity
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      , linking EV-delivered let-7i-5p to suppression of the TGFBR1/Smad2/3 signaling axis.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results identify hUC-MSC-EVs as an injectable, cell-free antifibrotic candidate for urethral stricture and let-7i-5p as a cargo on which their activity depends.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Reforestation efforts are often constrained by low seed survival under harsh environmental conditions due to seed displacement from suitable microsites. Myxospermous seeds produce mucilage that promotes post‐dispersal attachment and water retention, thereby enhancing seed establishment. Here, we investigated the biological factors governing mechanical attachment across four myxospermous species,
                    <jats:italic>Ocimum basilicum</jats:italic>
                    (basil),
                    <jats:italic>Salvia hispanica</jats:italic>
                    (chia),
                    <jats:italic>Plantago ovata</jats:italic>
                    (psyllium), and
                    <jats:italic>Linum usitatissimum</jats:italic>
                    (flax), which occupy diverse ecological environments. We used light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy, enzymatic treatments, physical characterization methods, and functional attachment assays to investigate the mechanisms underlying mucilage‐mediated seed attachment on heterogeneous surfaces. We found variation among mucilage‐mediated seed attachments under applied hydrostatic pressure. Enzymatic treatments revealed that pectin removal causes a marked loss of adhesion across all species. However, psyllium mucilage, which possesses hemicellulosic networks, showed stronger attachment than pectin‐rich flax mucilage on rough and porous substrates. Notably, mucilage could be transplanted to non‐myxospermous seeds, conferring functional attachment capabilities. Together, our results show that species‐specific mucilage properties generate distinct modes of attachment across diverse substrates, driven by differences in polysaccharide composition and fibrillar architecture. These findings link mucilage molecular structure to seed resilience and reveal an adaptive mechanism enabling seeds to persist in heterogeneous environments.
                  </jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Excess fat mass is causally linked to multiple diseases, but the use of existing therapies, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, is limited by varying effects and common side effects, including loss of fat-free mass. We aimed to identify proteins associated with fat mass, but ideally not also associated with fat-free mass, as potential drug targets for alternative therapeutic strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We used UK Biobank data on plasma levels of 3K proteins (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 35K) and fat and fat-free mass (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 368K). We applied a machine learning procedure to select proteins for downstream
                      <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>
                      Mendelian randomisation analyses, which estimated associations of genetically predicted protein levels with fat mass. These were followed by colocalisation analyses to assess shared causal genetic variants and further
                      <jats:italic>cis</jats:italic>
                      Mendelian randomisation analyses to assess associations with fat-free mass.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Here we present evidence on the associations of genetically predicted levels of 21 proteins with fat mass, including five which also colocalise with the trait (AGER, CRIM1, DNER, NEFL, and PRRT3). Seven of the 21 proteins have no clear association with fat-free mass, and ADM has an association with fat-free mass opposite in direction to its association with fat mass, suggesting that modulating these proteins may be less likely to also lower fat-free mass. Two proteins, AGER and ADM, have been investigated in advanced-stage clinical trials for indications unrelated to adiposity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings support prioritising several proteins for further research as potential drug targets for fat mass reduction. They highlight proteins that may help diversify therapy options beyond glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and suggest possible repurposing opportunities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
